[p. 350] (Surah al-Tawbah)

Its central theme is opposing those who turned away from what the preceding surah (al-Anfal) called them to: following the one who summons to Allah in His Oneness and following what pleases Him, and it calls for allegiance to those who turned toward Him. The clearest evidence in it for this aim is the story of those who stayed behind. Having admitted that they had lagged behind the one who summons, without an excuse, in the expedition of Tabuk, which admits of a remote interpretation in their favour, may Allah be pleased with them, they were shunned and turned away from in every respect, even in speech. This is the meaning of its name al-Tawbah (Repentance). It also indicates disavowal (al-bara'ah), because disavowal of them through their shunning, even in returning a greeting, was the cause of their repentance. So this is the naming of the effect by its cause (ism al-musabbab 'ala al-sabab, a figure of speech). Its name Bara'ah (Disavowal) is also clear in terms of its aim as mentioned. Likewise al-Fadihah (The Exposer), because whoever is exposed is fit to be disavowed. Also al-Buhuth (The Searching), because one only searches into the state of one who is hated. Al-Mu'thirah (The Stirring Up), al-Munaffirah (The Repelling), al-Muthirah (The Scattering), al-Hafirah (The Digging Up), al-Mukhziyah (The Disgracing), al-Muhlikah (The Destroying), al-Mushharridah (The Dispersing), al-Mudamdimah (The Annihilating) and al-Munakkilah (The Punishing) are all names with similar meanings, because only the condition of an enemy is searched out in this way, and so on afterwards. Al-Mushharridah (The Dispersing) is also greatly appropriate in this regard, in light of what al-Anfal alluded to in the verse: ﴿So scatter those behind them﴾ [al-Anfal 8:57]. The name Surat al-'Adhab (The Surah of Punishment) is also clear in its aim. Likewise al-Muqashqishah, because they said its meaning is:

[p. 351] the one that clears from hypocrisy, from taqashqashat qurahu, when a wound peels as it heals. Its justification is that whoever knows that Allah, His Messenger and the believers are disavowed from him for a matter is worthy of turning back from that matter. In my view, it is also a doubled form of qashsh, whose meaning is gathering, because it gathered together the types of hypocrites and their conditions. In this sense is also the statement about Abu Jahm ibn Hudhayfah, concerning one who wished to marry a woman: "I fear for you his qashqashah," meaning his pursuing of the taste of affairs, taken from al-qashsh, which is seeking food from here and there, or from his staff, which is the extreme of that. The root qashsh, its inversion shaqq, and their doubled forms qashqasha and shaqshaqa all revolve around gathering, and separation necessarily accompanies it. For what gathers is only what has been scattered, and what is scattered is only what has been gathered. These two examples divide the two meanings between them, except for a little. Thus qashsha al-qawm means the people became healthy and were revived after weakness by gathering flesh. Al-rajul (the man) qashsha means he ate from here and there and gathered whatever he could from the food on the table, which is clear in this respect. Aqshaw and inqashshu mean they set off, scattered and passed away fleeing. Inqashshu means they passed and went away swiftly, because they gathered together in that and collected whatever goods they could. Al-qashsh and al-iqshash mean seeking food from here and there to gather it. Al-qishshah (with kasra) is a monkey, as if because it gathers what it sees to eat into its mouth. Al-sabiyyah al-saghirah al-juththah (a small-bodied girl) who can hardly stand firm is like one gathered into herself. Likewise al-qashish is a small boy, and a small crawling creature like a beetle, either because it gathers in itself or because it gathers filth. Al-qashish (on the pattern of amir) is the gleaning, because gleaners gather it. The sound of a snake's skin rubbing against itself is also so named, because it occurs only when it coils and gathers. Qashsha min al-judari means he recovered from smallpox, like taqashqasha. It may be from separation, since he parted from it, or from gathering, since recovery gathered all of him and removed it. The hamza may be for removal. Taqashshashat al-qurah and taqashqashat mean the wounds peeled as they healed, either from gathering, because the powers gather for health, or from separation and cessation. Likewise taqashqasha al-ba'ir means the camel was cured of mange. It is said qashshashahum bi-kalamihi means he spoke foul words and harmed them, that is, by gathering their concerns upon hatred of him or their faults. Likewise qashsha al-shay' means he gathered it with his hand until it fell away, that is, he peeled all of it, so it is suitable for both separation and gathering. Qashsha means he walked like one emaciated, that is, he was agitated, and this necessitates hurrying and bending, so it suits both gathering and separation. Qashsha also means he ate what people throw on refuse heaps or ate the crumbs of charity, because that is the extreme of gathering. Qashsha al-nabat means it dried up, so it deserved to be gathered. Al-qashsh is poor dates, like al-daqal and the like, because it is itself gathered. Al-dalw [p. 353] is a huge bucket because of how much it gathers. In the hadith: "Say: O you who disbelieve, and say: He is Allah, One, the two al-Muqashqishan," that is, the two that clear from polytheism, because of what is in the hadith: "Recite: Say: O you who disbelieve, when you sleep, for it is a disavowal of polytheism." The meaning is that they gather every polytheism and subtle or great hypocrisy and thus remove it. Al-qashqashah imitates a sound before the roar, in the pure shaqshaqah before it thunders with the roar, because the beginnings of the roaring sound are of extreme bulk, so it is gathering, and so is what it imitates. Al-qashqashah is also a staff, because it gathers what is intended by it, or because its bark is peeled off as the skin of a snake is peeled. As for the inverted form, it is said of it: shaqqahu, meaning he split it, that is, separated it. Al-Khalil said: a crack may be in one of the two sides without penetrating, whereas a shaqq (split) is only penetrating. Shaqqa nab al-ba'ir means the camel's tooth came through, because it parted the flesh.

Shaqqa al-'asa means he split the staff in two, and he separated the community. Shaqqa 'alayhi al-amr means the matter was hard, so it separated him from himself. Shaqqa 'alayhi means he put him in hardship. Shaqqa basar al-muhtadir means the dying person looked at a thing and his glance did not return from it, because it is aimed in one direction and turned away from the other directions. Al-shaqq is the singular of al-shuqqah, cracks. Al-subh (dawn) is so named because it separates the army of darkness. Jawbat ma bayn al-shafratayn (the opening between the two lips) is the female's genital. Al-tafriq (separation) is from this, including shaqq 'asa al-muslimin (splitting the staff of the Muslims). Istitalat al-barq ila wasat al-sama' (the lightning stretching to the middle of the sky) without veering right or left is so named because it splits the clouds straight, as it splits the board and the staff. Al-shiqq (with kasra) is a side, because it is separated from the other side, and it is a name for what you look at because it is on one side. It is also a kind of jinn, because it is a group of them, and it means half of anything. It may be vocalised with fatha. Al-mal bayni wa baynaka shiqq al-sha'rah (the wealth between me and you is a hair's split), which may be vocalised with fatha, means two equal halves. Al-shiqqah (with kasra) is a splinter of a board, or of a staff, or of a cloth or other thing that has been split lengthwise. Al-shaqiyyah is a type of intercourse, as if it were on one side. Al-shuqqah (with damma or kasra) means distance and direction that the traveller aims for, and a far journey. All of these are clear in the sense of separation. Also al-mashaqqah (hardship), because it takes one side of the self. The far horse is the one whose legs are far apart and which is tall, as if its parts were separated so that it became long. This is the opposite of what came before about the small girl. Al-ashaqq also means a calf when it has become strong, as if, having reached maturity, it has split the earth by ploughing. Everything split into halves is mushshaqq. Al-shaqiqah (like safinah) is the gap between two mountains that produces grass, because it separated the two mountains and its grass separated the joined parts of its land. Al-matar (rain), the heavy and wide downpour, is so named because the cloud is split by it. Also lightning spreading from the horizon, because it splits the cloud. Also a pain that takes half the head and face. Shaqa'iq al-Nu'man (anemones) is well known. They were named for their redness, as a comparison with shaqiqat al-barq (the splitting of lightning), so they say. In my view they were named for the separation of their petals and their clapping together, so they are like split things while gathered. Al-shuqaq (like ghurab) is a cracking that affects the ankles of animals. Al-shiqshiqah (with kasra) is a thing like the lung that a camel brings out of its mouth when it is agitated, as if it splits its throat so that it comes out, and it causes its roar, which splits the closure of its cavity to make a sound. From this: shaqshaqa al-fahl means the stallion roared, and al-'usfur means the sparrow chirped. Shaqqaqa al-kalam means he brought out speech in the best manner. Shaqqaqa al-hatab means he split each piece into two or more. Inshaqqat al-'asa means the matter was divided. Al-ishtiqaq (derivation) is taking the side of a thing, and taking in speech or in dispute to the right and left while abandoning the intended direction, because it splits the directions of meanings. It is also taking one word from another word, as if it separated its parts. This is my brother, shiqq nafsi (half of my self), and shaqiqi (my full brother), as if he splits his lineage from his lineage, or as if he is a half of him.

This surah is the last surah to be revealed. al-Bukhari in the book of Tafsir, and others, related in his Sahih from al-Bara' (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "The last verse revealed was: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning al-kalalah﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:176], and the last surah revealed was Bara'ah."

Since the connection of its beginning, which calls to disavowal of those whose breaking of the covenant is feared, to the end of al-Anfal, which explains who is fit for guardianship and which concludes with the comprehensiveness of knowledge at a great level of clarity, together with what preceded about the connection of the end of al-A'raf to the beginning of al-Anfal, al-Anfal was placed before Bara'ah despite its brevity, and Bara'ah despite its length and the confusion of its status among the Companions as to whether it is an independent surah or part of a surah. Likewise Al 'Imran was placed before al-Nisa' despite its brevity, for the same kind of connection. So what is mentioned in Bara'ah about disavowal and turning away is an explanation of the end of al-Anfal. Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad, Abu Dawud in al-Sunan, al-Tirmidhi in al-Jami' and graded it hasan, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Abu Ya'la, al-Bazzar, al-Bayhaqi, and the imam Abu Muhammad Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Bustī, the judge, in his Tafsir, by the chain of al-Tirmidhi and al-Bayhaqi, and the imam Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas without a chain, related from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) who said: "I said to 'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may Allah be pleased with him): What led you to combine al-Anfal, which is of the mathani (oft-repeated surahs, meaning those between the mi'in and the mufassal), and Bara'ah, which is of the mi'in (surahs of about a hundred verses), and join them together without writing between them the line 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,' and place them among the seven long surahs? What led you to do that?" 'Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sometimes receive surahs with many verses, and when something was revealed to him he would call some of those who wrote for him and say: 'Place these verses in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned.' al-Anfal was among the first things revealed at Madinah, and Bara'ah was among the last of the Qur'an to be revealed. Its story was similar to its story, so I thought it was part of it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away without explaining to us that it was part of it." al-Nahhas said: "I forgot to ask him about it. For this reason I combined them and did not write between them the line 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,' and placed them among the seven long surahs." Ibn Rahawayh added: "And they were called al-Qarinatayn (the Two Companions)."

End of quotation.

So he explained that the two had become confused for him, and that he placed them among the long surahs because of their connection to them, on the assumption that they were one surah. In al-Qamus he said: "al-Sab' al-Tiwal (the Seven Long Surahs), on the pattern of Surad, are from al-Baqarah to al-A'raf. The seventh is Surat Yunus, or al-Anfal and Bara'ah together, because they are one surah." End of quotation.

In al-Kashshaf he said: "It is also said: Surat al-Anfal and al-Tawbah are one surah. Both were revealed about fighting, and they are counted as the seventh of the long surahs, and what follows them is al-Mi'un. This view is evident, because together they total two hundred and six verses, so they stand in the place of one of the long surahs. The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) differed. Some said al-Anfal and Bara'ah are one surah, and some said they are two surahs. A gap was left between them for the view that they are two surahs, and the basmalah was omitted for the view that they are one surah." End of quotation.

And on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: "They only imagined that because al-Anfal mentions covenants and Bara'ah mentions the abrogation of covenants, and one was placed beside the other." By al-mathani here is meant what is below the mi'in and above the mufassal. Abu 'Ubayd al-Harawi said: "It was called mathani because the mi'in were made beginnings, and those that follow them are mathani." End of quotation.

The better view regarding that, in relation to al-Mufassal (the last section of the Qur'an, from Surah al-Hujurat onward), is on two grounds. The first: al-Mufassal is the first general designation for the short surahs, and above it come al-Mathani (the surahs of medium length, about a hundred verses or a little less), then al-Mi'un (the surahs of about a hundred verses), then at-Tiwal (the long surahs). So al-Mathani is, in reality, the second after al-Mufassal, and it is only that al-Mi'un follow it when we begin the count from the long surahs at the other end. The second: when these surahs exceeded al-Mufassal, the division of a surah among them into two rak'ahs of the prayer became like reciting two surahs of al-Mufassal, so they were called al-Mathani (the repeated ones), because they are repeated within the whole of the prayer by reciting part of them in each of the two rak'ahs. Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas said: Abu Ishaq said: one of our companions related to me, from our companion Muhammad ibn Yazid, that he said: "The basmalah (*Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*) was not written at the beginning of Surah Bara'ah, because the basmalah is an opening of goodness, while the beginning of Bara'ah is a threat and the breaking of covenants. Therefore it was not written at its beginning." And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "I asked 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: Why was 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim' not written here?" He said: "Because 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim' is a security (amān)." End.

On this view al-Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Shatibi also relied in his poem, where he said:

*"Whether you join it, or begin Bara'ah, its descent is with the sword, and you are not one who recites the basmalah."*

And he said in al-Kashshaf: Ibn 'Uyaynah was asked and said: "The name of Allah is peace and security, so it is not written in [a context of] repudiation and war. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not say to one who gives you greeting of peace, "You are not a believer"﴾ [al-Nisa: 94]."

It was said: "But the Prophet (ﷺ) wrote to the people of war: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.'" He said: "That was only at the start, inviting them, and he had not repudiated them. Do you not see that he says: 'Peace upon those who follow guidance'? So whoever is invited to Allah and responds, and is invited to the jizyah and responds, has followed guidance. As for repudiation, it is only disavowal and cursing." End.

The report of Ibn 'Abbas from 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with them both, does not contradict this. Rather it is similar to the fact that it was revealed without the basmalah, for the meaning mentioned. Its situation was unclear to the Companions, may Allah's good pleasure be upon them, and no question was asked about it until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away. So their agreement with the surahs in naming it by a name specific to it is evidence that it is a surah in its own right, while their differing from them in not sending down the basmalah at its beginning, together with the possibility that it was left out for the meaning mentioned or for another reason, is evidence that it is part of a surah. Abu Dawud and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) did not know the division of a surah." In another narration: "He did not know the end of a surah until there was revealed to him: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.'" The Hafiz Abu Shamah said: "This is a good (hasan) hadith." Al-Hakim also has in al-Mustadrak from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Muslims did not know the end of a surah until 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful' was revealed. When it was revealed they knew that the surah had ended. When its situation became unclear, they left off writing the basmalah at its beginning, and separated it from al-Anfal a little." And Allah is the Granter of success.

This has already been explained in brief, the similarity of the two stories, at the beginning of al-Anfal and in the midst of al-A'raf. As for the detail: in each of them there is the repudiation of a covenant with whoever is feared to break it; that the Sacred Mosque is not fit for its custody except by the God-fearing; that the polytheists are impure and have no fitness for approaching it; that the few of the party of Allah do not harm them if they hold fast to the five pillars of victory, and that their many do not benefit them if their steadfastness is compromised by doubt; the urging to jihad in more than one place; and the guarantee of sufficiency, as He indicated in al-Anfal with His words: ﴿For them are degrees with their Lord, and forgiveness and a generous provision﴾ [al-Anfal: 4]. And it mentions the rulings of the charities (sadaqat), which belong to the category of spoils, and enumerates the categories of each; and the command to spend, indicated in al-Anfal and elsewhere by His words: ﴿And those who disbelieve, some of them are allies of others﴾ [al-Anfal: 73], meaning by mutual support in spending and otherwise, as they did with the trade wealth which they had set aside until they used it to aid the battle of Uhud, indicated by the verse: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth﴾ [al-Anfal: 36], together with the verse: ﴿unless you do it﴾ [al-Anfal: 73]; and the explanation of the conditions of the hypocrites, indicated in al-Anfal by His words: ﴿When the hypocrites say﴾ [al-Anfal: 49]. The matter that gathers all of this is that both of them together explain the condition of the Prophet (ﷺ) at the beginning of his affair, in its course, and at its end.

Al-Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said in his book: "Its connection with al-Anfal is too clear to need any strained explanation. Indeed, the intensity of their resemblance and cohesion, although the Lawgiver, upon him be peace, had not made clear their separation, required that they not be separated by 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.' That is because al-Anfal contained the command to fight: ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah﴾ [al-Anfal: 39], and it explained the rulings on fleeing from the battle line and the ruling on the required steadfastness in it, with the incurring of sin for the one who flees; and that these are under the rule of weakness, the rule of captives, and the rule of the guardianship of the believers and what falls under this guardianship and who is excluded from it. Then in the other surah he mentioned the ruling on whoever among the polytheists had been given a covenant, and the disavowal of them if they do not fulfill it, and the ruling on whoever sought protection from them, and what is connected to this. All of it is one chapter and rulings flowing upon one story, which is the clarification of the ruling on the opponent. So the two surahs were joined in the strongest joining." Then the discourse returns to the ruling on the hypocrites and the tearing away of their veils. End.

As for the correspondence of the end of al-Anfal with its beginning, it has appeared from what has passed. Also, in the end of the surah preceding it there was the command regarding a covenant: at times to repudiate it toward those whose treachery is feared, whoever they may be, in His words: ﴿Then throw back to them [their covenant] on equal terms﴾ [al-Anfal: 58]; and at times to hold to it when there is safety from that, in His words: ﴿except for a people between you and whom there is a covenant﴾ [al-Anfal: 72]; and it distinguished who is fit for alliance and who is not. And it was concluded with the information of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge.

This surah begins with the command to repudiate people by name, who broke their covenant or were feared to do so. This is an explicit statement of what the verses of alliance in the preceding surah implied: that one of the two groups is not fit for alliance with the other. So Allah, exalted is He, said:

* *

﴿A declaration of disavowal﴾, meaning: a great one. Then He described it with His words: ﴿from﴾, meaning: attained and conveyed ﴿from Allah﴾, meaning: the One encompassing the attributes of perfection, so He is the Knower of who deserves alliance and who deserves disavowal. ﴿and His Messenger﴾, meaning: the one who follows His command, because of his knowledge of Him.

Since they had hesitated at al-Hudaybiyah, all of them or most of them, at times regarding the covenant itself and at times regarding delaying the order to shave the head, and then followed in each of these matters, and since the disbelievers were in a place far from every good, He indicated this by the particle of the limit (ila). The placing of the Messenger (ﷺ) alongside Allah is an indication that he does not oppose Him at all. And the covenant was attributed to them as an indication of that hesitation, as a warning against its recurrence. So He said, informing about the described repudiation: ﴿to those with whom you made a covenant﴾, meaning: you established a covenant between you and them ﴿of the polytheists﴾, meaning: even though your treaty with them was only by permission from Allah and His Messenger. So just as you made the treaty by their permission, do the breaking following them. The context of the speech and what it contains of wonderful coherence indicates that the covenant was only for the sake of the believers. As for Allah and His Messenger, they are free from need of it: as for Allah, by absolute self-sufficiency; as for the Messenger (ﷺ), by the One who chose him for prophethood, because He did not do that with him except that He was able to support him with cause and without cause. And it is known that this applies to whoever broke it or came close to breaking it, from His words after: ﴿except those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists, then they have not failed you in anything﴾ [al-Tawbah: 4] – the verse.

Al-Baghawi said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to Tabuk, the hypocrites were spreading rumors, and the polytheists began breaking covenants that were between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah commanded the breaking of their covenants. That is His saying: ﴿And if you fear from a people treachery, then throw back to them [their covenant]﴾ [al-Anfal: 58]. End. Ibn Ishaq and others mentioned this too. Perhaps He spoke here without restriction and did not specify those feared to break it, so that at the beginning of the surah it would signal that treachery and the intention to break were the habit of most of them, especially the polytheists of Quraysh. And they, because Quraysh are the leaders of the people and the people follow them in good and evil, deserve to be referred to by what everyone understands.

The foundation of this surah is disavowal from the polytheists and alliance with the believers, which is indicated by the obedience of Allah in prayer, zakat, and jihad against whoever is commanded to be disavowed, whether few or many, near or far, in ease and hardship, in what is pleasant and what is disliked.

When the apparent situation at the time of the complete descent of this surah, which was Shawwal, or Dhu al-Qa'dah, or Dhu al-Hijjah of the ninth year after the return of the Prophet (ﷺ) from Tabuk, was that war had laid down its burdens and its fires had been extinguished by the spreading of Islam among the special and the general, and between Yemen and Syria, and the spread of its banners and standards, and its leader and imam was strengthened by the subduing of the armies of the disbelievers, and people came to him to follow from all the cities, He emphasized the matter of jihad and confronting rivals in this surah with an emphasis not given in any other. Al-Waqidi mentioned at the end of the Battle of Tabuk a statement, then said: They said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Medina – meaning from the Battle of Tabuk – in Ramadan of the ninth year. Then he said: The Muslims began selling their weapons and saying: "Jihad has ended." So the strong among them began to buy them for the excess of their strength. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he forbade them from that and said: "A group of my community will continue to fight for the truth until the Dajjal comes out." And I only said that the complete descent of this surah was in Shawwal or in Dhu al-Qa'dah or in Dhu al-Hijjah because al-Baghawi transmitted from al-Zuhri that its beginning was revealed in Shawwal. Ibn Ishaq said – and al-Bayhaqi transmitted it from him in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah: "Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained after his departure from Tabuk for the rest of the month of Ramadan, and Shawwal, and Dhu al-Qa'dah. Then he sent Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, as commander of the Hajj in the ninth year, to establish the Hajj of the believers, while the people of polytheism were in their places of pilgrimage." And al-Bayhaqi, in his Dala'il, traced to 'Urwah who said: "When the people began the Hajj at the completion of the ninth year, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr as commander over the people and wrote for him the sunan of the Hajj." End.

Surat Bara'ah (al-Tawbah) was revealed concerning the annulment of the treaty between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the polytheists. The treaty they had made with him stipulated that no one who came to the House (the Ka'bah) would be barred from it, and that no one would be feared in the sacred month. This was a general covenant between him and the people of polytheism. Abu Muhammad al-Basti reported from him that he said: "This period, and the covenant that existed between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Arabs, was that no one would be barred from the House, that no pilgrim (hajj) or visitor (umrah) would be molested, and that no fighting would take place in the sacred month. It was a widely known security among them, one tribe toward another, without a specified term." He then returned to what I saw in his biography: "There were, besides this, covenants between his messenger (ﷺ) and some tribes of the Arabs, which were specific, up to named terms. Surah Bara'ah was revealed concerning him and concerning those hypocrites who stayed behind from him at Tabuk, and concerning what some of them said. Through it, Allah exposed the inner secrets of people who used to conceal what was other than what they displayed."

Then Ibn Hisham said: Ibn Ishaq said: Hakim ibn Hakim ibn 'Abbad ibn Hunayf narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali, that he said: "When Bara'ah was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he had sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) to lead the people in the pilgrimage. It was said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah! If only you had sent it to Abu Bakr!' He said: 'None may deliver it on my behalf except a man from my family.' Then he called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) and said to him: 'Go out with this account from the beginning of Bara'ah, and proclaim to the people on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr), when they gather at Mina, that no disbeliever will enter Paradise, that no polytheist may perform the pilgrimage after this year, that no one may circumambulate the House naked, and that whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), it remains his until its term.'"

This indicates that it was revealed after Abu Bakr's journey (may Allah be pleased with him). I have restricted the matter to the completion of its revelation only because it is reported that what concerned the annulment, which he sent with 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), consisted only of ten verses or seven. In some narrations there is an explicit statement that it was revealed before Abu Bakr's journey (may Allah be pleased with him). In the additions to the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, it is narrated from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "When ten verses of Bara'ah were revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ), he summoned Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and sent him with them to recite them to the people of Makkah. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) called me and said: 'Overtake Abu Bakr, and wherever you reach him, take the writing from him and go with it to the people of Makkah and recite it to them.'" He mentioned it, and in it: Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said to the Prophet (ﷺ) after he had returned: "Has something been revealed concerning me?" He said: "No. But Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me and said: 'None will convey on your behalf except you or a man from you.'"

Al-Baghawi narrated from Ibn Ishaq that "he (ﷺ) sent with Abu Bakr forty verses from the beginning of Surat Bara'ah to recite to the people of the season (al-mawsim). Then he sent 'Ali after him upon his she-camel al-'Adba' to recite to the people the beginning of Bara'ah, and commanded him to proclaim in Makkah, Mina and 'Arafah." In it: Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "O Messenger of Allah! Has something been revealed concerning me?" He said: "No, but it is not fitting for anyone to convey this matter except a man from my family."

Thus it becomes clear that the first (report) is the use of the whole to refer to a part, especially since it is the part containing the disavowal (bara'ah), and the surah was named Bara'ah only because of it. The meaning is: "None may deliver on my behalf concerning the covenants," not absolutely; for he sent messengers to deliver on his behalf from outside his family.

Al-Mahdawi said in his tafsir concerning: ﴿So travel freely in the land﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:2]: "It is related that this verse was revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ) after Abu Bakr had set out with the people to perform the pilgrimage with them in the ninth year. The Prophet (ﷺ) sent 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) with it to recite it to the people at the place where the two groups gather, which is Mina. He commanded him to proclaim: 'No polytheist may perform the pilgrimage after this year, and no one may circumambulate the House naked.' 'Ali proclaimed, and Abu Hurayrah and others (may Allah be pleased with them) assisted him. At that time 'Attab ibn Asid (may Allah be pleased with him) was in charge of Makkah; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had appointed him as deputy on the day of the Conquest, which was in the eighth year. The pilgrimage of 'Attab and Abu Bakr was in the ninth year, in Dhu al-Qa'dah." He said this, and the refutation of it will come later, and its contrary has preceded from Ibn Ishaq in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah.

Imam Abu Muhammad Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Basti al-Qadi said in his tafsir: Qutaybah narrated to us from al-Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he finished from Tabuk, intended to perform the pilgrimage. He said: 'Polytheists come to the House and circumambulate it naked, so I do not like to perform the pilgrimage until that no longer happens.' He sent Abu Bakr and 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both), and they went among the people at Dhu al-Majaz and at all their marketplaces where they used to trade, and throughout the entire season. They announced to the people of covenants that they would be secure for four months, meaning the sacred months that have passed (al-munsalikhat), the successive ones: twenty days from the end of Dhu al-Hijjah to ten days in Rabi' al-Akhir. After that, they would have no covenant. So he announced to all the people that there would be fighting unless they believed, and all the people believed."

In the Sirah of Ibn Ishaq: Yunus, meaning Ibn Bukayr, narrated to us from Asbat ibn Nasr al-Hamdani, from Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Suddi, concerning ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:2], that it means: "From the twentieth of Dhu al-Hijjah to the tenth of Rabi' al-Akhir. After that there is no security or covenant for anyone, except the sword or Islam."

Ibn Hisham said: Until, on the Day of Sacrifice, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) stood and proclaimed to the people what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had commanded him, and gave the people a period of four months from the day he proclaimed to them, so that every group might return to its place of safety.

In al-Tirmidhi: "From Zayd ibn Uthay' who said: I asked 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): 'With what were you sent?' He said: 'With four things: no soul will enter Paradise except a Muslim soul; no one may circumambulate the House naked; Muslims and polytheists will not gather after this year of theirs; and whoever has a covenant between himself and the Prophet (ﷺ), his covenant remains until its term, and whoever has no term, then it is four months.'"

Ibn Sayyid al-Nas narrated from Ibn 'A'idh that when he (ﷺ) set this term for the polytheists, they said: "Rather, now we do not seek that period; we disavow you and your cousin, except by striking and stabbing." So the people performed the pilgrimage that year. When they returned, Allah made the polytheists desirous (of Islam), and they entered Islam willingly and unwillingly. Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth, and no polytheist performed the pilgrimage after that year, and no one circumambulated the House naked.

Many texts and indications in much of Surat Bara'ah show that it was revealed before the return from Tabuk or before the excuse-making. Among the texts is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had it been a near gain and a moderate journey, they would have followed you; but the distance seemed long to them. They will swear by Allah, "Had we been able, we would have gone out with you."﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:42], and His saying: ﴿So if Allah returns you to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out, say: "You will never go out with me, ever."﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:83], and the verses that follow.

﴿They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say: "Make no excuses; we will not believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news."﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:94], up to His saying: ﴿They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them, that you may turn away from them﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:95].

As for the indications, al-Waqidi said in his biography: "So there was revealed of the Qur'an concerning the expedition of Tabuk," and then he mentioned most of Surat Bara'ah. He and others among the writers of biographies said: "A group of hypocrites were travelling with the Prophet (ﷺ) at Tabuk, among them Wadi'ah ibn Thabit." He mentioned the account in which some of them said, to frighten the believers: "Do you think fighting the Banu al-Asfar (the Byzantines) is like fighting others? By Allah, it is as if we see you tomorrow tied up in chains!" Each of them said something, until he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to 'Ammar ibn Yasir: "Overtake the people, for they have burned up; ask them what they said. If they deny it, say: 'Yes, you said such and such.'" ... until he said: Some of them said: "We were only plunging and playing!" So Allah revealed concerning it: ﴿And if you ask them, they will surely say, "We were only conversing and playing."﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:65] up to His saying: ﴿because they were criminals﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:66]. Then he said: Al-Jullas came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and swore that he had said nothing of that. He had said: "If Muhammad is truthful, then we are worse than donkeys." So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning him: ﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say it, but they had said the word of disbelief﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:74], to the end of it. Then al-Jullas confessed, repented, and his repentance was good.

He mentioned the mosque of harm (masjid al-dirar), and that its people had asked the Prophet (ﷺ), while he was preparing for Tabuk, to pray for them in it. He excused himself to them because of his preoccupation with the journey, and promised them that he would pray in it when he returned. When he (ﷺ) alighted at Dhu Awan, Ibn Hisham said: a place between it and Madinah about an hour of daytime, news of it and of its people came to him from heaven. He summoned two of his companions and commanded them concerning it, and they burned it. Its people scattered, and there was revealed concerning it what was revealed of the Qur'an: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:107], to the end of the account.

Al-Waqidi said: 'Asim ibn 'Adi used to say: "We were preparing for Tabuk with the Prophet (ﷺ), and I saw 'Abd Allah ibn Nabtal and Tha'labah ibn Hatib standing at the mosque of harm..." until he said: "By Allah, we had not returned from our journey before the Qur'an was revealed condemning it and its people."

﴿And those who took a mosque for harm﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:107], to its end. Among this is its being called "the Exposer" (al-Fadihah), for had it not been revealed before the knowledge of their news, it would not have been exposing. Outwardly it is for the covenanted, and inwardly it points to the people of apostasy, and that no faith is accepted from them unless they combine prayer and zakat, as Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) understood. This is supported by indications, among them the repeated combining of prayer and zakat in the context of faith, a repetition not found in other surahs. So it is among the signs of prophethood.

Abu Muhammad Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Qadi al-Basti narrated in his tafsir from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them), who said: "This religion (al-Islam) is thirty shares: ten of them are in Bara'ah, ten in al-Ahzab, and ten in al-Mu'minun, and a questioner asked..."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 2:

When Allah, glorified is He, informed them that He had returned their covenant to them, and they were mixed with the people of Islam, He provided them with a way out if they preferred to remain in polytheism. At the same time, He informed them that there was no escape for them, because they were in His grip. So He addressed them and all polytheists, giving the reason for the disavowal, saying: ﴿So travel freely﴾. *Siyaha* (wandering freely through the land) means extending one's journey and distancing oneself from cities and settlements, along with eating and drinking little. For this reason the fasting person is called *sa'ih* (one who wanders). The meaning intended here is simply travel in general.

Since *siyaha* is also used for other things, he clarified the meaning by saying: ﴿in the land﴾, that is, in whatever direction you wish.

﴿for four months﴾, that is, from the days of the Hajj, so that the last of them would be the tenth of Rabi' al-Akhir. During them you will be secure, and we will not expose you to any harm. Rather, you may go wherever you wish, or repair your fortresses, prepare your weapons, and gather your scattered affairs. We will not betray you, because our religion is founded upon good conduct. Had the matter not concerned our own souls, we would not have rejected your covenant or broken your pact. But the danger lies in the soul, and signs of treachery and tokens of evil have appeared from you. "And for which soul after my own soul shall I fight?" So when the four months have passed, prepare yourselves for our fighting and arm yourselves for our combat.

Since Islam had appeared after being hidden, and had grown strong after being weak (p. 372), he opened his admonition with the word that is said first to one whose hearing is to be shaken and whose heart is to be awakened, and to alert him that what follows is an important matter deserving added attention. So he said: ﴿And know that you﴾, that is, O disbelievers, though you are many, ﴿will not escape Allah﴾, because His knowledge encompasses everything, and He is capable of everything possible.

﴿And that Allah﴾, that is, by virtue of His encompassing majesty and generosity, ﴿will disgrace the disbelievers﴾, that is, all of them, both among you and among others, in this world and in the Hereafter. This is because His word has already preceded in this regard, and His word is not changed. *Ikhza'* (disgrace) is humiliation together with the manifestation of scandal and shame. He placed the descriptive attribute in the position of the pronoun, to generalize and to attach the ruling to it. Perhaps the shift to direct address indicates that whoever abandons the command of Allah out of partiality toward a relative or a clansman is one of them, and the protection (*dhimma*) has been cleared of him. Let him save himself, for he will have no salvation. Or it may be for the sake of winning over the disbelievers, making the address sweet to them while warning them with the threats of punishment.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 3:

When He had sent down the disavowal (al-Bara'a), He commanded that it be proclaimed at the greatest assembly, so as to cut off all excuses. He said, linking the sentence's lower part to its meaning, by way of informing about the obligation of proclaiming what was established by the first sentence that precedes it, the disavowal: ﴿And a proclamation﴾, i.e., this is a notification and public announcement that has arrived and reached ﴿from Allah﴾, i.e., the One who encompasses all attributes of greatness, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, i.e., the one whose greatness derives from His greatness, so that He does not direct him to anything without raising him above it. Since the intended purpose was the conveying, which is the function of the Messenger, He made it transitive with the particle of ending (ilaa, "to"), so He said: ﴿to mankind﴾, i.e., all of them, from among the people of the disavowal (p-373) and others, ﴿on the day of the greatest pilgrimage﴾. He restricted it, because the minor pilgrimage (al-'umra) is called the lesser pilgrimage.

Since it was as if it had been said, "What is this proclamation?", He said, explaining it and stating plainly what is intended, lest any kind of ambiguity arise, omitting the relative clause (silah) to indicate that this is a resumed statement (mustaʼnaf) based on the assumption of a questioner's question, not an object (maʼmul) of "proclamation": ﴿That Allah﴾, i.e., the One to whom belong absolute self-sufficiency and overwhelming power, ﴿is disavowed of the polytheists﴾, i.e., those who have no specific covenant, so there is no barrier to fighting them. It was said: those from whom the disavowal took place are of two categories: one whose term was less than four months, so it was raised to that term; and the other whose term was without a limit, so it was restricted to that. Whoever had no covenant at all is more deserving [of it]. And whoever had a covenant limited to more than four months, and did not commit any evil, was commanded to complete his covenant to its term. ﴿And His Messenger﴾, i.e., he is disavowed of them. It is therefore in the nominative, as a conjunction with the implied pronoun in "disavowed" (bari'un), or with the position (mahall) of "that" (anna), which is pronounced with a kasra, with its noun, according to those who read it with a kasra. It has also been read in the accusative, as a conjunction with the noun of "that" (anna), or because the waw means "with" (ma'a). It has also been read in the genitive by proximity (al-jiwar). It was said: it is by way of an oath. This is what az-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf. He said: It is related that a Bedouin heard a man reciting it, so he said: "If Allah is disavowed of His Messenger, then I am disavowed of him." The man seized him by the collar and brought him to 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. The Bedouin recounted the man's recitation. Thereupon 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, ordered the learning of Arabic (al-'Arabiyya). Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Bashshar al-Anbari related in the introduction of his book on pause and start (al-Waqf wal-Ibtida') with his chain of narration (isnad), from Ibn Abi Mulayka, who said: A Bedouin came in the time of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "Who will teach me of what Allah sent down upon Muhammad ﷺ?" A man taught him the Bara'a, so he recited: "That Allah is disavowed of the polytheists and His Messenger" with the genitive (p-374). He said: "Has Allah indeed disavowed Himself of His Messenger? If Allah is disavowed of His Messenger, then I am disavowed of him." The statement of the Bedouin reached 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, so he summoned him, meaning he questioned him and he informed him. 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It is not like this, O Bedouin!" He said: "Then how is it, O Commander of the Believers?" He said: ﴿That Allah is disavowed of the polytheists, and His Messenger﴾. The Bedouin said: "By Allah, I too am disavowed of what Allah and His Messenger are disavowed of." So 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, ordered that none should teach the Qur'an except one who knows the language.

He also commanded Abu al-Aswad, and he laid down the grammar (nahw), and similar matters in the concern for the Arabic language, as related by ash-Sharif Muhammad ibn As'ad al-Juwani, the genealogist, in his book on lineages, in the biography of Abu al-Aswad ad-Du'ali, with his chain (isnad) to him, that he said: I entered upon the Commander of the Believers, 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and I saw him bowed in thought. I said: "About what are you thinking, O Commander of the Believers?" He said: "I have heard a lahn (solecism) in this your land, so I wished to compose a book on the foundations of Arabic." I said to him: "If you do this, this language will remain among us." Then I came to him after some days, and he handed me a sheet in which was written: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Speech is entirely noun (ism), verb (fi'l), and particle (harf). The noun is what indicates the named thing; the verb is what indicates the movement (p-375) of the named thing; the particle is what indicates a meaning that is neither a noun nor a verb." Then he said: "Follow this and add to it what occurs to you. Know that things are three: the apparent, the implied, and that which is neither apparent nor implied. People differ only in recognizing what is neither implied nor apparent." Abu al-Aswad ad-Du'ali said: "So I gathered things and presented them to him, and among them were the particles of the accusative (huruf an-nasb). I mentioned from them: inna, anna, layta, la'alla, and ka'anna, and I did not mention lakinna." He said to me: "Why did you omit it?" I said: "I did not reckon it among them." He said: "Rather it is among them, so add it to them."

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan az-Zubaydi said in Tabaqat an-Nahwiyyin: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Yazid said: Abu al-Aswad ad-Du'ali was asked about the one who opened for him the way to laying down grammar and guided him to it, and he said: "I learned it from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib." In another narration: "He threw to me principles upon which I modeled." In the abridgment of their tabaqat by the memorizer Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Marzubani: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, had outlined for Abu al-Aswad ad-Du'ali some letters (huruf) to teach the people when their tongues became corrupt. He did not like to reveal that, out of stinginess with it after 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. When Ziyad came to power, he sent to him: "Do something in which you will be an imam and from which people will benefit; for you had already begun it to correct the people's tongues." So he deferred it until one day he passed by the pasture of Basra, where a reader was reciting: "That Allah is disavowed of the polytheists and His Messenger," and until he heard a man say: "My staff has fallen." He said: "It is no longer lawful for me to leave the people [like this]!" So he came to Ziyad and said: "I will do what the Amir ordered. So let him seek for me a discerning, intelligent scribe who understands what I say." So a scribe from 'Abd al-Qays was brought to him, but he did not approve of him; then another from Thaqif was brought.

Ibn al-Anbari said in the book on pause: My father related to me, saying: Abu 'Ikrima related to us, saying: al-Utbi said: Mu'awiya wrote to Ziyad asking for his son 'Ubayd Allah. When he came to him, he spoke with him and found that he committed solecisms (yalhanu). So he sent him back to Ziyad and wrote to him a letter rebuking him, saying: "Should 'Ubayd Allah be left to be ruined like this?" So Ziyad sent to Abu al-Aswad and said: "O Abu al-Aswad! This redness (al-hamra', i.e., the non-Arab masses) has increased and has corrupted the tongues of the Arabs. If only you would lay down something by which people may correct their speech and read the Book of Allah correctly." Abu al-Aswad refused this and disliked answering Ziyad's request. So Ziyad sent a man and said to him: "Sit on the path of Abu al-Aswad. When he passes by you, recite something of the Qur'an and deliberately commit a solecism in it." He did so.

When Abu al-Aswad passed by him, the man raised his voice reading: "That Allah is disavowed of the polytheists and His Messenger." Abu al-Aswad was greatly alarmed by this and said: "Exalted is the Face of Allah from disavowing Himself of His Messenger!" Then he returned at once to Ziyad and said: "O man! I have answered your request, and I have decided to begin with the i'rab (grammatical inflection) of the Qur'an. So send me thirty men." Ziyad brought them, and Abu al-Aswad chose ten of them, then he continued choosing until he chose from among them a man from 'Abd al-Qays. He said: "Take the mushaf and a dye that differs from the color of the ink. When I open my lips, put one dot above the letter; when I close them, put the dot beside the letter; when I part them (kasra), put the dot beneath it. If I follow any of these vowels with a nasal sound (ghunna), put two dots." He began with the mushaf until he reached its end. Then he placed the abridged work attributed to him after that. End quote.

The Day of the Pilgrimage mentioned here is generic (li-l-jins), i.e., in all the days of the pilgrimage, as said by Sufyan ath-Thawri, like the Day of Siffin, the Day of the Camel, and the Day of Bu'ath, meaning the time and era in which that occurred. For this reason 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, proclaimed it himself and those he appointed to do so during all those days. Abu Hayyan said: The apparent meaning is that it is one single day. 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, and a group said: It is the Day of 'Arafa, and it is related as a marfu' (attributed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ). Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, and a group said: It is the Day of Sacrifice (yawm an-nahr). It was also said: all the days of the pilgrimage. This is what Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said. Ibn 'Atiyya said: What the hadiths abundantly support is that 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, proclaimed these verses on the Day of 'Arafa, right after the sermon of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. Then he saw that he had not reached all the people by making them hear it (p-378), so he followed them up by proclaiming them again on the Day of Sacrifice. On that day Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, sent those who would assist him in proclaiming them, such as Abu Hurayra and others, may Allah be pleased with them all, and they also followed the markets of the Arabs, such as Dhu al-Majaz and others. By this the statement of Sufyan is preferred. End quote. 'Abd ar-Razzaq related from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that it is the Day of Sacrifice. He also said in his tafsir: Ma'mar informed us from al-Hasan, who said: It was only called the Greatest Pilgrimage because Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, performed the pilgrimage that he performed, in which Muslims and polytheists gathered together, and that day also coincided with the festival of the Jews and the Christians.

When He, glorified be He, had announced the disavowal concerning them, He made the following a consequence of it, encouraging and warning, by turning to direct address: ﴿So if you repent﴾, i.e., from disbelief and treachery, ﴿it is better for you﴾, i.e., that great matter, which is the repentance, ﴿for you﴾, i.e., because you will succeed in fulfilling the pledge of security in this world, and in Islam with safety in both abodes.

Since repentance is naturally loved for the benefit it brings, He said: ﴿But if you turn away﴾, i.e., you impose upon yourselves what is contrary to what is desired from repentance, in conformity with the original nature (fitra), and you persist in disbelief and treachery, following the desire acquired from the corruption of disposition and the badness of the humors which have caused the soul to fall from its first height to the lowest abyss. ﴿Then know﴾, i.e., with a knowledge free of any doubt, ﴿that you cannot escape Allah﴾ (p-379), i.e., because He possesses the attributes of perfection, of majesty and beauty. The turning of address (iltifat) here is like that in: ﴿So travel [freely]﴾ [At-Tawba: 2], and the indication of it is to what was mentioned in that.

When He had confronted them with the threat, He turned away from them, addressing the Best of His creation, in order to belittle them, giving him good news in the style of mockery toward them. So He said, linking to what is implied: "So give the treacherous the good news of humiliation," or "So give those who repent the good news of everlasting bliss": ﴿And give good news to those who disbelieved﴾, i.e., who brought about this attribute, ﴿of a painful punishment﴾, i.e., in this world and in the Hereafter, or in both.

Now when He informed them of the disavowal (al-bara'ah) and of the time at which it would be announced, and since the meaning of disavowal from them was that they had no covenant, He made an exception for some of those with whom a treaty had been made, saying: ﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant﴾, i.e., you established a covenant between yourselves and them, ﴿from among the polytheists, then﴾, i.e., after a long period of time, they were characterized by the fact that ﴿they have not fallen short of you in anything﴾, i.e., of the signs indicating fidelity in themselves, as the Banu al-Dil of the Banu Bakr broke (their covenant) in their fighting against Khuza'ah, the allies of the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿and have not supported anyone against you﴾, i.e., have not given support in a manner that shows (their backing) against you, ﴿any [of your enemies]﴾, as Quraysh supported their allies from the Banu al-Dil against your allies from Khuza'ah. ﴿So fulfill for them their covenant until their term⦆ — and He indicated their distance from good by the particle of limit (ila) — so He said: ﴿to them their covenant until their term﴿, i.e., even if it is long. Al-Baghawi said: they are the Banu Damrah, a tribe of Kinanah, and nine months remained of their covenant, and the reason for this was that they had not broken it. Al-Nahhas said: it is said that this is specific, meaning the Banu Damrah alone. Abu Muhammad al-Busti said: Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: there was a covenant between the Banu Mudlij and Khuza'ah, and they are those of whom Allah said: ﴿So fulfill for them their covenant until their term﴾.

Since their observance of their covenant is among the instances of taqwa (God-consciousness), and since the command to show kindness to a person is among the actions of one who loves, He, exalted, said, giving the reason: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, i.e., He who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿loves the righteous (al-muttaqin)﴾, i.e., He acts toward them and toward you with the actions of one who loves. Thus it is a statement urging everyone toward taqwa, and each understands it according to what he grasps, and this is from the striking miraculousness (of the Qur'an).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 5:

When he had established the matter of disavowal (al-bara'ah), affirming and negating, he commanded what to do after the term he had set for them, saying: ﴿So when﴾, that is, consequently, when ﴿the sacred months have passed﴾, that is, have ended, been stripped away, departed and gone, ﴿the sacred months﴾, that is, those in which I forbade you to fight them and made them a term for their wandering (siyahah). The definite article here is like it in: ﴿As We sent to Pharaoh a messenger﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 15], ﴿but Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 16]. ﴿Then kill the polytheists﴾, that is, the covenant-breakers for whom you set this term out of benevolence and generosity. Al-Baghawi said: al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: this verse abrogates every verse in the Qur'an that mentions turning away and patience in the face of the enemies' harm. End of quotation.

The meaning of ﴿wherever you find them﴾ is: whether within the sacred territory or outside it, in a sacred month or otherwise. ﴿And seize them﴾, that is, by capture. ﴿And besiege them﴾, that is, by confinement, preventing them from coming to the mosque and from moving freely in the lands of Islam and from every aim. ﴿And sit in wait for them﴾, that is, specifically for their sake, for that is among the best of acts of worship. ﴿At every place of ambush﴾, that is, watch for them and seize them by every route possible, even by surprise or ambush, without prior call. Its being in the accusative is as an adverb of place, because the meaning of "sit in wait for them" is "watch for them." When the verb governing a restricted adverb of place is derived from its own wording or its meaning, it may reach that adverb without the intermediary "fi" (in). Just as the verb extends to a verbal noun not of its own wording when it has the same meaning, so it extends to the adverb of place. This was mentioned by Abu Hayyan. The expression "sitting" (al-qu'ud) for watching and waiting implies deliberateness, steadiness and firm occupation, and the conveying of the verb to the place indicates that they should occupy in watching every part of every ambush-point, if they are able to do so. This differs from what would be the case had he expressed it with "fi," for that would indicate only the occupation of each ambush-point by being in one spot of it, whichever spot it might be.

When God Most High had commanded restricting them, He explained what requires holding back from them, saying: ﴿But if they repent﴾, that is, from disbelief, ﴿and establish prayer and give zakah﴾, that is, and they substantiate their claim of repentance with an upright proof by establishing ﴿the prayer and giving zakah﴾, that is, they join what is between them and the Creator and what is between them and the creatures, in humility before God Most High, abandoning corruption, and engaging in righteousness in the manner commanded by the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When these two upright witnesses are found, ﴿then let them go their way﴾, that is, because of this, ﴿their way﴾, that is, do not confront them concerning anything of what has preceded, for God accepts that from them and forgives them what has passed. ﴿Indeed﴾, that is, because ﴿Allah﴾, that is, He to whom belongs majesty and honor, ﴿is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, that is, of far-reaching erasure of the sins from which their doer has repented, and of bestowing honor upon the one who follows Him.

When He completely closed to them the path of associating with them, as long as they had not shown the repentance indicated by the two mentioned witnesses, and opened it fully once they had shown it, He followed this with another, intermediate and restricted path, saying: ﴿And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection﴾, i.e., those whom We have commanded you to fight, ﴿seeks your protection﴾, i.e., asks that you deal with him in honour, as one deals with a neighbour, after the period of travel has ended, ﴿then grant him protection﴾, i.e., give him safety and defend him against anyone who intends him harm, ﴿until he hears the word of Allah﴾, i.e., of the Supreme King, by hearing the recitation that indicates Him, so that he knows from it what he is being called to of excellent qualities, and becomes certain that it is not the speech of created beings. When He mentioned his protection, and it was possible that after it he would repent or persist, and since the case of the one who repents had already been mentioned, He explained what is to be done with him if he persists, saying: ﴿Then deliver him to his place of safety﴾, i.e., if he wishes to depart and has not become Muslim, to the place where he will be safe. Then fight him after he reaches his place of safety, if you wish, without (p-383) treachery or betrayal. Al-Hasan said: this ruling is muhkam (definitive) until the Day of Resurrection. Then He gave the reason for this, which shows their treachery, saying: ﴿That is because they are a people who do not know﴾, i.e., the command to grant protection for the stated purpose is due to the fact that they are a people with no knowledge, for they have no covenant with prophethood, messengership, or scripture. Once they come to know, it is likely that knowledge will benefit them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 7:

When the command to renounce (the covenants) was likely to cause surprise, He expressed wonder and said: who, then, is surprised at it? He also disapproved of it, saying: ﴿How can there be for the polytheists﴾, that is, the people of ancient standing in polytheism, whose long-established ways and love of its prominence make them break the covenant, which among the Arabs has no more shameful or abominable act, ﴿a covenant with Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses all the attributes of perfection, so He does not love the breaking of it from His allies, let alone from His enemies, ﴿and with His Messenger﴾, that is, the one who is the most perfect of creation, the most faithful, the most mindful of covenants and the most observant of them. They are his opposites, so their deeds are the opposites of his deeds, and treachery has already appeared from them.

Since the interrogative of denial carries the sense of negation, the exception from it is valid, so it is as if it was said: there shall not be for the polytheists a covenant ﴿except those with whom you made a covenant﴾, that is, from among them, as has preceded, ﴿at the Sacred Mosque﴾, that is, the Sacred Precinct, on the day of Hudaybiyah. This indicates that the preceding exception from ﴿those﴾ in His saying: ﴿A declaration of immunity from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists﴾ [al-Tawbah: 1] (p-384) was narrated by al-Baghawi: al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Ibn Ishaq said: they are from the tribes of Bakr: Banu Khuzaymah, Banu Mudlij, Banu Damrah and Banu al-Dil, and they were the ones who had entered into the covenant of Quraysh on the day of Hudaybiyah. Only Quraysh and Banu al-Dil from Banu Bakr broke the covenant, so he ordered that the covenant be fulfilled for those who had not broken it. When he made the exception, he explained the ruling concerning those excepted, saying: ﴿So as long as they remain true to you﴾, that is, they take the most upright path in fulfilling their covenant, ﴿then be true to them﴾. The discussion of ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing majesty and beauty, ﴿loves those who are mindful of Him﴾ is as has preceded.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 8:

When Allah, glorified is He, denied that the polytheists other than those excepted could have a covenant, He explained the cause that necessitates the denial, repeating the interrogative particle of denial for emphasis of the meaning, and He said: ﴿How﴾, i.e., how could they have a firm covenant, ﴿when﴾, i.e., while the situation is that they conceal treachery and betrayal toward you, so that if they ﴿gain the upper hand over you﴾, i.e., if they prevail over you, by overcoming you after the covenant and pledge, ﴿they will not observe﴾, i.e., they will not regard or respect, ﴿concerning you﴾, i.e., in harming you, ﴿any tie of kinship [ill]﴾, i.e., any binding kinship, ﴿nor covenant﴾, i.e., pact. He means that the matter that permits the repudiation is the fear of betrayal, and the All-Knowing of the unseen informs you that they are in the utmost degree of betrayal toward you. The word "il" (ill) here means kinship, and this is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas. The root revolves around the meaning of "ala" (lance), which is a spear with a broad blade, and it entails clearness, thinness and brightness; and it is used as a figure for swift running and for steadfastness in itself. From it come kinship, covenant, and change in its description; and from it come the change of the smell of a vessel, the decay of teeth and of the voice, and from it the moaning and wailing in supplication along with weeping, the flowing of water, piercing and subduing. From it also comes: "Indeed, this" — i.e., the speech of Musaylima — "is not from il," i.e., from lordship, and "in the il of Allah," i.e., His power and divinity.

Since that was a likely occasion for someone to say: "They have confirmed oaths to us and strengthened covenants, and have left no door of appeal unturned," He said, giving the reason for what has passed and responding to one who finds it unlikely: ﴿They please you﴾, and He expressed it with the furthest extent to which speech can go from the heart, to establish that there is nothing of it in their hearts, so He said: ﴿with their mouths﴾, i.e., with that confirmation. He stated the intended meaning with His saying: ﴿but their hearts refuse﴾, i.e., refuse to act upon what their tongues have expressed. Few among them are those whom fear or the like leads to steadfastness, or who turn back from defiance and believe. ﴿And most of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, i.e., firmly rooted in defiance, outside—because their deeds contradict their words—of what you seek. And when most of them break their word, the minority is compelled to agree with them.

[p-386] Since what you see of the uncovering of their inner selves has continued, He, glory be to Him, began to establish the proof against their wickedness and treachery by reminding them of what appeared from some of them of breaking the covenant. Earlier He had established that they were one body, some of them allies of others, and later that they were some of them from others. So He said, expressing by a phrase that conveys that they had become so firmly entrenched in opposition to faith that it was as if it were in their possession: ﴿They have bought﴾, meaning they persisted in their desires after the proof had been established, a proof about which they had no doubt. Then they took ﴿the signs of Allah﴾, meaning that which has nothing like it in majesty or beauty, despite its great worth in itself and its being attributed to Him, ﴿for a small price﴾ from the passing goods of this world. They were satisfied with it while remaining in disbelief. This is because Abu Sufyan fed them a meal, and they broke their covenants because of it. ﴿So they barred﴾, meaning that this caused for them and led them to bar ﴿from His way﴾, meaning anyone who wished to walk upon it, and they prevented themselves and whoever they were able to prevent from entering the religion.

When He had indicated what He had reported of the corruption of their hearts, He began to explain the great blame they deserved, saying, marveling at them: ﴿Evil is what they have done﴾. He showed that their deep-rootedness in ugly deeds, and that these were in their nature, by mentioning the verb of being, so He said: ﴿they used to do﴾, meaning they renewed their practice of it at every time. It seems that He, glory be to Him, is pointing by this to what Adal and al-Qarah did to Asim ibn Thabit and Khubayb ibn Adi. Ibn Ishaq mentioned in the Sirah, from Asim ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, and al-Bukhari in the Sahih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, each adding to the other's account. I have combined their two narrations: "A group of Adal and al-Qarah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) after Uhud and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, there is Islam among us, so send with us some of your companions to instruct us in the religion, to recite the Qur'an to us, and to teach us the laws of Islam.' So he sent with them six men, and al-Bukhari said ten, and he appointed Asim ibn Thabit over them, and he went out with them. When they reached al-Raji' (a water belonging to Hudhayl), they betrayed them and called upon Hudhayl against them. When they came to them, they drew their swords to fight them. They said: 'By Allah, we do not want to kill you, but we want to get some of the people of Makkah in exchange for you, but we give you the covenant and pledge of Allah that we will not kill any of you.' As for Asim, he did not accept and fought until he was killed, along with some of his companions. Three men from them came down under the covenant and pledge, and when they had gained control over them, they loosened the strings of their bows and tied them with them. One of them said: 'This is the first treachery! By Allah, I will not accompany you. Indeed, I have an example in these,' meaning the dead. They dragged him and struggled with him, but he refused to go with them, so they killed him. They then took Khubayb and Zayd ibn al-Dathinah, and sold them in Makkah, and they killed them."

And the story of the 'Uraniyyin, who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and professed Islam, then went out to the Prophet's (ﷺ) milch camels, killed the herdsman, and drove off the camels after they had seen the signs. So the Prophet (ﷺ) sent in pursuit of them and he killed them. In the History of Ibn al-Furat, from al-Qutaybi: "The Prophet (ﷺ) sent Abdullah ibn Awsajah al-Bajali to the Banu Harithah ibn Amr ibn Qurt with a letter, and they threw his bucket with the letter in it. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'What is wrong with them! May Allah take away their minds! They are people of trembling and confused speech.'" And when the people of Makkah went out, after he (ﷺ) had dealt with them with the utmost kindness, freed them and pardoned them after those wars and harms, in the extremes of their attacks that only the prophets pardon the like of, they went out with him to Hunayn, not wishing to support him nor loving the elevation of his cause, but rather they were the ones who routed the people. This is as al-Baghawi related from Qatadah. Abu Hayyan said: "It is said that the Tulaqa' from the people of Makkah fled, intending to cast defeat upon the Muslims, and their group reached Makkah." End of quotation.

Al-Waqidi said: "The men of Makkah went out with the Prophet (ﷺ), and none of them stayed behind out of disbelief, riding and on foot, looking to see on whose side the turn of fortune would fall, so that they might obtain booty, and they did not dislike that the blow should fall upon Muhammad and his companions." He and others said: "When the defeat came, and the turn of fortune was against the Muslims, a people spoke of what was in their hearts of disbelief, rancor, and deceit, and mentioned that some of them had resolved to kill the Prophet (ﷺ), but Allah protected him from them."

This is some of what the disbelieving Arabs were guilty of breaking. As for the Jews, all of them broke their covenants: Banu Qaynuqa', then al-Nadir, then Quraydhah, then the people of Khaybar, until that became the cause of their expulsion from it and their exile to the lands of Syria. It is possible that this is an indication that the truth had become clear to them all, like the morning light, of what the Prophet (ﷺ) had told them. When they did not return merely because of their desires, they had bought with that a small price, which is enjoyment of what they were in for the duration of their lives, in their descent into lowliness of word and reversal of affairs. Whoever his desire leads him to abandon the supreme happiness for this passing, small worldly good is not to be trusted with anything, because he is a hostage to the caller of desire and the command of Satan; for he first began with himself, so he betrayed it and deceived it, without looking to any benefit or reflecting upon any consequence.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 10:

When God, exalted is He, informed of their deep-rootedness in corruption (fisq), He indicated it by stating that their treachery is not restricted to those addressed, but is general to everyone who is characterized by their attribute of faith. Thus the basis of their treachery lies in the attribute, and so He said: ﴿They do not observe regarding a believer any tie of kinship (illan)﴾, that is, kinship and a good, firm origin; ﴿nor any pact (dhimmah)﴾, that is, a binding covenant; ﴿and those are the transgressors (al-mu'tadun)﴾, that is, those far removed from all good, ﴿they﴾, that is, specifically, because of the extremity of their aggression. ﴿The transgressors﴾, that is, their habit is to exaggerate in driving themselves to overstep the limits, due to the absence of any divine restraint (wazi') or legal deterrent (radi') that would hold them back from that, as Amir ibn al-Tufayl did to the people of Bi'r Ma'unah, although they were under the protection of his uncle. Among the account of them: "that his uncle, Abu Bara' Amir ibn Malik ibn Ja'far, the spear-player (mula'ib al-asinnah), came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said to him: 'If you were to send men from your companions to the people of Najd, I hope they would respond to you.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'I fear for them from the people of Najd.' Abu Bara' said: 'I am their protector (jar).' So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr, brother of Banu Sa'idah, the one called al-Mu'anaq, to be killed along with seventy men of his companions (p-390), from the best of the Muslims. When they arrived at Bi'r Ma'unah, they sent Haram ibn Milhan with the letter of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to Amir ibn al-Tufayl, but he did not look at his letter and attacked him and killed him. Then he called upon Banu Amir for help against them, but they refused and said: 'We will not betray Abu Bara'.' So he called for help against them from tribes of Banu Sulaym: 'Usayyah, Ri'l and Dhakwan, and they killed them, and none escaped from them except three men, one of whom was 'Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri. This weighed heavily upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and he invoked against their killers for a month.'" Al-Baghawi said: Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: "The people of al-Ta'if supplied them—meaning Quraysh—with wealth to strengthen them against fighting the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." Thus, what God, exalted is He, has decreed regarding the abrogation of the covenant is a consideration for the religion, because it considers all its people, among whom it exists only through them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 11:

When he had explained what caused their distance from them and their hostility toward them, he explained what makes them (the disbelievers) into people (who are entitled to be treated as) brothers, and said: ﴿But if they repent﴾, i.e., by faith, because of what you have shown them of harshness (ghilzah); ﴿and establish﴾, i.e., they confirm that by ﴿establishing the prayer﴾, i.e., with all its limits (hudud); ﴿and give the zakah﴾, i.e., as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prescribed it; ﴿then they are your brothers﴾, i.e., they are; and he made clear that this is not brotherhood of lineage, so he said: ﴿in religion﴾. For them is what is for you, and upon them is what is upon you, so do not confront them with what they dislike.

When it was as if it had been said, as an urging and encouragement to reflect upon what he had detailed: "We have indeed detailed for you their affair in these verses in detail," he followed it with His saying: ﴿And We detail﴾, i.e., in every matter they need, all of the ﴿verses﴾. He magnified these verses and urged them to ponder them by His saying: ﴿for a people who know﴾, i.e., knowledge has become a quality for them, so they have a faculty by which they manage its roots and branches, and they are not deceived by mere speech whose nature is baseness and a contradiction between word and deed. The interjection of this between these closely linked sentences is a signal of the greatness of the matter he drew attention to, and an exhortation to examine it thoroughly, so it is known that what follows it is a matter of great importance and grand worth, lest it be thought to be mere repetition.

When he had explained the cause that makes them liable to be repaid in kind, namely disavowal of them and what follows from it, up to his concluding with the stipulation of their repentance, he returned to the counterpart of his words, ﴿So long as they remain upright toward you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 7], and said: ﴿But if they break their oaths﴾, meaning the oaths they swore to you. Since breaking an oath is harmful even when its duration is short, he used the preposition and said: ﴿after their covenant﴾, meaning the covenant they had contracted, ﴿and they attack﴾, meaning they inflict attacks ﴿upon your religion﴾, meaning by word or by deed.
