Then that sea came from Egypt until it reached the land of Palestine, passing by Ascalon and its shores, reached Beirut, and penetrated to the shores of Homs and Qinnasrin, until it mingled with the region from which the Euphrates had come, descending upon the edges of Qinnasrin and the Jazirah down to the black land of Iraq. The mountain of al-Sarah came from the depths of Yemen until it reached the edges of Syria, and the Arabs touched it as Hijaz, because it blocked between the Ghawr and Najd. So what lay behind that mountain on its western side was the Ghawr, which is Tihamah, and what lay before it on its eastern side was Najd." End of quotation.

Since what bordered it of the land of Syria and its like was entirely rivers or streams, it was treated as if it were a sea, since it has the status of its shore. Since their livelihood depended on trade, and the livelihood of trade depended on their gathering in their markets, and since their expulsion from those lands was likely to cause the severance of trade and the disappearance of profits, leading to need, and since He had commanded their expulsion out of concern for the matter of religion, and since He, glorified be He, knew that this would be hard on souls for the reason mentioned, especially since one of them said when ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) recited the verses of Bara'ah to the people of the season: "O people of Makkah! You will know the hardship you will face from the cutting of the road and the distance of the caravans," He, glorified be He, who is the Vast and the All-Knowing, promised what would make up for that. For whoever abandons the world for the sake of religion, Allah, glorified be He, brings him to what he seeks from the world along with the happiness he attains in religious matters. "Whoever leaves something for Allah, Allah will replace it for him with something better." So He said: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾, meaning: because of their being prevented from approaching the divine sites, ﴿poverty (ʿaylah)﴾, meaning: want and need. ﴿then Allah will enrich you﴾, meaning: He is the One of majesty and honor. ﴿from His bounty﴾, and He is the One of bounty, favor, strength, and power.

Since He, glorified be He, is the King, the Rich, the Powerful, the Strong, to whom nothing is owed by anyone and whose obedience is due from everything, He drew attention to this by His words: ﴿if He wills﴾. Since this was considered unlikely by them, He gave an explanation to bring it near, by His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, meaning: the One who has complete encompassing, ﴿is All-Knowing﴾, meaning: of the aspects of benefits, ﴿All-Wise﴾, meaning: in arranging their attainment and determining their flow. Allah, glorified be He, has indeed spoken truly, and who is more truthful in speech than Allah? For He enriched them, with the spoils that came into their hands about three years after their revelation, from the treasures of Khosrow and Caesar, with a wealth that never crossed their imaginings. Then He made that a cause for the mingling of some groups of all people with one another, as they became brothers in the religion, which was the cause for gathering, at the market of Mina and elsewhere during the days of the Hajj every year, of merchants of the Arabs and non-Arabs in a number unlike that found in any other place on earth. The term ʿaylah means poverty and need, and its root, in this order, revolves around need and the closing of avenues of provision. It was mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-Nisa' that its eight permutations, without regard to order, revolve around elevation, which entails increase and inclination, and from this comes need. He demonstrated this in all its particulars.

Since that was a matter of wonder, which would naturally prompt the question, "From where does that wealth come?", He answered with His words: ﴿Fight﴾, that is, the people of wealth and affluence, ﴿those who do not believe in Allah﴾, that is, in the One who possesses all the attributes of perfection, with a belief that conforms to what His messengers have told about Him. Had they believed in this way, they would not have denied any of the messengers. Moreover, the Christians are trinitarians, and some of the Jews are dualists. ﴿Nor in the Last Day﴾, that is, likewise. At the very least, they do not affirm the resurrection of bodies. ﴿Nor do they forbid what Allah has forbidden﴾, that is, the Sovereign Most High, to whom all command belongs, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, that is, of polytheism, the consuming of people's wealth by falsehood, and other such things, and of altering the Torah and the Gospel. ﴿Nor do they adopt the religion﴾, that is, they do not act upon it or establish it. He derived a verb from "dīn" (religion) and then attached it to its description, in order to emphasize their adopting it with that quality, so He said: ﴿the religion of truth﴾, that is, the one upon which their messengers took their covenants and pledges to follow it. Then He specified the relative clause together with its complement, saying: ﴿of those who﴾. The indication of His, glorified be He, disdain for them and His disassociation from them (p-435) is that He used the passive form in His words: ﴿have been given the Book﴾, that is, from among the Jews and Christians and those joined to them, ﴿until they pay the jizyah﴾, that is, the tax prescribed upon them in return for living securely in the lands of Islam. Its verb is from "jazā, yajzī."

When they pay what is due from them, ﴿with willing hand﴾, that is, with a dominating hand if the hand is that of the one who takes, or a subdued hand if it is the hand of the one who gives, from the saying of people: "So-and-so gave with his hand." ﴿And they are humbled﴾. In that there is a wealth unlike what you were engaged in, of fighting one another to seize what is in his hand of that base wealth, nor like the trades which you regarded as wealth, none of whose greatest or smallest yield reaches what We have guided you to, together with the honor, attainable through reform and obedience, that it entails. And you will see. He expressed by "hand" the force from which humiliation and subjugation arise, because it is the striking instrument. So the meaning is: "with a hand that dominates them," that is, through subjugation from you over them and force by means of deeds which their greatness has made them small and whose severity has humbled them. Abu 'Ubayda said: It is said of anyone who gives something unwillingly, not from good will: "He gave it with a hand." End of quotation.

He expressed it with "ʿan" (from), which denotes separation, because giving does not occur except after humiliating subjugation. This is the case if "hand" is taken to mean the hand of the one who takes. It is also possible that "hand" means the hand of the giver, and it is then a metonymy for the self, since the purpose of the jizyah is wealth, and the hand is its greatest means. So the meaning is: "until each one of them gives the jizyah from himself."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 30:

Since the intended meaning is generality, [the word "Jizya" (poll tax)] is given in the indefinite form so that it conveys this. This is supported by what the scholars have transmitted from the narrators of the conquests of lands, among them the memorizer (al-Hafiz) Abu al-Rabi' ibn Salim al-Kala'i, who said in his book *al-Iktifa' fi Waq'at Jalula'* (on the battle of Jalula' in the lands of Persia): (p-436) They said: some of them said: "The peasants were for the roads, the bridges, the markets, and the tillage, and the *dalala* (guidance/service) together with the *jizya* was from their hands according to their capacity. The *dihqans* (landed notables) were for the jizya from their hands and for the cultivation. They took the jizya from the Magians (Majus) only because the Prophet ﷺ took it from the Magians of Hajar, and he took it from them because they were originally people of a scripture." Al-Shafi'i said, in the chapter on the general and the specific (*al-mujmal wa al-mufassar*) in the book *Ikhtilaf al-Hadith* (Divergence of Hadith): "The Magians are people of a scripture other than the Torah and the Gospel. They forgot their book and altered it, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted taking the jizya from them." Sufyan informed us, from Abu Sa'd Sa'id ibn Marzuban, from Nasr ibn Asim, who said: Farwa ibn Nawfal al-Ashja'i said: "On what basis is the jizya taken from the Magians when they are not people of a scripture?" Then al-Mustawrid stood up to him, seized him by his collar, and said: "O enemy of Allah! You criticize Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali, Commander of the Believers"—meaning Ali—"when they took the jizya from them?" So he took him to the palace. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, came out to them both and said: "Enough! Enough!" So they both sat in the shade of the palace. Ali said: "I am the most knowledgeable of people about the Magians. They had a knowledge which they knew and a book which they studied. Their king became drunk and fell upon his daughter or his sister. Some of the people of his kingdom saw him. When he sobered, they came to enforce the punishment upon him, but he refused them. So he summoned the people of his kingdom and said: 'Do you know of a religion better than the religion of Adam, when Adam used to marry his sons to his daughters? So I am upon the religion of Adam.' So they pledged allegiance to him, and they fought those who opposed them until they killed them. In the morning, their book had been lifted, and it was removed from among them, and the knowledge that was in their breasts went away. Yet they are people of a scripture, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, took the jizya from them."

When He commanded fighting against them and described them with that which is the cause motivating it, He followed it with some of their statements that permit fighting them and make their punishment obligatory. He said: ﴿And said﴾, i.e., the speakers among the People of the Book (because they disbelieved in what We described them with), and ﴿the Jews﴾ among them said, falsely and calumniously: ﴿Uzayr﴾. The tanwin (nunation) of Asim and al-Kisa'i makes it clear that it is a subject (*mubtada'*), while the rest withheld it (from tanwin) considering its foreignness together with its being a proper name, and there is no diminutive in it. The predicate in this reading is their statement: ﴿is the son of Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses absolute exaltedness, so "there is nothing like unto Him." This Uzayr is the one called among them, in the Book of the Prophets, *Malakhya*, and he is also called *al-Azir*, which is the original, and *Uzayr* is its Arabicization. As for the one who compiled for them this Torah which is in their hands, al-Samaw'al ibn Yahya al-Maghribi, who had been a Jew and then embraced Islam, said: "He is another person named *Ezra*, and he was not a prophet." He mentioned this in his book *Ghayat al-Maqsud fi al-Radd 'ala al-Nasara wa al-Yahud* (The Aim of the Intent in Refuting the Christians and Jews), which is a very good book. This al-Samaw'al, despite his thorough knowledge of the law of the Jews and their reports, was well-versed in the sciences of geometry and others, was eloquent and articulate, (p-438) had excellent Islam, and his intelligence was proverbial. I saw that the Jews were in extreme animosity toward him, and one of them showed me a letter addressed to him from one of their rabbis, deriding his opinion about his Islam and confusing him with rhetorical and poetic devices. He replied to it with a wonderful reply, opening it with the words of the Exalted: ﴿The foolish among the people will say: "What has turned them from their qibla which they used to face?"﴾ [al-Baqara: 142]. Then he refuted his speech in the best refutation, and then said to him, in substance: "Leave aside such fables, and answer the matters I have obligated you with in the book *Ghayat al-Maqsud*." So he could not find an answer. Then, the one who uttered this statement among them—it is narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they were four; and it was said that the speaker was one, and it was attributed to all, as one says: "So-and-so rides horses," though he may have only one horse. This is like the Exalted's statement: ﴿Those to whom the people said﴾ [Al 'Imran: 173]. And it was said: this (saying) was widespread among them, and when Allah reproached them for it, they abandoned it, and they now deny it. And Allah is the Truest in speech. ﴿And the Christians said﴾, i.e., some of them, falsely and aggressively: ﴿the Messiah﴾, and they reported about him with their saying: ﴿is the son of Allah﴾, i.e., although He possesses absolute independence and supreme perfection. This Messiah is the son of Mary, daughter of Imran. Then he began a new sentence, interpreting the two statements of the two groups: ﴿That﴾, i.e., this statement, far from sound reason and contradicting the transmitted reports, ﴿is their saying with their mouths﴾, i.e., it is a bare utterance, which they were not ashamed of saying, despite its feebleness. Yet, with that, it is a statement whose reality does not go beyond the mouths to the intellects, because no rational person can conceive it. Rather, it is a meaningless utterance, like the sounds of dumb animals, whose meaning cannot be realized. He said: "Its apparent meaning is that its speaker has no intellect; it has no meaning beyond that. And because of its remoteness from being intended by any rational person, He expressed it with 'mouths,' which are further away than tongues from hearts."

Since it was as if it were said: "Why then do they say it, when this is their condition?" He said, in substance: "They are a people naturally inclined to imitate those who commit corruptions, just as they imitated the idol-worshippers, so they worshipped them more than once, while the prophets were among them calling them to Allah, and their Book calls to the like of that and warns them with the most severe warning." ﴿Imitating﴾, i.e., while they resemble, by this saying of theirs, ﴿the saying of those who disbelieved﴾, i.e., the like of it, namely the Arabs, when they said: "The angels are the daughters of Allah." Just as, when they saw those who devote themselves to idols they had, they said: ﴿O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods﴾ [al-A'raf: 138].

Since it is not impossible that those whom they resembled were after them, or in their time, before the clarification of the corruption of their saying, He negated that by His saying, indicating by the preposition (*harf al-jarr*) that their disbelief did not encompass the whole time before: ﴿before﴾, i.e., before this saying arose among them. This is evidence that the Arabs had altered the religion of Isma'il, peace be upon him, and had dared to utter the like of this saying before Bukhtanassar's attack on the Jews (p-440) or within its times. This is not far-fetched, given the long passage of time and the seduction of Satan. Indeed, between the time of Ibrahim and Uzayr, peace be upon them both, there were about fifteen hundred years—this according to what some scholars of the People of the Book related from their books, and it is supported by what al-Mas'udi mentioned in *Muruj al-Dhahab* (Meadows of Gold) regarding the kings of Babylon from Nimrod to Bukhtanassar. Some historians mentioned that the interval between the two periods exceeded two thousand years. Moreover, they transmitted what is explicit about the disbelief of the Arabs in that era. They related from Hisham ibn al-Kalbi that he said: "The beginning of the descent of the Arabs into the land of Iraq was that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Barkhiya, from the descendants of Judah: 'Go to Bukhtanassar and command him to raid the Arabs, whose houses have no doors, and to trample their lands with the armies, to kill their fighters, take their families captive, and seize their wealth. And inform him of their disbelief in Me, their taking of gods besides Me, and their denial of My prophets and messengers.'" And from someone other than Ibn al-Kalbi: that he arranged horsemen and infantry between Ubulla and al-Ayla, then they entered upon the Arabs and seized every living being they could overpower. Allah also enjoined on Barkhiya and Irmiya regarding Ma'add ibn Adnan, from whose offspring is Muhammad, with whom prophethood was sealed. He had mentioned their resemblance to the people of polytheism in order to belittle their status, to embolden [the Babylonians] to attack them, since He made them resemble those whom they had trained to fight and against whom they had marshaled [forces], and so they humiliated them after they had been in a might whose loss they did not fear, and in firm resolves whose dissolution they did not dread (p-441). All of that was by obedience to Allah in fighting them and seeking His pleasure by battling them, for He was against them, and whoever Allah is against does not prosper. He alluded to this in His saying concerning these people: ﴿Allah destroy them﴾, i.e., may the Supreme King destroy them, for whoever is fought by Him does not escape from Him. It was also said: "He curses them." It is narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Everything in the Qur'an of this form ('qatalahum Allah') is a curse."

﴿How are they deluded?﴾, i.e., how and from where are they turned away from the truth, when the decisive proofs for it are established?

Then He increased them in audacity against them, by alluding to the weakness of their basis, since it was a created being like themselves, through His saying: ﴿They took﴾, that is, they imposed upon themselves the deviation from God, the Capable over everything, and took ﴿their rabbis﴾, that is, from the scholars of the Jews. The ḥabr (scholar) originally means a learned person from any group. ﴿And their monks﴾, that is, from the ascetics of the Christians. The rāhib (monk) originally refers to one in whose heart awe (rahba) has taken firm hold, so that its traces appear on his face and clothing; by convention it became specific to the scholars of the Christians, the people of the monasteries (ṣawāmi'). ﴿As lords﴾, that is, as gods, because they did what belongs exclusively to the Lord, namely forbidding what they forbade and permitting what they permitted. He indicated the lowliness of their affair by His saying: ﴿besides God﴾, that is, the One possessing all attributes of majesty, so they relied on them and attributed their affairs to them, to the extent that they would follow them in what is lawful and unlawful. ﴿And the Messiah﴾, that is, the blessed one, who is fit to be anointed with the oil of holiness and to anoint others, ﴿son of Mary﴾, that is, (p-442) they took him likewise, since they made him a son and thereby qualified him for worship, despite his being the son of a woman. He is not fit for divinity in any respect, since he shares with human beings in gestation, birth, nurture, eating, drinking, and other human conditions that entail need and are incompatible with divinity. Moreover, he himself declared to them that he is the servant of God and His messenger. Thus reason and transmitted text agree that he is not a god.

When He disparaged for them what they had chosen for themselves, He disparaged it for them from the aspect of its opposition to His command, the Exalted, and said: ﴿And they were not commanded﴾, that is, they did that while the situation was that they had not been commanded, by anyone who holds authority, from the proofs of reason and transmitted text, ﴿except to worship﴾, that is, to obey in the manner of devotion, ﴿one God﴾, that is, who admits no division in any respect, neither in essence nor in likeness. That is the meaning of describing Him as: ﴿there is no god but He﴾, that is, it is not fitting that there be with Him another god. Since this was established for God, and His rank is exalted, He removed Him far from what they associated with Him, declaring Him free of it by His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, that is, His rank is far and high, ﴿above what they associate﴾ with Him in being worshipped or prescribed.

Abū Muḥammad Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Bustī al-Qāḍī mentioned in his tafsir, and others, from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while there was a golden cross around my neck. He said: 'Remove it,' so I removed it. Then I came to him while he was reciting Sūrat Barā'ah: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and the Messiah, son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no god but He. Glory be to Him above what they associate.﴾" I said: "O Messenger! (p-443) We did not worship them!" He said: "Indeed. Did they not make lawful for you what Allah had made unlawful, so you deemed it lawful, and make unlawful for you what Allah had made lawful, so you deemed it unlawful?" I said: "Yes." He said: "That is their worship."

The commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 32:

When He, glorified is He, had weakened their reliance (on their own power), He increased the weakening from the side of their desire, by informing that their fighting against the people of obedience is in fact fighting against God, and that He does not carry out their purpose, but rather wills other than what they will. It is established that nothing happens except what He wills. So He said, beginning anew or giving the reason for what preceded of their sayings and deeds: ﴿They want to extinguish﴾, that is, by what has been mentioned of their conditions, ﴿the light of God﴾, that is, the religion of the Sovereign King, who has the supreme encompassing, and His law which He prescribed for His servants through the tongues of the prophets and messengers. All of this is so that they may be able to act according to their aims and desires, for following the messengers is a decisive check on the appetites, and they are the furthest of people from that.

When He belittled their affair, He demolished it entirely by His saying: ﴿with their mouths﴾, that is, with a speech empty of anything that establishes it, or enforces it and carries it into effect. In calling His religion a light, and their opposition to it an attempt to extinguish it with mouths, there is an image of their condition as the condition of one who wants to extinguish the light of the sun by blowing on it. ﴿But God refuses﴾, that is, while the situation is that He does what the refuser does, which is that He does not accept, ﴿except that He perfect His light﴾, that is, He does not limit Himself to the mere shining of it, but rather He has promised, and His word is the truth, that it is necessary that it be completed (p-444) and that all else be extinguished and burned away. Because "yaʾbā" (refuses) contains the sense of denial, an exception was introduced after it, meaning: He refuses every state except the state of perfecting His light, continuously and perpetually. ﴿Although the disbelievers dislike it﴾, that is, those who are deeply immersed in disbelief, so how about others?

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 33:

When He had informed that He elevates His word and that He makes it complete, and that He lowers the word of those who oppose it, He gave a reason for that, the gist of which is that it is the custom of kings: when a matter has emerged for them, they do not accept that anyone should reject it. For that is the spirit of the king, who does not requite one who disparages it except with destruction. So He said: ﴿He it is Who sent His Messenger﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿with guidance﴾, that is, to make clear what heals by means of the miracles, both verbal and practical, ﴿and the religion of truth﴾, that is, perfect in its clarity and its firmness, perfect in a manner evident to every intelligent person. Then He increased them in boldness against the enemy by saying, giving the reason for His sending: ﴿that He may make it prevail﴾, that is, the Messenger (ﷺ) and the religion, may God perpetuate its prevalence, ﴿over all religion﴾. He presented all of this in the manner of an answer to one who seems to say: "How can we fight them when they are in such abundance and strength, as is not hidden?" So He said: "Why do you not fight them, when you do not rely on anyone other than Him under whose subjugation everything is, while they rely only on creatures like you? How do you not dare against them, when in fighting you they are only fighting your Lord, whose obedience you are in?" Or: "How do you not confront them, when it is He Who commanded you to fight them, so that He may help you and make manifest His signs?" Perhaps concluding with His saying ﴿though the polytheists dislike it﴾ is more eloquent, because disbelief may not involve obstinacy, whereas polytheism is founded on obstinacy by taking rivals, meaning: there is no escape from your being victorious over whoever opposes with mere opposition, or who adds to that opposition obstinacy by seeking help from whomever he wishes.

When he belittled their affair by making their reliance on their leaders a matter of division, and their state is well known in that they have neither benefit nor harm with them, and he exalted the affair of the people of God by gathering them upon it, and He is the One capable of all things, and turning toward this world was the greatest sign of abandonment (*khidhlan*), even if it were for something true, so how much more so for falsehood! He, glorified and exalted in status, turned toward the people of His love, seeking their inclination and gentleness, calling them by the name of faith, which He had founded His command upon at the beginning of this Book on spending rather than on acquiring, even if it were for something true, so how much more so if it were for falsehood. ﴿And they pay the zakat, and spend of what We have provided them﴾, alerting to the foolishness of one who leaves off him who does not ask him for anything, in exchange for giving guidance and calling to the religion of truth, while he is a pure envoy who does not speak from desire, and did not regard him as a messenger, and took as a lord one like himself, while he takes their wealth by falsehood as usury (*ribwan*). That necessitates their belittlement, not a general glorifying of them, let alone the rank to which they raised themselves and to which they qualified themselves, along with exalting themselves over them, for the purpose of consuming their wealth by falsehood. So He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning: those who affirmed the faith of their caller, from denial and what leads to it. ﴿Indeed, many of the rabbis﴾ [p. 446] meaning: from the scholars of the Jews, ﴿and the monks﴾ meaning: from the ascetics of the Christians, ﴿do indeed consume﴾ meaning: they take, but He expressed it with this word because it is the principal aim regarding wealth, and as an indication of the belittling of the rabbis and monks, that they do what contradicts the station in which they have placed themselves, ﴿the wealth of the people by falsehood﴾ meaning: by taking it through bribes (*rushā*) and various kinds of hunting for it, by displaying asceticism and exaggerating in religiosity, which attracts it through vows and the like, so they hoard it and do not spend it in the way of God, from those who come to them with it, by the inclination of His servants' hearts toward them.

When He informed about their turning toward this world, He followed it with the report of their turning away from the Hereafter, so He said: ﴿And they bar﴾ meaning: they scheme to divert those who come to them with those wealths and others ﴿from the way of God﴾ meaning: the religion of the King to whom all command belongs, by keeping them far from it, by concealing from them the verses that point to it, out of fear for the cutting off of their worldly life through the loss of their leadership, if those people were to turn toward the truth.

Since most of them hoard those wealths, He, glorified be He, legislated on hoarding in general, so from this, by the more fitting inference (*min bāb al-awlā*), the barring was understood, which is the cause of gathering, which is the cause of hoarding. So He said: ﴿And those who﴾ meaning: who do that, while the situation is that they know that those who ﴿hoard﴾ meaning: gather under the earth or above it, from their saying of the flesh that has gathered: *muktaniz* (compact), ﴿gold and silver﴾ meaning: from among them and from others, without paying zakat.

Since it is well known that these two are the most noble of people's wealth, and hoarding indicates abundance in these two, He returned the pronoun to them in a form that indicates the many kinds, so He said: ﴿and do not spend them﴾ meaning: they do not spend what is obligatory upon them from these wealths which they gathered from these two kinds, whether combined or separate. Had He used the dual, it would have suggested that their combination is a condition for the threat, and He returned the pronoun to them without mentioning *min* ("from"), though it is intended, for the greater encouragement to spend and warning against leaving it. It is also permissible for the pronoun to refer to silver, because the blame for hoarding it and the need for it because of its abundance is less, so the blame for hoarding gold is by the more fitting inference, since it is higher and more precious than it. Unlike the blame for hoarding gold; and al-Harrālī said regarding Āl ʿImrān: He attributed spending to both of them and did not single it out, since it was not from them, and ﴿and do not spend from them﴾ as He said regarding livestock: ﴿Take from their wealth﴾ [9:103], because these two jewels are seals by which the people of the world attain their benefits, and He had turned them away from benefiting from them, so there was no use in their existence except by spending them, because they are the idols of this nation, so breaking them is by destroying them. End.

﴿in the way of God﴾ meaning: the path which the Supreme King commanded spending it upon. ﴿So give them good tidings﴾ meaning: we say concerning them, because of that, in mockery of them: give them good tidings ﴿of a painful punishment﴾ in exchange for what they wanted of joy in the success of their aims.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 35:

Since the context clearly indicates that this punishment befalls them and strikes them, He placed as its governing clause His saying: ﴿On the Day when it is heated﴾, i.e., the heating occurs, which is intense kindling (al-ihma', "heating"), ﴿upon them﴾, i.e., upon the wealth they gathered, ﴿in the fire of Hell﴾ (p-448), i.e., a fire compared to which your fire is nothing, and they will be branded within it with scowling and frowning, just as they used to greet the poor and others of the people of God with such scowls, especially those who withheld what was due to Him of expenditure. ﴿And their foreheads will be branded with it﴾, i.e., with this wealth, ﴿their foreheads﴾, which are the noblest of their limbs, because they are the gathering place of the faces and heads and the seat of status (jah) for the sake of which they gathered wealth, because they frowned with them in the faces of the poor. ﴿And their sides﴾, which they stored it to fill with desirable foods and delightful drinks, and because they turned away from the poor with them. ﴿And their backs﴾, which they stored it to strengthen and adorn with clothing and to beautify, and because they turned their backs to the poor when they gathered in one place. Then it will be said to them: ﴿This is what you hoarded for yourselves﴾, and he indicated the motive for gathering, which contradicts reason, by His saying: ﴿for yourselves﴾, i.e., so that you might vie with it and take pleasure in it, and so you did not spend it in what God commanded. ﴿So taste what﴾, i.e., the retribution and punishment of what ﴿you used to hoard﴾, i.e., you continually renewed its gathering, persistently and greedily. He indicated by the verb of being (kuntum) that they were habituated to this. Al-Bukhari related in the Tafsir from Zayd ibn Wahb who said: I passed by Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, at al-Rabadhah, and I said: "What brought you to this land?" He said: "We were in Syria, and I recited: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾ [al-Tawbah: 34] – the verse." (p-449) Mu'awiyah said: "This is not about us; this only concerns the People of the Book!" I said: "It concerns both us and them." It is also related from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "This was before zakat was revealed; when it was revealed, Allah made it a purification for wealth," meaning: whoever gives its owner what is due upon it, that wealth is not a hoard.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 36:

Since many matters dependent on the calendar have already been mentioned — the pilgrimage (Hajj) at other than its fixed place, the (sacred) months, the fulfilling of the covenant of those who have a term until its term, the zakat and the jizya — and He concluded all of that with hoarding (kanz), which in the Law is not applied except to that whose zakat has not been paid; and since the polytheists of the Arabs — those from whom disavowal (al-bara'a) was previously commanded, and about whom these verses were proclaimed on the Day of the Greater Pilgrimage (yawm al-hajj al-akbar) — had altered the years from their fixed arrangement, which Allah had set for them, by means of the intercalation (al-nasi') which they had been commanded to proclaim in the Hajj as annulled, they had imitated the practice of the People of the Book in adopting the religious custom of making lawful and unlawful according to their elders, just as those had imitated the statement of the polytheists regarding prophethood and fatherhood. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the number of months﴾, that is, the total number of months of the year, ﴿with Allah﴾, that is, in the judgment and knowledge of the One who created time alone, and He alone is God, so there is no command for anyone along with Him, ﴿is twelve months﴾, that is, there is no addition to them and no alteration of them as you do in the intercalation, ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾, that is, the speech of the King who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, and His judgment, which is the gathering of guidance; so it is the most worthy that it be written, (p-450) and the months are not thirteen nor more, as was done by those whom I commanded you to disavow, whoever they were, in the intercalation, ﴿on the day﴾, that is, that was and took place on the day ﴿He created the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, the two from which time arose.

The meaning is that the ruling on this was before He created time. ﴿Of them﴾, that is, of the months, ﴿four are sacred﴾, that is, by their specific identity and not merely by number. ﴿That﴾, that is, the great matter and the judgment of high rank in soundness specifically, ﴿is the upright religion﴾, that is, that in which there is no crookedness and no place for the servants; rather it is by the decree of Allah, exalted is He, regarding the moon. Al-Bukhari narrated from Abu Bakra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said — meaning at the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Indeed time has returned to its form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred: three consecutive — Dhu al-Qa'da, Dhu al-Hijja and al-Muharram — and Rajab of Mudar, which lies between Jumada and Sha'ban." When He had explained the matter, He based on it His saying: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, that is, in the sacred months, ﴿yourselves﴾, that is, by means of postponing some of them and making others sacred in its place so that you may match the number — not the specific months — which necessarily results in each of them being violated by committing injustice in it and by making sacred the others. Qatada said: good deeds and bad deeds in them are greater than in other than them, although that is in itself great; but Allah, exalted is He, because of the greatness of the One who commanded it, does what He wills. Abu Hayyan said, in summary: the Arabs refer the pronoun to a plural of multitude as to a feminine singular, which is why He said ﴿of them (p-451) four﴾, that is, of the months; and to a plural of paucity for non-rational things with the feminine plural ending, which is why He said ﴿so do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, that is, in the four.

Since their postponing was in order to make fighting lawful for them according to their claim, He said: ﴿And fight the polytheists all together﴾, that is, all of you are equal in that, in unity and in the gathering of the word; ﴿as they fight you all together﴾, that is, all of them are equal in that. That ruling applies throughout the whole year; I do not forbid you from fighting them in one of its months, so you have no need to change My ruling concerning it for fighting or otherwise, if you fear Allah. So do not fear them, even if their numbers increase and their strength multiplies, for Allah will be with you. ﴿And know that Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom belongs all greatness, is with you — this was the original form, but He made the attribute manifest in order to attach the ruling to it and to generalize it, so He said: ﴿is with the God-fearing﴾, all of them, and they are those who keep their piety upon what He has prescribed for them, not upon the postponing or the like; and whoever Allah is with is certainly victorious.

[p. 452] When it was understood from this that the postponement (al-nasi') is nullified, since it is an act of the people of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic era), and that there is no piety in it, it was as if it were said: "Is there then no piety in the postponement? For its cause is only fear of violating the sanctity of Allah by fighting in the month He made sacred." This is because they were people of raids and wars, yet they respected the sacred months (al-ashhur al-hurum) from fighting, to the extent that if a person saw the slayer of his father with no obstacle to him, he would not confront him. So when a sacred month came while they were at war, it was hard for them to abandon fighting, and it was hard for them to abandon that for three consecutive months. So they made the postponement for this purpose. Then it was stated explicitly what the preceding had implied, namely that none of that is in it: ﴿Indeed, the postponement﴾, meaning: postponing a month to another month. It is either the verbal noun of "nasa'a, yansa'u, nasi'an," meaning he postponed it, or it is a passive participle, meaning: the month whose sanctity the Arabs postpone from among the sacred months away from its time. ﴿is an increase in disbelief﴾, meaning: because it opposes what Allah legislated, and in it is concealment of the prohibition that Allah made manifest.

When he clarified the ugliness that is in the postponement, it became clear that they had fallen into the opposite of their intention. For if they had fought in the sacred month, they would have fought while believing in its sanctity and fearing its consequences, so they would not have been entirely outside the circle of piety. But now, by making it lawful, they have gone far outside its circle, because they commit in it every grave matter while feeling secure, due to their belief in its lawfulness through the permission of what they believed to be unlawful. Thus he (the one who made the postponement) would say: "I am not questioned, nor am I blamed, and there is no repelling of my decree, and I have made the forbidden lawful and forbidden Safar," and other such speech that befits none but God. That is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, explaining what precedes it: ﴿by which those who disbelieved are led astray﴾, meaning: by this postponement, which is the nasi', there results for them a going astray from what Allah legislated. [p. 453] This is according to the reading of the majority. The meaning according to the reading of Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs, with the passive form, is: a misleader from Allah leads them astray. According to the reading of Ya'qub, with a damma: Allah leads them astray. Then He explained their going astray by His saying: ﴿they make it lawful﴾, meaning: that month. He expressed the year with a word that revolves around the meaning of abundance, indicating that they do it even if no drought year or harsh time compels them to it, but merely by whim. So He said: ﴿one year, and they make it unlawful another year﴾, thus always, whenever they wished. It is not meant that every year they do that without regard for any year among the years. This act was abrogated among them, even though they regard abrogation as a defect in religion. ﴿So that they may conform﴾, meaning: that they may agree, ﴿to the number of what Allah has made unlawful﴾, meaning: the number that encompasses majesty and honour, in the fact that the sacred months are four, ﴿and so make lawful﴾, meaning: this act results in their making lawful ﴿what Allah has made unlawful﴾, meaning: the Sovereign, the Greatest of all of them. So this act leaves them no month without violating its sanctity. They wanted by this to avoid violating the sanctity, but instead they did not leave any sanctity without violating it. How far is this from error!

When the ugliness of their act was exposed by this explanation, it was as if it were said: "Indeed this is strange! What led them to that?" So it was said: ﴿Made fair-seeming﴾, meaning: a beautifier beautified it. It was read as an anomalous reading with the verb attributed to Allah. ﴿To them is the evil of their deeds﴾, meaning: until they saw as good what is not good, so they went astray and were not guided. Allah did that to them because He knew their nature's inclination to disbelief, so He did not guide them. ﴿And Allah﴾, meaning: the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿does not guide﴾, meaning: does not create guidance in hearts, ﴿the disbelieving people﴾, meaning: [p. 454] the One who imprinted on them disbelief, so they are deeply immersed in it and never depart from it.

As for al-nasi', said al-Fayruzabadi in al-Qamus: it is the noun from "nasa'a al-shay'," meaning he drove it, pushed it, and delayed it. He said: and a month that the Arabs used to postpone in the Jahiliyyah, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade it. Ibn al-Athir said in al-Nihayah: al-nasi' is fa'ul in the sense of maf'ul. Ibn Faris said in al-Mujmal: al-nasi' in the Book of Allah is postponement, and when they departed from Mina, a man from Kinanah would stand and say: "I am the one whose decree is not repelled!" They would say: "Postpone for us a month," meaning: delay from us the sanctity of the sacred month and place it in Safar. End.

The root n-s-'' revolves around displacement. The cause of this act was that they would sometimes wish to fight in a sacred month, so they would make it lawful, and make in its place a month from the months of permissibility sacred, and postpone that month. Ibn Faris said: That is because they disliked that three months should pass consecutively in which they could not raid, since their livelihood was from raiding; so the Kinanite would make the sacred month lawful for them. End.

The nasa'ah (those who postponed) were from Banu Fuqaym of Kinanah. The first of them to do that was al-Qalammas, who was Hudhayfah ibn 'Abd ibn Fuqaym, and the last of them, under whom Islam came, was Abu Thumamah Junadah ibn 'Awf ibn Umayyah ibn Qal' ibn 'Abbad ibn Hudhayfah ibn 'Abd ibn Fuqaym ibn 'Adi ibn 'Amir ibn Tha'labah ibn al-Harith ibn Malik ibn Kinanah ibn Khuzaymah. He postponed for forty years. When the Arabs finished their pilgrimage they would gather to him, and he would make the four sacred months sacred. When they wished to make lawful one of them, he would make the sacred month lawful, and they made it lawful, and he would make Safar sacred in its place, and they made it sacred, so as to conform to the number of the four sacred months. When they wished to depart, he would stand among them and say: "O Allah, I have made lawful for them one of the two Safars, the first Safar, and postponed the other for the coming year." The people of the biographies (ahl al-siyar) mentioned this. From Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, it is reported that the first to postpone was 'Amr ibn Luhayy.

As for the investigation of the meaning of what the Arabs used to do with it, and the variation of the names of the months by it, so that it causes the years to turn, so that the names of the months do not coincide with what they name except from time to time, is difficult. Few have addressed it in a manner that clarifies the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Farewell Pilgrimage, as has passed: "Indeed time has turned back to its form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth." Here I mention what leaves no ambiguity after it, God willing. The meaning of his saying "and I postponed the other for the coming year" is that when he made the sacred month lawful and named it Safar, he began the year after it with Muharram, then Safar, to its end, so between Safar and Dhu al-Hijjah, in which the postponement occurred, there are two months, whereas there should have been one month between them. So he postponed this which should have been [in its place] to the coming year. So the meaning is: "I have postponed the second Safar from its place to the coming year," so when the coming year comes, its postponement ends, and when it ends, it returns to its place. It may be that Abu 'Ubayd's words in Gharib al-Hadith fit this, [p. 456] he said after the middle of the third part of it, in explaining the "turning" (al-istidarah): "The beginning of that, and Allah knows best, is that the Arabs used to make the four months sacred, and this was among what they held to from the religion of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. So they sometimes needed to make the sacred month lawful for war that was between them, so they disliked to make it lawful, and disliked delaying their war, so they postponed the sanctity of the sacred month to Safar, making Safar sacred and making the sacred month lawful. This is the nasi' about which Allah said: ﴿Indeed, the postponement...﴾ the verse. This was among Kinanah, who were the ones who postponed the months upon the Arabs, and the nasi' is the postponement. They would remain for a time making Safar sacred while they meant by it the sacred month, and they would say: 'It is one of the two Safars.' Some people interpreted the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying 'There is no Safar' in this light. Then they also needed to postpone Safar to the month after it, just as they needed to postpone the sacred month, so they postponed its sanctity to Rabi', then they remained with that as long as Allah willed, then they needed the same again, and so on. Thus one month pushes another until the sanctity turned around the whole year." Then Islam came, and the sacred month had returned to its place where Allah had set it, and that was after a long era. This is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed time has turned back to its form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth." He means: the sacred months returned to their place, and the nasi' ended. Some people claimed that they used to make the sacred month lawful for one year, and when the next year came they returned it to its sanctity. [p. 457] Abu 'Ubayd said: "The first is more beloved to me because of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying 'Time has turned back,' and there is no turning in the last interpretation." According to this interpretation which we have explained, His saying ﴿they make it lawful one year and make it unlawful another year﴾ may confirm it, for when they made sacred the sacred month in one year and Safar in the next, then after that needed to make Safar lawful as well, they made it lawful and made sacred the one after it. This is the explanation of His saying in the commentary: "they make it lawful one year and make it unlawful another year."

Abu Hayyan said in al-Nahr, the essence of which is: The Arabs, most of whom had no livelihood except from raids, found it hard to have the sacred months follow one another. The Banu Fuqaym were a people of religion and adherence to the law of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, so al-Qalammas, who was Hudhayfah ibn 'Ubayd ibn Fuqaym, took it upon himself, and postponed the months for the Arabs. Then his successor in this was his son 'Abbad, then his son Qal', then his son Umayyah, then his son 'Awf, then his son Junadah ibn 'Awf, and under him Islam came. When they finished their pilgrimage, whoever wished of them would come to him, gathered, and they said: "Postpone for us a month," so he would make the sacred month lawful, then they would keep the sanctity of Safar to conform to the number of the four months, and they would call that Safar "the sacred," and they would call the first Rabi' "Safar" and the second Rabi' "the first Rabi'," and so on with the other months. Thus the ruling of the sacred month that had been made lawful for them falls away, and the year comes to thirteen months, the first of which is Muharram, which is in reality Safar.

Al-Baghawi said: Mujahid said: They used to make pilgrimage in every month two years. [p. 458] So they made pilgrimage in Dhu al-Hijjah two years, and made pilgrimage in Muharram two years, then they made pilgrimage in Safar two years, and so on for the months. So the pilgrimage of Abu Bakr coincided with the second year in Dhu al-Qa'dah. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) made pilgrimage the following year, the Farewell Pilgrimage, and his pilgrimage coincided with the months of the legislated pilgrimage, which is Dhu al-Hijjah.

'Abd al-Razzaq said in his tafsir: Ma'mar informed us from Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief﴾. He said: Allah made obligatory the pilgrimage in Dhu al-Hijjah, but the polytheists would name the months: Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, Rabi' [one], Rabi' [two], Jumada [one], Jumada [two], Rajab, Sha'ban, Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah and Dhu al-Hijjah. Then they would make pilgrimage in it once more, then they would be silent about Muharram and not mention it, so they would name it, I think he said, "Muharram Safar." Then they would name Rajab "Jumada al-Akhirah," then they would name Sha'ban "Ramadan," and Ramadan "Shawwal."

Then they would call Dhu al-Qa'dah "Shawwal." Then they would call Dhu al-Hijjah "Dhu al-Qa'dah," then they would call al-Muharram "Dhu al-Hijjah" and perform the Hajj in it, and its name among them was Dhu al-Hijjah. Then they returned to a similar state, and they would perform the Hajj two years in every month, until the Hajj of Abu Bakr coincided, in the second of the two years, with Dhu al-Qa'dah. Then the Prophet ﷺ performed the Hajj he performed, and that coincided (p-459) with Dhu al-Hijjah. Therefore the Prophet ﷺ said in his sermon: "Indeed, time has turned around to its original state on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth." Ibn Ishaq said in the Sirah: I asked Ibn Abi Najih about the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: The Quraysh used to intercalate a month every year, and they would only coincide with Dhu al-Hijjah once every twelve years. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, granted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ success in the Hajj he performed, that it fell in Dhu al-Hijjah, and he performed it in that month. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, time has turned around to its original state on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth." I said to Ibn Abi Najih: Then what about the Hajj of Abu Bakr and Attab ibn Asid? He said: It was according to the way the people used to perform the Hajj. Then Ibn Abi Najih said: They would perform the Hajj in Dhu al-Hijjah, then the following year in al-Muharram, then Safar, until they reached twelve months. End.

His statement "this" gives the impression that there was disorder in the Hajj of Abu Bakr and Attab, may Allah be pleased with them both. It has already been stated, from al-Mahdawi and others, explicitly, that it was in Dhu al-Qa'dah. But this is open to scrutiny, because in the year in which Abu Bakr performed the Hajj, the proclamation was made regarding the prohibition of the nasi' and other matters of the Jahiliyyah. There is no doubt that in that year there was no intercalation, and ten months had passed of the month in which he performed the Hajj, and the eleventh was Dhu al-Qa'dah. The Prophet ﷺ set out at its end for the Hajj, arriving at the crescent of (p-460) Dhu al-Hijjah. When he stood at Arafat, he announced that time had turned around. Thus it is known with certainty that this turning around occurred in the Hajj of Abu Bakr. Likewise in the year eight, which is the year in which Attab led the Muslims in the Hajj. This is because the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, did not follow the reckoning of the people of Jahiliyyah, neither their intercalation nor anything other than their intercalation. For saying that they followed the matter of intercalation entails that they followed what is an increase in disbelief, and no one of sound mind says this. It has already been transmitted that the Prophet ﷺ sent Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, to perform the Hajj at the end of Dhu al-Qa'dah or after its conclusion in the year nine, and the Arabs, both disbelievers and others, met him in Dhu al-Hijjah. So the announcement of the bara'ah (disavowal) occurred on the days and places of the Hajj. Had there been disorder in Dhu al-Qa'dah through intercalation in the year of Attab, then Dhu al-Hijjah by the disbelievers' reckoning would have been al-Muharram by the Islamic reckoning, and the disbelievers' arrival for the Hajj would have been later than the arrival of the Muslims. Thus it is established by this as well that his Hajj, may Allah be pleased with him, was in Dhu al-Hijjah. Allah protected the people of Islam from any disorder occurring in their Hajj in any year of the years, and this is not the first of His blessings upon them. And Allah is the Granter of success.

Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Abi Ahmad, known as Ibn al-Qass, one of the great early scholars of the companions of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book Dala'il al-Qiblah, in the chapter on knowing the number of days of the year: The year is twelve months by the crescents, and sometimes a month is thirty days and sometimes twenty-nine. The total of the lunar year is three hundred and fifty-four days, eight hours, and four-fifths of an hour. The Indians said: the year is three hundred and sixty-five days, six hours, a fifth of an hour, and a portion of one four-hundredth of an hour, this being from the entry of the sun into the head of Aries until it enters it again the following year. So the difference between the lunar year and the solar year is ten days and twenty-one hours and two-fifths of an hour. When these hours and days are added to it, its reckoning agrees with the revolution of the sun. The Arabs used to add to it in the Jahiliyyah, and the one who innovated this for them was a man from Kinanah called al-Qalammas. He would gather this surplus, and when it completed a month he would add it to the year, making that year thirteen months, and he called it nasi', and he would lead them in the Hajj in that year in al-Muharram. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief﴾. "When the year in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the Farewell Hajj came, the Hajj coincided in that year with Dhu al-Hijjah, by what Allah, the Exalted, willed in establishing the Hajj in that year. So the Prophet ﷺ delivered a sermon and said:
"O people! Indeed, the year has turned around to its original state on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. ﴿Of them four are sacred; that is the upright religion﴾ [al-Tawbah: 36]." He meant by it the upright reckoning. The sacred months are Rajab, Jumada, Sha'ban, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram, and that Hajj was called "the most upright Hajj." A poet said:
"Dhu al-'Arsh abolished the nasi' and al-Qalammas, and the Messenger of Allah succeeded with the most upright Hajj."
End.

Al-Qalammas is pronounced with a fathah on the lam and a shaddah on the mim. The nasi' in the verse is written without the hamzah (p-462) so that the meter is sound, and al-Aqwam has its hamzah's vowel transferred. His statement that the reason for the nasi' was harmonizing the solar and lunar years is open to scrutiny. The apparent reason is what is mentioned in the biographies, namely their being compelled to fight. The matter of "turning around" in each of these statements is clearly evident. The intended meaning is not that every season of the year coincides with its place of heat and cold, or that the name of each month coincides with what it names according to its derivation, so that Ramadan, for example, falls in extreme heat, and likewise others, even though in fact the matter was so in that Hajj, since it has preceded that the expedition of Tabuk began in the month of Rajab, and that was, as has preceded, in extreme heat and at the time when the fruits had ripened. Rather, the principal meaning of the turning around is that the name of each month coincides with what it names, not with the name of another month, for the sake of the cycling caused by the nasi', as is evidenced by the fact that he ﷺ only mentioned it for that reason. He said in some transmissions of the lengthy hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him: "Indeed, the nasi' is an increase in disbelief, and indeed time has turned around to its original state on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months." Observe how he followed this with restricting the months to twelve, negating their making it a year of thirteen months through the nasi'. He said: "Of them four are sacred," and specified them, and said: "What month is this?" When they were silent, he said: "Dhu al-Hijjah is a sacred month." All of this is to clarify that the intended meaning of the turning around is the return of each month from what the people of Jahiliyyah had altered to its proper place, which Allah set for it, its name matching what it names. Our months were made lunar, with the prohibition of the nasi', so that the turning around would occur, and by it every act of worship we are bound to would occur in every season of the year, unlike their months by reckoning, for their acts of worship were specific to a time of the year that they did not exceed. And Allah is the One who grants accord to it.

Al-Qadi Abu Muhammad Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Bustiyy said in his tafsir: Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, who said: The month which Allah removed from the Shaytan is al-Muharram.

The conclusion is that there is no doubt that the nasi' never occurred except in al-Muharram, for what has preceded, and that the Hajj never occurred, in Jahiliyyah or in Islam, except in a month called Dhu al-Hijjah, according to what the transmitters of language, hadith, and reports have said. Ibn al-Athir said in al-Nihayah, Nashwan al-Yamani in Shams al-'Ulum, al-Qazzaz in his Diwan, and Ibn Makturn in Tartib al-'Ubab and al-Muhkam: Dhu al-Hijjah, with a kasrah, is the month of the Hajj. al-Muhkam added: it was named so for the Hajj. al-Qazzaz said: the fathah in it is more common. In al-Nihayah: the Day of Tarwiyah is the eighth of Dhu al-Hijjah, named so because they would draw water (tarawwa) from it for what follows, i.e., they would draw water and give water to drink. Al-Majd said in al-Qamus: the Day of Arafat is the ninth of Dhu al-Hijjah. (p-464) In the book Aswaq al-'Arab by Abu al-Mundhir Hisham ibn Muhammad al-Kalbi, in the narration of Abu Sa'id al-Sukkari, it is mentioned that 'Ukaz was among the greatest markets of the Arabs. When its people saw the crescent of Dhu al-Hijjah, they would all set out for Dhu al-Majaz, which is near 'Ukaz, and 'Ukaz is in the upper part of Najd, and they would stay there until the Tarwiyah. The Hajj pilgrims of the Arabs and their leaders who intended the Hajj, along with those who had not attended those markets, would meet them in Mecca. al-Azraqi said in the History of Mecca: When they saw the crescent of Dhu al-Hijjah, they would move to Dhu al-Majaz and stay there eight nights while their markets were in operation. Then on the Day of Tarwiyah they would go out from Dhu al-Majaz to Arafat, and they would draw water on that day at Dhu al-Majaz. The day was named Tarwiyah because of their drawing water at Dhu al-Majaz; they would call out to one another: "Draw water! There is no water at Arafat or at Muzdalifah on that day." He then mentioned that only merchants attended that, and said: Whoever had no trade would leave his household whenever he wished, and whoever was from the people of Mecca and did not intend trade would leave Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah with his chain, from 'Urwah and Musa ibn 'Uqbah, separately, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered into ihram for the 'umrah from al-Ji'ranah in Dhu al-Qa'dah." Then he transmitted from Ibn Ishaq that he said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his 'umrah, he returned (p-465) to Medina, and he appointed Attab ibn Asid over Mecca, and left with him Mu'adh ibn Jabal to instruct the people in the religion and teach them. The 'umrah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Dhu al-Qa'dah or in al-Hijjah, and the people performed the Hajj that year as the Arabs used to perform it, and Attab ibn Asid performed the Hajj that year, the year eight." The hadith of his ﷺ performing 'umrah in Dhu al-Qa'dah was transmitted by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), and it continued according to what the Arabs did regarding circumambulating naked and the like. Al-Waqidi mentioned it from shaykhs who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached al-Ji'ranah on the night of Thursday, five nights having passed of Dhu al-Qa'dah. He stayed at al-Ji'ranah for thirteen nights. When he wished to return to Medina, he left al-Ji'ranah on the night of Wednesday, twelve nights remaining of Dhu al-Qa'dah, and he entered into ihram." He then mentioned his 'umrah, and then said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Attab ibn Asid over Mecca, and left Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with them both, teaching the people the Qur'an and jurisprudence in the religion. Attab ibn Asid, may Allah be pleased with him, led the people in the Hajj that year, which was the year eight, and some Muslims and polytheists performed the Hajj according to their period. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered Medina on Friday, three nights remaining of Dhu al-Qa'dah. Al-Waqidi said: He remained the rest of Dhu al-Qa'dah and Dhu al-Hijjah, and when he saw the crescent of al-Muharram, he sent out the collectors of charity." End.

[p. 466]

Having established this, it is known that the Hajj was never held except in the month they call Dhu al-Hijjah. This is something that does not occur to the mind nor enter the imagination with any doubt, and it needs no lengthy mention or elaboration. Sometimes its name corresponds to what it designates, and sometimes it does not, because of the *nasi'* (the intercalation of months, a pre-Islamic practice of postponing or advancing sacred months).

It is also known that the Hajj of 'Attab ibn Asid took place in Dhu al-Hijjah after the Prophet ﷺ returned from al-Ji'ranah to the blessed city of Madinah. Thus it was not delayed beyond Dhu al-Hijjah except through a transmitted report. And the Hajj of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, in the year nine was in Dhu al-Hijjah for that same reason. This is also consistent with what has preceded: that his departure from the blessed city of Madinah was at the end of Dhu al-Qa'dah or the beginning of Dhu al-Hijjah. It is also consistent with their statement that the four months granted to the polytheists were counted from the Day of Sacrifice (*yawm al-nahr*), and with their statement that the last of the four months was the tenth of Rabi' al-Akhir.

It is known that if that year's Dhu al-Hijjah had coincided with the designation of Dhu al-Qa'dah, then Dhu al-Hijjah in the year ten, in which the Prophet ﷺ performed the Hajj, would not have fallen in its proper place which Allah set for it, except if that year had been thirteen months, through *nasi'* or something else. Both of these are invalid. As for the first, Allah the Exalted nullified the *nasi'* in that year, among the pre-Islamic practices He nullified in this surah, and the Prophet ﷺ sent out the proclamation of this, as has passed. As for the second, it is an extraordinary matter that breaks the normal course of things, and nothing like it had occurred since Allah created the heavens and the earth. What breaks the normal course is among the things whose transmission is strongly motivated, yet there is no transmitter of this at all. Therefore it is invalid. When it is invalid, it is established that the year ten consisted of twelve months, [p. 467] especially after Allah revealed in this matter what He revealed in this surah. When the matter is thus, the month in which the Prophet ﷺ stood at Arafat is in the same position as the month in which the Siddiq (Abu Bakr), may Allah be pleased with him, stood, exactly alike. It has been established without any doubt that the time had completed its cycle to its form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth, so it is established beyond dispute that the month of the Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, was likewise. It is also established that the year of 'Attab ibn Asid, may Allah be pleased with him, was likewise, for what I have mentioned: there was no *nasi'* in it, because the Hajj of the Muslims and the polytheists coincided in the year nine.

This indicates that it [the year] consisted of twelve months, so Dhu al-Hijjah in it was in the place which Allah set for it, just as it was in the year nine. Indeed, the apparent meaning of Abu 'Ubayd's words, "Then Islam stood, and Muharram had returned to its place, as has passed," is that Allah preserved the entire era of Islam from *nasi'*. This is what I believe. And it has become clear from this that the reason for the saying of whoever said that the Hajj of the Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, coincided with Dhu al-Qa'dah, is that he understood from the Prophet's ﷺ saying, "The time has indeed completed its cycle," that the cycle occurred only in that year. But that is not the implication of this wording, as is not hidden. And Allah is the Granter of success.

Then I found the explicit transmission in the additions (*zawa'id*) of the two lexicons of al-Tabarani, al-Awsat and al-Asghar, by the memorizer Nur al-Din al-Haythami, in accordance with what I understood. In the tafsir of Surat Bara'ah (al-Tawbah), he said: Ibrahim, meaning Ibn Hisham al-Baghawi, related to us: al-Salt ibn Mas'ud al-Jahdari related to us: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Tufawi related to us: Dawud ibn Abi Hind related to us, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, meaning [p. 468] 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Arabs used to make a month lawful one year and two months the next year, and they would not hit the Hajj except once every twenty-six years. This is the *nasi'* which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in His Book. When the year came in which Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, led the people in Hajj, that year coincided with the Hajj, and Allah named it the Greater Hajj. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the Hajj in the following year, and the people faced the new moons. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'The time has indeed completed its cycle to its form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth.'" Only Dawud related this from 'Amr, and al-Salt is the sole narrator of it. End of quotation. It is a good hadith, Allah willing. Then I saw al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id say: "Its narrators are trustworthy," which confirmed the certainty that I understood, that it is good. I have only prolonged this discussion, though its clarification may not require it, because of the abundance of disputants who are obstinate, and the futile arguments of rigid contenders.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 38:

When He, glory be to Him, had urged them to jihad, removed all their excuses, and made clear that its excellence is not restricted to one month rather than another, and that some of them used to make lawful for themselves and make unlawful (a practice called *nasi'* (intercalation of the sacred months)), so that they would follow it by making the lawful month unlawful and the unlawful month lawful through fighting in it, God, glory be to Him, rebuked them for staying behind from the Messenger of God ﷺ, who was commanding them to march out for the expedition of Tabuk by His command. Its beginning was in the month of Rajab in the ninth year. So He, exalted is He, said, by way of appeal and reminder of the blessing of faith (p-469), after concluding the previous verse with the statement that He does not guide the disbelievers, a statement that covers war and other matters and that necessitates boldness against them [because whoever has no guidance is blind, and the blind do not fear]:

﴿O you who have believed﴾, that is, those who claim that. ﴿What is [the matter] with you﴾, that is, what is it that happens to you that ﴿when it is said to you﴾, that is, by whichever speaker it is said, ﴿March forth﴾, that is, go out swiftly, with earnestness and vigor, in groups or individually, to support the party of God and to aid His religion, confirming your claim of faith. And *al-nafr* (marching forth) is leaving one place for another for a matter that has arisen. ﴿In the way of God﴾, that is, for the sake of facilitating the path to the King who possesses all the attributes of perfection.

Abu Hayyan said: He made *qila* (it was said) passive, while the speaker is the Prophet ﷺ, and He did not mention him, out of severity and roughness toward them, and to preserve his mention, since whoever inclined to ease and comfort and opposed his command had earned that. End of quote.

﴿You became heavy﴾, that is, you became very heavy, and in it [the doubling of the letter in *ithaqaltum*, which is the assimilation (*idgham*) of two similar consonants] there is an indication of what they did not state as an apparent cause, namely inclination and leaning, ﴿to the earth﴾, that is, toward the coolness of its shade, the pleasantness of its air, and the ripeness of its fruits. Thus you became earthly in the lowliness of your aspirations, not heavenly through the purity of your dispositions.

Since, among the causes mentioned earlier that were said to incline them to slacken in jihad, there was nothing that could bear them up for this expedition except fear of being killed and inclination toward present wealth, trusting in it and turning away from the promised wealth (p-470), which turning away from it may lead to denial, which in turn leads to the loss of the Hereafter. Along with this, there necessarily follows, without doubt, renunciation of the reward that yields the happiness of the final abode for this base thing. He said, explaining the baseness of what they inclined to, to discourage them from it, and the nobility of what they turned away from, to encourage them toward it, alerting that abandoning great good for the sake of small evil is a great evil, and denouncing those who were heavy, rebuking them:

﴿Are you content with the life of this world﴾, that is, with ease and comfort in this lowly, deceiving abode, ﴿instead of the Hereafter﴾, that is, the exalted and everlasting one. Abu Hayyan said: The opinions of the commentators agree that *min* here means "instead of" (*badal*, substitution), but our companions do not affirm that *min* can mean substitution. End of quote.

What appears to me is that they did not mean that it is established for substitution, but rather that it is applied to it because of what it may entail in such a phrase, namely leaving what follows for what precedes. For *min* indicates the starting point of a limit (*ibtida' al-ghaya*). So when you say, "I am content with such-and-such from Zayd," the meaning is that you took that thing starting from him, not turning to anything else. It is as if you made that a substitute for everything else that you might expect to receive from him besides what you took.

Since they had been given the Hereafter on condition of obedience, and they exchanged it for refusal, their turning toward this world was as if it began from what they had already prepared for themselves of the Hereafter while turning away from it. So it is as if it were said: "Are you content with inclining toward this world instead of the Hereafter?" What I have understood is supported by the fact that the scholar, the authority Alam al-Din Abu Muhammad al-Qasim ibn al-Muwaffaq al-Andalusi, mentioned in his commentary on *al-Jazuliyya* (p-471) that they counted five meanings for *min*, all of which return to the starting point of a limit according to the verifiers (*al-muhaqqiqun*), and he explained how this applies even to the explanatory (*bayaniyya*) use. So the meaning of ﴿So shun the abomination of the idols﴾ [al-Hajj: 30] is that its starting point is the idols, because the abomination includes the idols and other things.

Since the interrogative was a rebuke, its meaning was a prohibition, so the implied sense is: Do not be content with it, for that is the most foolish and corrupt opinion! Then He, exalted is He, said, giving the reason for this prohibition: ﴿Then the enjoyment of the life of this world is, in comparison with the Hereafter, but little﴾, that is, it is submerged in the face of the Hereafter. And whoever seeks profit in a trade, claims insight into it, and is wary of defects in it, is considered by such conduct to be wise, whereas whoever does the opposite is considered foolish.

When prolonged entreaty might lead to dispute and the abandonment of fairness, He threatened them with His saying: ﴿Unless you go forth﴾, i.e., in His cause, ﴿He will punish you﴾, i.e., for that, ﴿with a painful punishment﴾, i.e., in both abodes. ﴿And He will replace you﴾, i.e., bring in, in your place, ﴿a people other than you﴾, i.e., possessing valour and courage, differing from you in the qualities that were the cause of the replacement, for His support and the victory of His religion.

When He threatened them with what would harm them, He informed them that by their lethargy they harm no one but themselves, so He said: ﴿And you will not harm Him﴾, i.e., Allah and His Messenger, ﴿at all﴾, because He completes His command, fulfils His promise, and makes His religion prevail. When He thereby established His power over harming them and their inability to reach harm to Him, the implied meaning is: because He is able to support His religion and His Prophet with others than you. Then He joined to it, generalising His power and instilling dread of His great might, the saying: ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent﴾, i.e., the King who has complete encompassing power. (p-٤٧٢)

(p. 473) When He, glory be to Him, described His Most Holy Self with what befits Him of all-encompassing power and great might and strength, He followed this with a proof which implies that the one who calls them to march forth, namely His Prophet (ﷺ), does not need them, and that his victory does not depend on them, just as He did not need them, by the protection of the All-Powerful over him, in the past separation that He mentioned. It also implies that the benefit of this lies only for them, through gaining what they were promised and warding off what they were threatened with, in both abodes. All of this is indicated by His saying: ﴿What is the enjoyment of worldly life compared to the Hereafter?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 38], and the verse, and His saying: ﴿If you do not go forth﴾ [al-Tawbah: 39], and the verse. Then He said: ﴿If you do not support him﴾, meaning: you, in obedience to the command of Allah. The pronoun refers to the Prophet (ﷺ), either by way of istikhdam (a rhetorical device in which a single expression carries two referents) from "the way of Allah," because he is the one who makes clear the call to it, or because his noble name has been mentioned earlier implicitly in His saying: ﴿When it is said to you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 38], meaning: from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), seeking your support, and it is mentioned explicitly in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger﴾ [al-Tawbah: 33], and the verse. The strength of the relevance in each sentence, which requires that it embrace the one after it and not be separated from it, is the shortness of the separation between the noun and its pronoun. And the mention of the one who goes forth to war and the companion clarified the matter. This is because when He, glory be to Him, blamed them for taking leaders as lords, there was a strong need to explain that they were, in their distance from that, at a degree that is not hidden from one who reflects. So He described them with eating, which implies physicality, which implies need, and with their consuming the wealth of others falsely, and with their deceiving them in order to turn them away from the path, whose goodness is not hidden from anyone who has the least reflection. And since this was highly stimulating to the souls' eagerness to ask about the Arabs, whether they had done the same and followed their practice, He answered that their action in postponing the sacred months for them, by making some of the sacred months lawful and forbidding some of the lawful months, and adding to the number of months of the year, is like their action, the same.

When He commanded fighting the polytheists all together and urged them to piety, and some of them had been lax in that, the situation strongly called for reproach for being sluggish about going forth. So when this was completed in this wondrous style and lofty excellence, He urged support for the Messenger whom He had sent to make him prevail over all religion. He said, as the answer to the condition: ﴿Then [Allah has already supported him]﴾. That is: if support from you for him does not occur anew, then Allah is capable of supporting him, and He will support him and make him independent of you, and you will harm none but yourselves. So ﴿Allah has already supported him﴾, meaning: the Supreme King alone, and the matter was in the utmost severity, and there is no doubt for any sensible person that the future is with Him like the past. ﴿When﴾, meaning: at the time when ﴿those who disbelieved drove him out﴾. He expressed it in the past tense because among them were some who became Muslims after that. ﴿Those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: from Makkah, while they were in the utmost unity against him, when they consulted about killing him, or expelling him, or confining him.
