So that became the cause of Allah's permission for him to leave from among them, while he was ﴿the second of two﴾, meaning: one of them was Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), and there was no third for them, whom no one would help except Allah ﴿when they were in the cave﴾ (p. 474), meaning: the Cave of Thawr, which is at the top of the mountain facing the Yemeni Corner, at the lower part of Makkah, at a distance of an hour's walk from it, when they hid there for three nights so that pursuit would cease from them. This was before they reached you or relied for victory upon you. ﴿When he said﴾, meaning: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿to his companion﴾, meaning: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), out of trust in his Lord, not being disturbed by anything: ﴿Do not grieve﴾. Al-huzn (grief) is a thick concern accompanied by pain that softens the heart; hazana and ahzana have the same meaning. The Qamus says: "or ahzanahu: made him grieved, and hazanahu: put grief into him." Then he gave the reason for his prohibition to his companion by saying, expressing it with the Greatest Name, bringing to mind all the Most Beautiful Names and Sublime Attributes that He comprises, before which the hard necks submit and by whose majesty the lofty firm mountains crumble: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with us﴾, meaning: He to whom belongs all the command, ﴿with us﴾, meaning: by help and support. He suffices for every concern and is powerful to repel every affliction. The One who took on His support by protection at that time was capable of commanding the armies with which He strengthened him to destroy the disbelievers in every place, without this giving you any role in that or any reward for you through it. And just as He existed at that time with His Most Beautiful Names and Sublime Attributes, He is the same in this time and in every time. Thus it becomes clear, as the sun is clear, that the benefit in this is specifically for you, and that He, glory be to Him, arranged all of this in this manner only for your success. In this verse there is an indication of the high station of al-Siddiq, his precedence, his being foremost in Islam, the elevation of his rank, and the magnitude of his affair, which none knows except the One who granted it to him. Abu Hayyan and others said: The scholars said: whoever denies the companionship of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) has disbelieved, because he denies the speech of Allah. This is not the case for the rest of the Companions.

Since he (may Allah be pleased with him) had penetrating insight into the divine knowledge and was firmly rooted in that station, he did not stammer from the outset in opposing all the servants by renouncing the rivals. Then he trained in it, progressing for thirteen years. What troubled him was only the fear that harm would come to the Prophet (ﷺ), so that grief over that would overcome him, destroying him before he could rejoice in the victory of the religion and the suppression of the transgressors. He was neither ignorant nor had an ill opinion. Since this was so, he (may Allah be pleased with him) was deserving of tranquility coming to him upon hearing the noble and greatest name, which indicates that station and reminds one of that majesty before which every great thing vanishes and every large thing becomes small. For this reason this greatest name was mentioned and placed first, and he associated al-Siddiq in the companionship, and began with the prohibition against grief, because it is the thing intended in itself, and what follows it is its cause. As for the Children of Israel, they had no knowledge except what they witnessed of His, exalted is He, kindness toward Musa (peace be upon him), by the manifestation of those signs through his hand, until He rescued them by them from what they were in, and protected Musa (peace be upon him), despite his being alone, from the assaults of Pharaoh despite his greatness and what he would confront him with of hardship. So when they saw his armies approaching, their condition called for asking about that benefactor who had manifested those signs: is He with Musa (peace be upon him) as He was, so that He will protect them, or not? Therefore the denial of perception was stated first, then the affirmation of companionship specifically with him. He expressed the Deity by the name of the Lord, which indicates that kindness that was mentioned, so he said: ﴿Never! Indeed, with me is my Lord﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 62]. It was as if it were said: What will he do while the sea is before us and the enemy is behind us? So he said: ﴿He will guide me﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 62], meaning: to what I should do. Whoever is deeply versed in the journeys and the stories of the Children of Israel, as I mentioned in al-A'raf from the Torah, knows this, keeping in mind that al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), when they ascended to the cave, would mention the watchers and go ahead of the Prophet (ﷺ) to ransom him with himself; then he would mention the pursuers and fall back; then he would mention what was to the right and left and move to them, saying to the Prophet (ﷺ): "If I am killed, I am but one man; but if you are killed, the Ummah is destroyed." He knew that Allah, exalted is He, had undertaken to manifest the religion through the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which included protecting his noble self before that. For this reason he had that much anxiety on this day that was mentioned, while at the death of the Prophet (ﷺ) he was the most steadfast of people. For this reason he used the particle fa (then) implying immediate sequence in His saying: ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility﴾ (p. 477), meaning: the Supreme King. ﴿His tranquility﴾, meaning: the exceeding calm that is effective in producing serenity, ﴿upon him﴾, meaning: upon al-Siddiq, as Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said, because tranquility had not left the Prophet (ﷺ). Then He joined to ﴿Allah has already supported him﴾ His saying: ﴿and strengthened him﴾, meaning: the Prophet (ﷺ). The variation of pronouns here is not harmful, because it is not ambiguous. ﴿With soldiers you did not see﴾, meaning: of the noble angels. ﴿And He made the word﴾, meaning: the call of ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: those who committed disbelief, including whoever among them believed after that and others, ﴿the lowest﴾. So He frustrated their effort and turned back their plot. Then He began to inform about what belongs to Him, glory be to Him, continuously and without any interruption at all at any time, saying: ﴿And the word of Allah﴾, meaning: He who has complete encompassment of everything. Ya'qub put it in the accusative as a conjunction to what preceded: ﴿is the highest﴾, meaning: alone, nothing happens except what He wills, always and forever, and Allah is capable of that. ﴿And Allah﴾, meaning: the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, ﴿is All-Mighty﴾, meaning: absolutely, overpowering everything of that and other than that, ﴿All-Wise﴾, meaning: none of His purpose can be annulled, because of the causes that converge which no one has any hope of resisting; so there is no escape from their taking effect.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 41:

When these admonitions reached the attentive hearts to the degree that prepared them for acceptance, He, glorified is He, turned to them with a command and said: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy.﴾ By lightness is meant everything that is a cause of ease in jihad and of eagerness for it, and by heaviness everything that induces delay in it. Abu Hayyan said: "Here lightness and heaviness are used metaphorically for one who can travel with ease and one who can travel with difficulty. As for one who cannot travel, such as the blind man (p-478) and the like, he is excluded from this. End of quotation."

Al-Baghawi said: Al-Zuhri said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, may God have mercy on him, went out to the raid when one of his eyes had been lost. It was said to him: "You are ill and a person of harm." He said: "God has called forth the light and the heavy. If I cannot fight, I will increase the numbers and guard the baggage." Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili related in his Musnad, with a sound chain, from Anas that Abu Talha, may God be pleased with him, recited Surah Bara'ah and came to this verse and said: "I do not think my Lord calls me forth, young or old! Equip me!" He died, and they could not find an island to bury him in except after seven days, and he had not changed.

﴿And strive﴾: that is, exert your effort so that the effort of the disbelievers may be spent.

Since this verse is in the context of rebuke for those who grew heavy toward the earth and held back from jihad when called forth during the expedition to Tabuk, and since the cause of the holding back was what existed at that time of hardship in wealth, the severity of the heat, and the pleasantness of the shade in the gardens at the time of the ripening of the fruits, as is well known in the biographies, the context here required giving precedence to wealth and self, unlike what preceded. For the discourse before was about the comparison between jihad in the way of God and serving the House and those who make pilgrimage to it, in this surah whose revelation coincided with the time after the battlefields and the long separation from wealth and children. He gave precedence to wealth because it is viewed from two aspects: (p-479) its scarcity, and the love of residing in the gardens to enjoy them and fear of losing them, while in them is the sustenance of the souls. Thus the viewing of it became what drives one to stinginess with the self. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿with your wealth and your selves﴾, that is, with both together as far as you are able, or with one of them, ﴿in the way of God﴾, that is, the Supreme King, so that no obstacle remains from Him. ﴿That﴾, that is, the great matter, ﴿is better﴾, that is, in itself, attained, ﴿for you﴾, that is, specific to you. It is permissible that it be an elative of preference, in the sense that the worship of the fighter through jihad is better than the worship of the one who sits at home with other than it, whatever it may be, as the Prophet ﷺ said to one who asked him: "Is it possible to attain the rank of the fighter?" He said: "Can you stand without tiring and fast without breaking your fast?" He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿if you were to know﴾, indicating that this matter, although general, benefits only those of clear minds and abundant indications, for knowledge, and nothing is counted as knowledge except what is beneficial, urges toward action and toward doing it well by sincerity of intention, correcting aims, strengthening resolve, and other such things, while its opposite produces its opposite.

This rebuke indicated that among them were some who lagged behind from jihad, preoccupied with things like wealth and children. And since what these verses contain of commands, admonitions and exhortations was fit to lighten every burdened person and rouse every lazy person, souls longed to know what would happen afterward. So God, glory be to Him, informed them, in eloquent expressions that report the states of those who stayed behind and the tales of the sluggish, implying that there were those [p. 480] whom wretchedness had overcome, so that they did not benefit from the admonitions. He therefore turned from the gentleness of address to the reproach of the burdened, using the mode of turning away, which signals wrath that is certain, expresses displeasure, exposes their disgraces, scatters their ugliness, and brings out of them what they had entered into under the general address by the name of faith. He said: ﴿If it had been﴾, that is, what you call them to, ﴿an easy gain﴾, that is, worldly goods within easy reach, ﴿and a moderate journey﴾, that is, a middling, just, near journey, ﴿they would have followed you﴾, that is, for the sake of hoping for the gain together with the ease of the journey, because their aspirations are limited and bound to the immediate. ﴿But﴾, that is, they did not follow you, out of heaviness toward the earth and contentment with the transient present over the enduring absent, because ﴿the distance seemed long to them﴾, that is, the stretch that is covered by the measure of feet in walking, through which hardship and difficulty are obtained, and what they would gain from its fatigue did not match what they hoped for from the gain. So they asked your permission. In this is an indication of their blame for the lowness of their aspirations and the baseness of their dispositions, through incapacity, laziness, greed and heaviness, and an indication that this religion is firm and is carried only by one of resolute purpose and true determination, as the poet said:

*When he resolves, he sets his resolve between his eyes, and turns aside from remembering the consequences, leaving them behind.*

How excellent is the wisdom of those of firm resolve and of patience in hardships and burdens! Since He had censured them for their stinginess with the world, He followed it with their charge of being generous with religion. He said, reporting what would happen from them as a sign of prophethood: ﴿They will swear﴾, that is, those who stayed behind, with a report that is certain and admits no breach, ﴿by God﴾, that is, the One above whom there is nothing greater, when you return to them, in addition to what they violated of your sanctity by staying behind from you, adding to it the violation of God's sanctity through lying, saying: "By God, ﴿if we had been able﴾, that is, to go out to what you called us to, ﴿we would have gone out with you.﴾" They swear while ﴿they destroy themselves﴾, that is, by this oath whose purpose is to preserve their lives, because they lied in it and so violated the sanctity of the name of God. ﴿And God﴾, that is, while the Great King, who encompasses all in knowledge and power, glory be to Him, ﴿knows that they are indeed liars.﴾ Thus they combined the destruction of themselves with disgrace before God, since He knows their lie in claiming they were unable. The recompense of the liar in such a matter is perpetual wrath, which requires everlasting, eternal punishment.

(p-٤٨١)When He rebuked them for turning away, for staying behind, and for swearing falsely about it, He turned to him (ﷺ) with reproach in gentle address, while persisting in leniency toward them, conciliating them, accepting their pardon, and abandoning opposition to this extent. He said, indicating that they had stayed behind only with his (ﷺ) permission, on excuses they claimed, lying in them just as they lied in this oath. He placed the supplication before the reproach because of the intensity of His concern for his (ﷺ) affair and His gentleness toward him (ﷺ): ﴿May God pardon you﴾, i.e., the Possessor of majesty and honor. This is as the custom of the Arabs was in addressing their elders, saying: "May God set right the commander," and "the king," and the like.

Since it is known that he (ﷺ) would not give permission except for what he saw as pleasing to God, such as winning them over and the like, He made clear that He, glorified is He, was pleased with him for abandoning the granting of permission. So He said, by way of allusion to this: ﴿Why did you give them permission?﴾, i.e., to stay behind you, holding fast to the command previously given to be gentle with them and to overlook their faults, in agreement with what you were disposed to, namely love of gentleness. This was indeed (p-٤٨٢) at the outset, out of fear of dissension and strife. But now religion has become dominant and the affair of the believers has become firmly established, so what is commanded is severity toward the hypocrites. Why then did you not refrain from granting them permission ﴿until it becomes clear to you﴾, i.e., with complete clarity, ﴿who are truthful﴾, i.e., in fulfilling the commands, by what they acknowledged of the word of tawhid, ﴿and you know the liars﴾, i.e., in what they displayed of faith with their tongues? For if you did not grant them permission, they would have stayed behind without permission, not observing the covenant they made with you to obey in hardship and ease, in what is welcome and what is disliked.

Abu Hayyan said: "And ḥattā (حَتّى, "until") is the limit of a question." End of quotation. This is because, although it governs an affirmative verb, its meaning is negation, i.e., "What is the matter with you that you did not compel them to go out with you, so that by that compulsion it might be realized who obeys and who disobeys?" The conclusion is that what he (ﷺ) did was good and in accordance with what God commanded him, for he does not speak from desire, but from the command of God, either by a fresh revelation that had just arrived or by reliance on a prior revelation already present and ready. What He, glorified is He, pointed to is the best example: ﴿That God may forgive you what preceded of your sin﴾ [al-Fath: 2], by way of "the good deeds of the righteous are the sins of those brought near," and by way of elevation from a high station to a higher station, a gentle governing of them by justice, since it became clear that they were not people of virtue.

Al-Ustadh Abu al-Hasan al-Harali said at the end of his book, al-ʿUrwa (العُرْوَة, "The Handhold") fī tafāwut wajh al-khiṭāb fīmā bayna (p-٤٨٣) mā unzila ʿalā wifq al-waṣiyya aw unzila ʿalā ḥukm al-kitāb (in the variation of the mode of address between what was revealed in accordance with the testamentary charge and what was revealed according to the judgment of the Book): Know that God, glorified is He, sent Muhammad (ﷺ) with mercy to all the worlds, and made his character one of pardon and kindness, as is found in the earlier books in the saying of the Exalted: "And I will make pardon and kindness his character." He charged him with this, as is related from him (ﷺ) that he said: "My Lord charged me, without interpreter or intermediary, with seven qualities: fear of God in private and in public; that I join those who sever ties with me; that I pardon those who wrong me; that I give to those who deprive me; that my speech be remembrance, my silence reflection, and my gaze a lesson."

Among what his Lord charged him with, blessed and exalted is He, without interpreter or intermediary, was that he should join whoever severed from him, pardon whoever wronged him, and not sever from one who disbelieved in Him and turned away from Him. So he (ﷺ), by the judgment of what he was sent with, what he was disposed to, and what he was charged with, was committed to pardoning those who wronged him and joining those who severed from him, unless he was openly compelled to abandon this and return to the right of justice, retaliation, and vindication, which is contrary to the breadth of his charge, but which accords with the judgments of the ways of the earlier peoples in calling them to account with truth and justice. This was in order to find in his comprehensive law something like what preceded of truth and justice, however little, and because his law is distinguished by what God specially granted him (ﷺ) of mission, with the breadth of mercy and grace: ﴿Indeed God commands justice and excellence﴾ [al-Nahl: 90]; ﴿And God would not punish them while you are among them﴾ [al-Anfal: 33].

So among the Qur'an (p-٤٨٤) is what was revealed in the manner for which he was sent, disposed, and charged, such as His saying: ﴿Repel evil with that which is better﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 96]; His saying: ﴿Take what is easily given, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant﴾ [al-A'raf: 199]; His saying: ﴿Had you been harsh and hard of heart, they would have scattered from around you. So pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the affair﴾ [Al 'Imran: 159]; His saying: ﴿So forgive with gracious forgiveness﴾ [al-Hijr: 85]; His saying: ﴿So overlook them and say, "Peace"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 89]. The root of its meaning is in the sense of His saying: ﴿There has come to you a messenger from among yourselves; he grieves over what troubles you, is anxious for you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128]. So what was revealed in this manner, in which the charge and the Book cooperated, and which he (ﷺ) accepted by disposition, state, and action, without any hesitation on his part, because the two matters were mutually supporting and the two addresses agreed: the address of the charge and the address of the Book. This mode of revelation is specific to the Glorious Qur'an, which is specific to him (ﷺ), which no one before him was given: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated and the Glorious Qur'an﴾ [al-Hijr: 87].

Among the Qur'an is also what was revealed according to the judgment of justice and truth, whose merit was previously established in the ways of the earlier peoples and the books of earlier generations, and in the enforcement of God's justice, glorified is He, against those held to account; and in being content with the connection of one who connects, distancing the self-sufficient, turning toward the one who seeks, and taking vengeance upon the fleeing. This differs from what God disposed His Prophet to and what He charged His beloved (ﷺ) with. So when something was revealed to him (ﷺ) —that is, from the Book— according to the requirement of truth and the enforcement of justice, he (ﷺ) would await its lightening and hope for its ease, until he was openly compelled to take it and to be bound by its judgment. At that point he would stand up for God with it and manifest his excuse in its enforcement. Thus for him, in the address of stringency upon him in taking it, there is the greatest praise and most eloquent commendation from God, contrary to what the ignorant imagine. Among what was revealed as an announcement of his praise, for his pausing to enforce the judgment of justice and truth, hoping to make up for the creatures and seeking the compassion of the Truth, is something like His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their traces if they do not believe in this message﴾ [al-Kahf: 6]; and His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself, that they will not be believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3]; and His saying: ﴿And We know that your breast is constricted by what they say﴾ [al-Hijr: 97]. Among what was revealed in the manner of declaring over him what he was upon of mercy, and his pausing before taking up the ways of the earlier peoples, until he would be compelled to it, so that his excuse would stand in limiting himself to the judgment of the charge and the state of disposition, is something like His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions, the Fire is his promised place. So do not be in doubt about it; indeed it is the truth from your Lord﴾ [Hud: 17]; and His saying: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them entirely. Would you then compel the people until they become believers?﴾ [Yunus: 99]; and His saying: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, ask those who read the Book before you. Certainly the truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [Yunus: 94]. That is: do not pause in seeking mercy for them as the doubter pauses over a thing, or the one who is uncertain about it, because he knows that there must be for his community (p-٤٨٦) a portion of the enforcement of the word of justice against them and the realization of the word of punishment upon them, and the carrying out of the judgment of might against some of them but not all, according to the practice of those before them among the people of the earlier books in calling them to account for their sins. So God seized them for their sins: ﴿So each We seized for his sin﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 40]. And their turning back at the sight of signs did not benefit them: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before﴾ [Yunus: 91]; ﴿Do not flee, but return to what you were made to enjoy and your dwellings﴾ [al-Anbiya': 13]. This is because every one who is confronted with punishment returns, necessarily, from his falsehood when it no longer benefits him: ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a town We have destroyed that they will not return﴾ [al-Anbiya': 95]; ﴿Except the people of Yunus; when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the worldly life﴾ [Yunus: 98]. Because God, exalted is He, had concealed within the heart of their prophet, upon him be peace, a resolve to destroy them, He showed them mercy. And when He filled His Prophet (ﷺ) with mercy for his community —its disbelievers, its believers, and its hypocrites— He pointed, with verses showing their being held to account, and informed him of the restraint of His Prophet (ﷺ) from winning them over, and He made him reckon among them the believers rather than the disbelievers and hypocrites: ﴿O Prophet, God is sufficient for you and for those who follow you of the believers﴾ [al-Anfal: 64]. All of that was known to him (ﷺ) before its occurrence, by the sense of His saying: ﴿The practice of those We sent before you of Our messengers﴾ [al-Isra': 77]; (p-٤٨٧) ﴿The practice of God that has already occurred before﴾ [al-Fath: 23]; ﴿So they would not believe in what they had denied before﴾ [Yunus: 74]; ﴿Thus We let it enter into the hearts of the criminals﴾ [al-Hijr: 12]; ﴿They do not believe in it, and the practice of the former peoples has already passed﴾ [al-Hijr: 13]. "And for this reason he (ﷺ) said, when it was revealed to him: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you﴾ [Yunus: 94]: 'As for me, I do not doubt, nor do I ask.'" Because he knew the totality of God's command: that among them are those whom mercy will overtake and those upon whom the word of punishment is due. Yet he remained committed to winning them over and attracting them until he was compelled to abandon this by a public address, such as His saying: ﴿He frowned and turned away﴾ [‘Abasa: 1]; ﴿That the blind man came to him﴾ [‘Abasa: 2]; ﴿And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself﴾ [‘Abasa: 3]; ﴿Or be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him﴾ [‘Abasa: 4]; ﴿As for one who considers himself self-sufficient﴾ [‘Abasa: 5]; ﴿You give attention to him﴾ [‘Abasa: 6]; ﴿Though it is not upon you that he not purify himself﴾ [‘Abasa: 7]; ﴿But as for one who came to you striving﴾ [‘Abasa: 8]; ﴿While he fears [God]﴾ [‘Abasa: 9]; ﴿You are unmindful of him﴾ [‘Abasa: 10]; ﴿No! Indeed, it is a reminder﴾ [‘Abasa: 11]; ﴿So whoever wills may remember it﴾ [‘Abasa: 12]; and such as His saying: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives until he inflicts a massacre upon the land. You desire the commodities of this world, but God desires the Hereafter, and God is Mighty and Wise﴾ [al-Anfal: 67]; ﴿Had there not been a decree from God that preceded, you would have been touched for what you took by a great punishment﴾ [al-Anfal: 68]; ﴿So eat of what you have gained, lawful and good, and fear God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Anfal: 69]. These verses and the like are heard by the knowledgeable one who understands their place, under compulsion upon the Prophet of mercy, until he returns to the justice of the Prophet of the battle, from among the praises of the Qur'an for him and the testimony to his fulfilment of a covenant and a charge, until his naming as "Prophet of mercy," steadfast upon the charge, and "Prophet of the battle," enforcing at a time (p-٤٨٨) the judgment of truth and the manifestation of justice. So he (ﷺ), by all of the Qur'an, is praised and described with the great character, comprehensive of what the books of earlier generations contained and of what God specially gave him of the breadth of the Glorious Qur'an. This is the aspect of the difference between the charge and the Book in the clear address. And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. End of quotation.

When the Prophet ﷺ was unable to identify them by this means, the Knower of what is in hearts (al-'Alim bima fi al-Damair) described them to him by means that compensate for that, saying, in answer to a question: ﴿Those who truly believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission﴾. That is: they seek your permission only out of the utmost desire for it. ﴿Those who believe in Allah﴾: that is, they renew their faith in Allah at all times, sincerely from their own souls, in the King who possesses the attributes of perfection. ﴿And the Last Day﴾: that is, the Day on which recompense with reward and punishment takes place. ﴿That﴾: that is, regarding ﴿they strive with their wealth and their lives﴾. Rather, they hasten to striving when you point to it and urge them to it in general, let alone asking your permission to stay behind from it. The sincere ones among the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers) used to say: "We will never ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission in jihad, for our Lord has urged us to it again and again, so what benefit is there in asking permission! We will surely strive with him with our wealth and our lives." They were such that if he ﷺ had ordered them to remain behind, it would have been hard for them, as happened to 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) in the expedition of Tabuk, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Are you not pleased to be to me in the position of Harun to Musa?" Since the implied sense is: whoever has this attribute, know that he is God-fearing by the reports of Allah, he (the author) connected to it (p-٤٨٩) His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of the God-fearing﴾. That is: the One who has complete encompassing knowledge, of those who fear Allah, all of them.

When he had informed about the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), he identified their opposites in a restrictive manner, as emphasis to affirm the attribute of knowledge with what He, glory be to Him, had reported. Thus permission-seeking was negated from the believers twice, and it was established for the hypocrites in the most emphatic way: ﴿Only those seek your permission﴾, i.e., for the like of that; so how much more so for seeking permission to stay behind! ﴿who do not believe﴾, i.e., faith would be renewed for them, ﴿in God﴾, i.e., the Sovereign, Most High, to whom belongs ultimate greatness, with a faith that gathers all the requisite conditions, ﴿and the Last Day﴾, because they do not hope for reward nor fear punishment, even if they claim that with their tongues.

Since this is the attribute of those who openly profess disbelief, he clarified that the intended ones are the hypocrites by His saying: ﴿and their hearts are in doubt﴾, i.e., they followed the whisperings and deliberately walked along with them until they were molded by doubt. Since the doubter is always pulled between the goodness of natural disposition and the evil of whisperings, He said: ﴿So they﴾, i.e., as a consequence of that, ﴿in their doubt, go back and forth﴾, i.e., between negation and affirmation, in the manner of one bewildered, never resolutely affirming either of them, even if they believe that God exists, for the polytheists also believe in that, but it does not benefit them due to the failure to meet its condition. And their seeking permission is not in order to strive out of a desire for jihad, but rather a preparation so that, when you command them to it, they may say: "We have no equipment for this time, so grant us permission to stay behind until we prepare!" But they have lied; that is not their condition, (p-490) rather their condition is that they do not want to go out with you.

﴿Had they intended to go out, they would have prepared for it﴾, that is, before its occurrence, ﴿a preparation﴾, that is, strength and readiness of provisions, weapons and mounts, ﴿such that they would be characterized by what you enjoined upon them of urging [to fight], in the manner of what was commanded in al-Anfal, so that they would be like those present in the heart of the battle, standing in the line, having made ready for it with all its equipment﴾. ﴿But﴾ they never intended that at all, so ﴿they did not prepare any preparation for it﴾. Then, when you gave the command, they began to make excuses for lacking the preparation, though that was not the reason. Their only obstacle was their aversion to going out. This is because ﴿Allah disliked﴾, that is, the Possessor of Majesty and Honor, acted as one who dislikes, so He did not desire ﴿their setting out﴾, that is, their marching with you, in compliance with their request for that, because He knew of their unfitness for it. ﴿So He held them back﴾, that is, He restrained them from it with a great restraint, by occupying them with the desires He made beloved to them and the hardships He made hateful to them, because they hope for no reward and fear no punishment other than the sword. They confined their base aspirations to bestial qualities. When desires took control over them and the base souls possessed them, they were called from that direction: "Where are you going?" ﴿And it was said﴾, that is, to them, when they rushed eagerly toward those desires, ﴿"Sit [behind]"﴾, that is, remain behind and do not accompany my army. In His saying ﴿"with those who sit"﴾, that is, those whose condition is that, such as the sick, the disabled, the children and the women, there is a rebuke (p-491) of such magnitude that its measure is known only to people of lofty aspirations and noble souls. He expressed it in the passive voice to indicate that they obey the command to sit, literally and figuratively, whoever they may be, just as they disobey the command to march forth, whoever it may be, because their souls are receptive to lowliness and unfit for excellence in any respect.

When it was as though it were said: "What is the matter with Him that He hindered them, when We were intending a distant journey and a great, formidable enemy, so we are in need of assistance, even if only by increasing the numbers?" It is said: ﴿Had they gone forth among you﴾, that is, He did that to them, because if they had ﴿gone forth among you﴾, that is, even if they were few, reinforced by your groups, ﴿they would have added to you nothing﴾, that is, by their going forth they would have added nothing of any kind, ﴿except ruin﴾, that is, they would not have brought you anything beyond what you already had, other than ruin. The exception here is the *istithnā' mufarragh* (an exceptive construction in which the excepted noun is omitted), and the omitted noun (the *mustathnā minhu*, the thing that is understood to be attributed to them) is "a thing." This does not imply that any of them was characterized by ruin before the hypocrites went forth. *Khabal* means corruption, and it is understood as deception and taking someone off guard. ﴿And they would have rushed about﴾, that is, they would have carried out *al-īḍā'* (quick riding or hurrying). He omitted the object to indicate that their aim was the hurrying itself, not restricted to any particular mount. He used the expression *al-īḍā'* because it applies to a rider, and a rider is faster than a walker. ﴿Between you﴾, that is, they would have hastened in their going back and forth among you, seeking out your faults and waiting for your slips, so that they might find an entry point for corruption through tale-bearing and other means if they did not find them. *Al-īḍā'* in travel may be gentle or swift, and what is meant here is swiftness. The root *w-ḍ-ʿ* in all its forms revolves around movement, sometimes upward and sometimes downward, and this entails stillness and a receptive place for that. On this basis, the words *al-ʿuḍw* (limb), *al-ʿiwaḍ* (substitute), *ʿawḍ* (which means "time," *al-dahr*), *ḍawʿ al-rīḥ* (the scent of the wind), *al-taṣwīt bi'l-bukā'* (wailing with weeping), *al-ḍaʿah* (a kind of tree in the desert), *al-waḍʿ* (placing something down in a place), and *al-sayr al-layyin wa'l-sarī*ʿ (gentle and swift travel) are all explained. *Khilāl* is the plural of *khalal*, which means a gap. ﴿They seek to cause you trouble﴾, that is, while they desire for you *al-fitnah* (trouble), meaning the scattering of your unity and the separation of your companions. Earlier, at ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾ [al-Anfāl: 39], it was explained that *fitnah* is a mixing that causes deviation from the proper state. That is, they desire for you the thing that would befall you, changing your condition to one that would harm you and gladden them. ﴿And among you are those who listen to them﴾, that is, while the situation is that among you there are those who are most receptive to their speech because of the weakness of their knowledge and opinions. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾, that is, He who informed you of this about them has comprehensive knowledge of everything, and He is Knowing of them, so trust what He tells you about them. This was the original wording, but He said ﴿of the wrongdoers﴾ to point to the quality that brought them misery by keeping them away from the place of goodness, and to generalize the ruling by stating that He knows them, those who listened to them, and every wrongdoer. The conclusion is that He likened their striving to corrupt you to a man whose camel is placed in a land containing close-set, towering objects. He is intensely occupied with discerning the gaps among them and contemplating them, out of fear that something from those objects might strike him and give him the cup of death. Thus they have no concern except the desire to corrupt you, by not reaching any of their aims.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 48:

When He, glorified is He, had informed of that and urged acceptance of their reports, by what He had described His Most Holy Essence with of comprehensive knowledge, He began to establish the proof for what He had said by reminding them of matters whose witnessing from them had already preceded. He said, giving the reason for what He had informed of: ﴿Indeed, they sought discord﴾ meaning: they all sought, with great seeking, ﴿to cause you turmoil﴾ meaning: to scatter you, ﴿before [this]﴾ meaning: before this expedition, on the day of Uhud, by breaking the hearts of the army through withdrawing from it, to the point that some of them nearly lost heart; and at al-Muraysi', by what Ibn Ubayy said: ﴿The more honorable will surely expel the more humble from it﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8]; and at the Battle of the Trench, by what occurred from them of denial regarding the taking of the treasures of Kisra and Caesar, and spreading rumors against you concerning the breach by Banu Qurayzah, and other things, as they had done before it at the expedition of Qaynuqa' and al-Nadir, in their intention to strengthen each of them against you; and in other days of Allah in which He reversed their intentions and made their fortunes sluggish. ﴿And they turned over﴾ meaning: a great turning over ﴿matters for you﴾ meaning: those matters in which there was harm for you, back and forth, by reversing opinions and devising schemes and stratagems, perhaps they would find an opportunity to break your command, which they would seize, or a gap in a situation which they would widen. Their condition extended in this state ﴿until the truth came﴾ meaning: the established reality, about which there is no dispute in its occurrence, of what His promise, glorified is He, had preceded concerning the manifestation of the religion and the suppression of the corrupters ﴿and the command of Allah prevailed﴾ meaning: the One characterized by all attributes of perfection, of majesty and beauty, such that they had no hope of concealing it ﴿while they were averse﴾ meaning: to all of that. So they had no hope of attempting anything, whether by confrontation or by deception, and their concern became now withdrawal and exaggeration in concealing conditions and hiding deeds and words.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 49:

When He had summarized them in this ruling, and He had already indicated that among them were those who had asked permission to go out in preparation for an excuse for it, he began to differentiate them, and he began with the detailed ones by those who openly asked permission to stay behind. So He said, conjoining it to ﴿They had certainly sought [to cause] discord﴾ [At-Tawbah: 48], ﴿And among them is one who says﴾, i.e., by his disposition, renewing this statement without shame, ﴿"Grant me permission [to stay behind]"﴾, i.e., to remain behind you, ﴿and do not put me into temptation﴾, i.e., do not be a cause of my temptation by being decisive in the command to march forth, so that I would be tempted, either by staying behind, whereby I would be openly disobeying, or by traveling, whereby I would incline toward the women of the Byzantines (banu al-Asfar) and apostatize from the religion, for I have no patience regarding women. The one who said this was al-Jadd ibn Qays, who was among the Ansar and a hypocrite.

When they showed that they intended to distance themselves from something, and then they had committed themselves to it, the opportunity was seized to inform of that in the most emphatic manner, by introducing a negation upon a negation, to obtain the firm affirmation through the confession of the one questioned. So it was said: ﴿Verily, in temptation have they fallen﴾, i.e., by what they said and did. Thus, temptation became a container for them, and by this they placed themselves in Hell. In the expression "fallen" there is an indication of their being quickly ensnared in the snares of temptation with force, such that their escape from it became difficult. ﴿And indeed, Hell is encompassing of the disbelievers﴾, i.e., because of the encompassing of the temptation into which they had cast themselves over them. He said "the disbelievers" (p-495) to generalize and to draw attention to the attribute that led them to that.

And since it was as if it had been asked: "What is the trial into which they fell, so that Hell encompasses them because of it?" it was answered: ﴿If﴾, i.e., the trial is their being that. It may also be that this is the cause of Hell encompassing them. Because they are of the al-Aws and al-Khazraj, and the Ansar (the Helpers) are their relatives, they singled out the Prophet (ﷺ) for enmity and intense rage. Likewise, they were not troubled or pleased by good or bad fortune except by what had a real impact, as indicated by the expression "befalls" (iṣābah) rather than "touches" (massa), and not by what fell short of that. This was to protect the hearts of their relatives and to guard the secrets of their women. So He said, alluding to this: ﴿If good befalls you﴾, i.e., by God's decree, ﴿a good thing﴾, i.e., victory or something else, ﴿it distresses them﴾, i.e., because of the rancor and sickness in their hearts. ﴿And if a misfortune befalls you﴾, i.e., a calamity, however small, as happened on the Day of Uhud, ﴿they say﴾, i.e., out of delight and boasting in the soundness of their opinions, ﴿"We had already taken our precaution"﴾, i.e., "We disobeyed the one who commanded us, and we did not surrender our reins to anyone, so that we would be like the blind." For al-amr (the matter, affair) is the event, and it is the opposite of the prohibition. From it comes al-amīr (the commander). One says rajulun imarrun wa-imarratun, with the letter mīm pronounced with shadda and fatḥa, with kasra on the hamza, and it may also be pronounced with fatḥa: meaning weakness of judgment, one who agrees with everyone regarding whatever they want from his entire affair. This is al-a'mah (the blind one) in both form and meaning. (p-496) ﴿Before﴾, i.e., before this calamity occurred. So we were not following any command that would afflict us, and thus what befell those who followed him did not befall us. Their command, had they been obedient, would have been something firmly in the hand of the one who commands. But when they disobeyed him, they became as though they had already taken it from him.

And since their saying was far from uprightness, and thus was fit not to be said, and if it was said, it was worthy of being retracted through a mubārāh (a contest of conduct) toward turning back from it and seeking forgiveness for it, the Exalted indicated their persistence in it, so He said: ﴿And they turn away﴾, i.e., from this position in which they said that, even if it lasted, to their families, ﴿while they rejoice﴾, i.e., at your misfortune, because of their disbelief and because of their deliverance from it.

When their statement contained the delusion that one could guard oneself against fate (qadar), God, the Exalted, said, informing of His answer to them and addressing the Messenger for the loftiness of his station: "Say" (qul), meaning: We do not say your statement, because we know that we possess no harm and no benefit. Rather, we say: "Nothing will befall us" (lan yuṣībana), meaning of good and evil, "except what Allah has decreed" (kataba), meaning predestined, "Allah," meaning the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge. Since the decree of Allah is entirely good for the believer, so that if ease befalls him he gives thanks and if hardship befalls him he is patient, He expressed it with the lam (of possession) and said "for us" (lanā), meaning that none can avert it from us except Him, glory be to Him. "He is" (huwa), meaning He alone, "our Mawlā" (protector and master), meaning the One near to us who takes charge of all our affairs, and there is no one near to us other than Him. So if He willed, He would repel every calamity from us, because He is nearer to us than it is. It does not reach us without His knowledge, and He is able. We know that for Him in this there is a subtle inner wisdom (laṭīf sarīrah), before which the sharpest insights of thought are diminished, and before the full grasp of its reality the gaze of the eyes falls short. Therefore we do not accuse Him in His decree, because we have relied upon Him and entrusted our affairs to Him, and the one who entrusts does not accuse the one entrusted (al-wakīl). "And upon Allah" (wa-ʿalā Allāh), meaning the Supreme King and no other, "let the believers rely" (fa-l-yatawakkal al-mu'minūn), meaning all of them, with a great and resolute reliance from which there is no turning away. Thus the distinction between the believer and the disbeliever is the surrender of the self to Him alone, without objection to Him, who turns it however He wills and rules over it as He desires.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 52:

Since this (the preceding discussion) entailed that their (the believers') times of ease and their times of hardship are both good for them, in that acceptance of the bitter decree necessarily brings the Decreer's turning toward the one decreed upon with clemency and mercy, He stated this explicitly in His words: ﴿Say: "Do you await for us anything but one of the two best outcomes?"﴾ That is: you wait with a great waiting. ﴿One of the two best outcomes﴾ That is: either that we strike our enemies, so we are victorious, take spoils, and are rewarded; or that they strike us with death or something else, so we are rewarded. Both matters are good. As for the ease, which you agree is good, its matter is clear. As for the hardship, it necessitates Allah's pleasure with us and His reward for us, for patience in it and our contentment with it, out of reverence for Him and submission to His command. So it is a good outcome, as we know, not an evil one as you imagine. ﴿And we await for you﴾ That is: we await one of the two evil outcomes, which is ﴿that Allah afflict you﴾ That is: the One who has all power, and we are of His party, ﴿with a punishment from Himself﴾ That is: with no causation on our part in it, as He destroyed the earlier generations as insights for mankind; ﴿or by our hands﴾ That is: by means of us, through killing, plunder, captivity, striking, and other such things; because your caution does not protect you from Allah. All of that is hateful to you.

Since this explanation entailed that evil belongs particularly to the party of Satan, it was fitting that they be commanded, in mockery of them and to belittle their standing, with what had led them to it. So He said: ﴿Then wait﴾ That is: you (wait), ﴿indeed we﴾ That is: we, ﴿are with you waiting﴾ That is: for you. We do as you do, though the intention differs. This verse is of the type called ihtibak (interlocking ellipsis): He omitted first the affliction, to indicate it by what He affirmed second, and second the "one of the two evil outcomes," to indicate it by affirming the "two best outcomes" first.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 53:

Since the sum of what befalls them from Us at their hands is the punishment of spending, the purifying of what their wealth has been cleansed of through aid in the way of Allah, out of fear of being accused of hypocrisy in their statements, so that they might ransom themselves thereby from the journey, He said: ﴿Say: Spend, willingly or unwillingly﴾, i.e., bring about spending for everything that is called spending, ﴿willingly or unwillingly﴾, i.e., displaying willingness or displaying unwillingness. And since turning away from them was only caused by their disbelief and not by their spending, He did not link the answer with the particle fa (then), but said: ﴿It will never be accepted from you﴾, i.e., there occurs an acceptance of anything that comes from you at all, from anyone who has the capacity to accept, whoever he may be. For this reason He built the verb in the passive form, because your hearts are unwilling and have no good intention in spending or in anything else. Thus the division of your spending into willing and unwilling is only with regard to the outward appearance. It seems that He expressed it with the form tafa''ala (taqabbala, "to be accepted") as an indication of its being accepted from them outwardly. And since it is not accepted inwardly in any state whatsoever, He gave the reason with His saying: ﴿Indeed you have been﴾, i.e., by nature and disposition, ﴿a people who are defiantly disobedient﴾, i.e., deeply immersed in defiant disobedience, having reached its utmost extent.

The commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 54:

When he gave the reason for their deep-rootedness (ʿarāqa) in departing from obedience, he explained it in His words: ﴿Nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted from them﴾, meaning inwardly. For this reason he expressed it with the bare form (al-mujarrad), and for this reason he put the verb in the passive, because what benefits is acceptance in reality, not that it comes from a specific source. ﴿From them, their expenditures﴾, meaning even if they were great. ﴿Except that they disbelieved in God﴾, meaning the One who possesses all the attributes of perfection, of majesty and of beauty, because of the corruption of their natures and the evil of their dispositions.

Since the acceptance of expenditures prepares for the purity that prayer produces, the context for their non-acceptance was more eloquent, in order that the prohibition of praying over them would follow from it, because it is more indicative of impurity (khubth). So he emphasized their disbelief by adding the preposition (al-jarr, the particle) to signal that disbelief in each of the two, on its own, is a barrier. So he said: ﴿And in His Messenger﴾, meaning their wickedness lies in their not being believers, and this by itself is the sufficient barrier to acceptance. Then he impugned the two witnesses to what they showed of faith, namely prayer and almsgiving, and other forms of spending on good works, with what is necessarily entailed by disbelief and indicative of it. So he said: ﴿And they do not come to prayer﴾, meaning the obligatory prayer and other than it, ﴿except lazily﴾, meaning in a state of laziness; they never come to it with eagerness. ﴿And they do not spend﴾, meaning a spending of obligation or otherwise, ﴿except while unwilling﴾, meaning in a state of reluctance, even if the opposite appears to you. All of this is due to the lack of a sound intention and belief in the Hereafter. This does not contradict [the description of spending as] voluntary, because that is according to what is assumed or apparent, whereas this is according to what is actual.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 55:

(p-500) Since the otherworldly benefit, which is the true benefit, has been negated from their wealth, there follows from this a renunciation of it (zuhd), which necessitates not paying attention to it and not believing that there is blessing in it or that it is a sign of good. So He said, clarifying the corruption within it that is supposed to be righteousness: ﴿So let not﴾ — with the fa' of causality, so the context is more eloquent than the context of the following verse after the prohibition of praying over them — ﴿their wealth impress you﴾, meaning: even if they spend it in My cause and equip the warriors with it. For that is not from them with sincerity, nor with good intention, nor with a beautiful inner disposition. Rather, it is because it humiliated them with the might of Islam and frightened them with the force of retribution, so it is among the torments. He joined the children to it, since they share with it in pleasures, strength, and use in jihad. So He said, emphasizing the negation by repeating the negating particle: ﴿nor their children﴾. It is as if it were said: For what purpose is their being given that? Had they withheld it and the sincere ones been given it, it would have been a strength for the religion. So He said: ﴿Allah only intends﴾, meaning: He causes the intention in them by it, the King who has the comprehensive encompassing of all wisdom just as He has the encompassing of complete power. And He made the restriction more emphatic by introducing the lam in His saying: ﴿to punish them﴾, meaning: in order that He punish them ﴿with them in the life﴾, meaning: even if it appears to be delightful, because that is the nature of life; so in reality it is for them a death. ﴿of this world﴾, meaning: at times through gathering and cultivating it, and at times through spending it unwillingly in the cause of Allah, or in purifying it, and at times through other than that. ﴿And that their souls depart﴾, meaning: and He only intends by empowering them over us that their souls depart at the time of death with extreme difficulty ﴿their souls﴾ (p-501) meaning: because of them, ﴿while they are﴾, meaning: while they are in the state of ﴿disbelievers﴾, meaning: deeply immersed in disbelief. And thus, everyone whom He, glory be to Him, intends to lead gradually (istidraj) — He typically multiplies their wealth and children for this very reason, because when they see their increase in these over some of the sincere believers, they assume that this is only for their honor and the goodness of their condition, so they continue upon it until they die. So He, glory be to Him, did not intend by it to bestow a gift upon them, but rather a trial and a tribulation. As for the religion, the Capable strengthens it by other than that, so that it is more manifest in its proof and clearer in its path. The conclusion is that it appeared to them that they were honored by these, and it was hidden from them that these were a cause of their punishment in life through their reliance upon them, and at death through its difficulty for them, alluded to by the word "depart," and in the Hereafter through their dying in the state of disbelief by their being led on by them. As for the believer, he does not die until he sees from the reward what consoles him for everything, so he longs for the meeting with Allah, and his soul departs while he is in the utmost love for its departure, because the body is an obstacle to him from what he sees.

Now that these matters have made clear their opposition to the believers and their departure from the bond of religion, which confirms their being described as defiantly disobedient (fisq), he clarifies another confusion regarding their conditions, which they sustain through false oaths. So He says: ﴿And they swear by God﴾, meaning: they seek to bring you turmoil while in fact they renew their oaths, ﴿by God﴾, meaning: by Him with the full extent of His greatness, ﴿that they are surely of you﴾, meaning: the hypocrites are surely of you, O believers, in your belief inwardly as they are outwardly, ﴿but they are not﴾ (p-502) meaning: while in fact they are not truthful in their oath that they are ﴿of you. Rather, they are a people﴾, meaning: although they have strength and resolve in what they attempt, ﴿who are fearful﴾, meaning: they fear you for their lives with a great fear that scatters their concerns; it is this fear that compels them to swear falsely, to display Islam outwardly.

Thus it is as if it were said: "Why then do they remain among us, when one who harbours hatred does not keep company with the one he hates?" It is said in reply: because they do not find anything that can protect them from you. ﴿If they could find a refuge﴾, that is, something to take refuge in, such as a fortress, a mountain, or a people who would protect them from you, ﴿or caves﴾ in the mountains that could contain them, the plural of maghārah (a place one enters; it is a mafalah form derived from ghāra fī al-shay', meaning to enter into it), and al-ghawr is what is low of the land.

Since the ghirān (that is, the holes bored into the mountains) were wide and easy to reach, He said: ﴿or a place of entry﴾, that is, a place they could enter only with the utmost difficulty and hardship because of its narrowness, or because of some obstacle on its path, or a people with whom they could associate, even though they dislike them. This is indicated by the intensive form in: ﴿they would turn towards it﴾, that is, they would hasten in their turning towards it, turning away from you, ﴿running headlong on their heels﴾. ﴿And they would rush headlong﴾, that is, their condition is the condition of a beast that was quick to obey its rider, then turned back on its heels and began, without intending to, to run with the utmost speed and the greatest eagerness and urge, so that nothing turns it back: not a well into which it falls, nor a place of destruction, nor anything else.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 58:

When he had established the condition of those who stay behind from jihad, and who sometimes gave their wealth in it as a ransom for their own journey, he began to mention those who share with him in spending and hypocrisy and who oppose him (p-٥٠٣). So he said: ﴿And among them are those who find fault with you﴾, meaning: they criticize you in the presence of their like, habitually, in concealment and secrecy, or openly and with little shame, ﴿concerning the charities﴾, meaning: those which you distribute to your followers. When he had informed about the finding fault, he informed that it was for the sake of their own share and not for the sake of religion, so he said: ﴿If they are given from them, they are pleased﴾, meaning: with you, ﴿but if they are not given from them﴾, then they suddenly show the anger that renews itself every moment, and they do not refrain from it at all. He expressed this by his saying: ﴿behold, they are angry﴾. Thus they agreed with the earlier ones in making the world their concern, but differed from them in that those (earlier ones) spent in order to enjoy staying behind, while these sought (wealth) in order to enjoy the very money they take. It was said: "It was revealed concerning Dhu al-Khuwaysira, when he said to the Prophet ﷺ while he was dividing the spoils of Hunayn: 'Be just, O Muhammad! For I have not seen you being just.' The Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'Woe to you! Who will be just if I am not just?'" And its hadith will come.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 59:

When Exalted is He informed about their bad and base state, which neither benefits them in this world nor saves them in the Hereafter, He alerted them to what is best for them of the noble and lofty state, saying: ﴿And if only they had been content with what Allah gave them﴾ — i.e., the hypocrites — ﴿and His Messenger﴾ — whose greatness derives from His greatness — ﴿and said: "Allah is sufficient for us"﴾ — i.e., with contentment — meaning: He suffices us, because He possesses all greatness, so He is absolute self-sufficiency (al-ghina al-mutlaq). ﴿and [if they had said]: "Allah will give us of His bounty, and [so will] His Messenger"﴾ — i.e., the Mighty King, by a promise that does not fail, and they would have believed that no one has a right [over them]... (p-504) Since sufficiency sometimes comes through immediate, prompt provision and sometimes through trust in a deferred promise, he made clear that the second is what is meant, because it is a stronger indication of faith, saying: ﴿Allah will give us﴾ — i.e., the Greatest King — by a promise in which there is no breach, and they believed that no one has a right to [anything], so they said: ﴿of His bounty and His Messenger's﴾ — i.e., He whose command is not opposed, according to what He has decreed for us from eternity. Then they gave the reason for that by saying: ﴿Indeed, to Allah we are ardent seekers﴾ — i.e., to Allah alone, who combines all attributes of perfection — ﴿ardent seekers﴾, i.e., deeply devoted in desire; therefore we are content with what comes to us from Him, whatever it may be. That is, it would have been better for them, because nothing reaches them except what Allah, glorified is He, has apportioned to them, whether they wish it or refuse.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 60:

When he had reported their defaming (lamz) of him concerning the charities (sadaqat) and had established what is better for them, guiding them to salvation, he gave the reason for the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) action in them and made clear that he would do nothing else, because it is the truth, and in his most perfect law nothing other than it is permissible. They defamed him, or they abandoned (it), or they were indifferent or eager. So he said, using the particle of restriction (adat al-qasr) in respect of what has been mentioned: ﴿Charities are only﴾, that is, this category, with all the individual items that fall under it. Apparently he put the more important first and then the less important. Hence al-Shafi'i said that the poor (faqir) are the neediest, because he began with them. He said: ﴿for the poor﴾, that is, those who have nothing, or who have something that does not suffice for their needs; ﴿and the needy (masakin)﴾, that is, those who have no sufficiency, as evidenced by ﴿As for the boat﴾ [al-Kahf: 79], and ﴿a needy person in misery﴾ [al-Balad: 16]. (p-505) Its restriction indicates that the unrestricted term is other than this. ﴿And those employed to collect them﴾, that is, the trusted agents in the administration and authority over collecting them. ﴿And those whose hearts are to be reconciled﴾, that is, so that they may embrace Islam, or so that through them others may embrace Islam, or so that they may remain steadfast in their Islam. al-Bukhari in the Tafsir section and others narrated from Abu Sa'id (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "Something was sent to the Prophet (ﷺ) and he divided it among four people and said: 'I am reconciling their hearts.' A man said: 'You have not been just!' He said: 'There will come forth from the progeny of this man a people who will pass through the religion (as an arrow passes through its target).'" In another narration: "A man asked his permission to strike his neck, and he said: 'No, leave him; for he has companions, such that one of you will consider his prayer insignificant in comparison with their prayer.'" The hadith (continues). "And if I were to encounter them, I would surely kill them as (the people of) 'Ad were killed." It should not be said that the reason requires their killing and not refraining from them, for his action in the Khidri station, as previously mentioned, shows that there is no honour (karamah) given to any prophet except that the Prophet (ﷺ) has its like, or something higher than it, either personally or through one of his community.

When he had finished with these four categories, whose members receive the charity into their hands to dispose of it as they wish, as indicated by the use of the preposition li- (for), he mentioned those who are given the charity to settle what is upon them, as indicated by the use of the expression "fi" (in) (p-506). So he said: ﴿And in the necks (ar-riqab)﴾, that is, and for slaves seeking manumission (mukatabin), by means of freeing their necks from bondage. ﴿And the debtors (gharimin)﴾, that is, those who have borrowed in what is not disobedience; what is given to them is spent only on the payment of their debts. ﴿And in﴾, that is, and for those who strive in ﴿the way of Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom the entire command belongs, by way of expenditure, conveyance, and assistance with weapons and other things. Al-Qaffal transmitted from some jurists that they generalized the "way" (sabil) and permitted spending it on all good purposes, such as shrouding the dead, building mosques, and the like. ﴿And the wayfarer (ibn as-sabil)﴾, who is the traveller cut off from his land; he is given what will convey him there. In this there is an indication that our Messenger (ﷺ) did not do what led to their defaming him on account of it except by a true command. For we have appointed for him the recipients of the charities, so he does not deviate from them for anything at all, because he stands by what pleases Us. If they are among them he gives to them, and otherwise he withholds from them. Whoever is pleased is pleased, and whoever is angry is angry. He has ordained this. Or it is established for the poor, with it being ﴿an obligation﴾, that is, existing ﴿from Allah﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, because of His knowledge that in this is the greatest benefit. This is like a warning against opposing the apparent meaning. ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses all the attributes of perfection, ﴿is All-Knowing﴾, that is, of absolute knowledge of what sets right the religion and the world and brings together the hearts of the believers. ﴿All-Wise﴾, that is, He (p-507) makes His acts so firm that none other can undo them. Abu Hayyan said: "innama" (only), if it was laid down for restriction, then the restriction is derived from its wording; and if it was not laid down for restriction, then the restriction is derived from the attributes, since the ruling being tied to an attribute requires that it be the cause, and causation by something requires limiting the ruling to it."

The wisdom of zakat, from the side of the owner, is that wealth is loved, because it obtains what is loved, and persistence in loving it leads to turning away from Allah, the Giver of it. So it was part of the wisdom to remind the owner of it of the true Owner, in that He obligated him to give out a portion of it, so that the soul's complete absorption in it is restrained, the soul is purified of its love for it, and it is purified from merely spending on desires. From the side of the recipient, since his need for it and the need of the owner (even if only possibly) come together, there are two causes for having authority over the wealth: one is the owner's acquisition of it, and the second is the recipient's need for it. Both causes are observed to the extent possible: the owner prefers to keep the greater part and gives the lesser part to the recipient. al-Shafi'i applied the verse according to its apparent meaning and said: if the owner of the wealth gives it out himself, the share of the collectors drops out along with the share of those whose hearts are to be reconciled, and it is spent on the eight categories; if the imam divides it, then it is spent on seven, and it is obligatory to give three persons from each category; and if any category is not found, its share is returned to the remaining ones. It is equal among the categories, not among the individuals within a category. Abu Hanifa said: it is permissible to spend the whole of it on one of the categories, because the verse only requires that the charity not be taken out from them, not that it be spread across all the categories. This is also the view of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Hudhayfah, Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ata', Abu al-Aliyah, and Maymun ibn Mihran (may Allah be pleased with them all).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 61:

When he had explained the two previous categories and concluded their affair with the attributes of knowledge and wisdom, he followed them with another category, one who harms by doing what makes a deficiency in the attributes of the Messenger (ﷺ). Thus, the accusation against the knowledge and wisdom of the One who sent him is inevitable. So He said: ﴿And among them are those who harm the Prophet﴾, i.e., the one whose rank Allah has exalted. He informs him of what He wills of the hidden secrets. When He had informed of harm in general, encompassing speech and action, He joined to it His saying: ﴿and they say, "He is an ear"﴾, i.e., because of his excessive listening to what is said to him. Their meaning is that he believes everything he hears and accepts the word of everyone, just as the spy is called "an eye." Abu Hayyan said: Khidham ibn Khalid, Ubayd ibn Hilal, al-Jullas ibn Suwayd, and others were harming the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Some of them said, "Do not do this, for we fear that it will reach him and he will strike us." Al-Jullas said, "Rather, we will say whatever we wish, for Muhammad is a listening ear. Then we will come to him and he will believe us." So this was revealed. It has also been said otherwise.

"A man is an ear (rajul udhun)" if he listens to the speech of everyone; the word applies to the singular and the plural alike. End of quotation. Their meaning is that he (ﷺ) does not know the deceit of one who schemes against him or the trickery of one who deceives him. They lied. He is the most knowledgeable of people in this, but he turns away at times of benefit, which is not fitting for the excellences of the religion other than this. Allah, exalted is He, explained this with His saying: ﴿Say, "An ear of good for you"﴾. Then He explained that the benefit of this returns to them with His saying: ﴿for you﴾. Then He elucidated that with His saying: ﴿He believes﴾, i.e., he brings about belief for the angels who come to him from Allah, by turning away from denial, in that he confirms them, acknowledging ﴿in Allah﴾, i.e., because of what they inform him of concerning Him, with the true faith, because of his perfect knowledge of the attributes of majesty and generosity that belong to Him, glory be to Him. The sum of it is that the act of believing is implicit within the act of confirming (taṣdīq). Then the verb was omitted, and from it a circumstantial state (ḥāl) was extracted and placed in its stead; then that was omitted and a complement indicating it was brought, as they said concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and that you may glorify Allah for having guided you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], that the implied meaning is: "praising Him for having guided you." So the implied meaning here is: "he believes, confirming in Allah." This is its reality, and it produces the love and loyalty of the believers. For this reason He followed it with His saying: ﴿and believes for the believers﴾, i.e., the steadfast ones. He brings about belief for them, in contrast to denial, by confirming them in everything they inform him of that admits of confirmation. This is for the sake of their welfare and to bring them together, along with what is established of their truthfulness. For if he were to hold them to his own intellect and the extent of his knowledge, he would love the liar and punish the traitor merely on the basis of his knowledge and his discernment, and most minds would fall short of that, and most conjectures would go astray because of it. Hearts would be repelled, and accusation would generally arise.

When the confirmation of the existence of God, with all His attributes of perfection that require command and prohibition, was governed by the particle bi- (بِ), here the confirmation was merely for the sake of informing about whatever it was, so it was governed by the particle li- (لِ). And by restricting the verb, though it is transitive, it indicates an emphasis on confirmation, to the point that it is as though there were no confirmation other than this.

When He, glory be to Him, explained that His confirmation, both outwardly and inwardly, is only for the steadfast in faith, He explained that His confirmation of others is only outward. So He said: ﴿and mercy﴾, i.e., and he is a mercy ﴿for those who believe﴾, i.e., who manifest faith with their tongues ﴿among you﴾. This, Allah knows best, is an indication of the hypocrites and those in their position, whose tongues are firm but whose hearts are unsteady. That is, manifesting their confirmation by accepting what appears from them, and concealing their shameful secrets, is a cause of restraint from their blood. And the believers' display of their scorn for them may perhaps be a cause for the sincerity of their faith, as they witness the excellences of faith over the passage of time. It is not unlikely that the expression in the past tense indicates the hypocrites, especially after the expression with the active participle (ism al-fā'il). Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Harrali said in his book "al-Miftah" the following text:

"Chapter Four: on the levels of exposition concerning the development of the human being through his advancement in the stages of faith and his decline into the depths of disbelief. Know that Allah encompasses everything in creation and command, first and last, outward and inward, and He is praised. He has exaltedness in the manifestation of His command and the greatness of His creation, and concealment in contrast to that from His creation and command, through what He has manifested of His wisdom and the causes of His guidance and His trial. That exaltedness is His divinity (ilāhiyyah), and that concealment is His kingship (mulk). Between them is the establishment of every creation for what it was created, and the support of every command from both for what it was established. That is His lordship (rabbāniyyah). For every splitting (fatq) of His creation and command there is a prior joining (ratq).

For every difference there is equality, and that is His compassion of the All-Merciful (raḥmāniyyah). For every nearer one within the extent of the veil there is special favor; that is His mercy of the Most Merciful (raḥīmiyyah). For every farther one within the extent of the veil there is a severe grasp from Him in returning him to nearness, and that is His vengeance (niqmah). For every one of His exalted descents, outward and inward, there is a particular command, and for every command there is a creation. The explanation of the Qur'an comes to every creation according to the reality of its essence, the special rank of its nearness, and the place of its distance. Allah, glory be to Him, made Adam and his offspring vicegerents for Him in all His command and its details, and sent down the Qur'an as a building upon the totality of that. The lowest state for this vicegerent is the station in which he is called 'man' (insān), namely when he is at ease with himself and with others and forgets the covenant of his Lord. For this reason the Qur'an describes him with blame: ﴿Woe to man, how ungrateful he is!﴾ [ʿAbasa: 17] ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful to his Lord﴾ [al-ʿĀdiyāt: 6]. Then comes the station in which he is given a chance, where he is alert to hearing the reprimand of his Lord. For him this is like the age of discernment for a boy of seven. It occurs only through gathering and mutual observation, and this is the age in which they are called 'people' (nās), from their nawS, that is, their oscillation between hearing the reprimand of their Lord and the dominance of their desires over them. For this reason the Qur'an builds their blame upon the censure of most of them: ﴿But most people do not know﴾ [al-Rūm: 6], and 'do not give thanks.' Then comes the station in which acceptance, hearing, and faith in the unseen of the command and creation are realized for them, but they waver from it greatly at every occurrence of attainment and every deceptive elevation. For them this is like the age of the one who has reached puberty, who has tasted the emergence of the seed from his inner self, and whose intellect rises to examine the realities of sensible things. This is the age in which the phrase 'those who believe' (alladhīna āmanū) is directed, and it is the first age of receptivity. Therefore, all the etiquette of the Qur'an and its instruction are directed to the people of this age. Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: 'When you hear Allah, mighty and majestic, say, "O you who believe," give it your ear, for it is either good that He commands you to, or evil that He forbids you from.' Just as what concerns the mature, rational adult does not include the discerning child, and what concerns the discerning child does not include the adult, likewise the address of 'those who believe' has not yet reached people, and the address to people has passed beyond 'those who believe,' because they have been restrained by what their hearts accepted from what people are restrained from, and they have complied with what people comply with. These stages are known to the people of insight, and their specific address is more manifest than the ages of the bodies to those who see. The lack of insight into these levels of conditions and exposition is the locks upon the hearts that prevent contemplation of the Qur'an. Likewise, above the age of 'those who believe' is the age of 'those who have faith' (alladhīna yu'minūn), and they are at the first limit of nearness, a station equivalent to reaching maturity (ashudd). The age of 'those who believe' and of 'people' is within the extent of the limit of distance, and for this reason they are addressed with the particle 'yā' (O), which is used for the limit of distance: ﴿O you who believe, shall I guide you to a commerce that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 10] ﴿You believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 11]. Above that is the age of the believers, nearer in proximity. For this reason, the particle of distance 'yā' is not used in the Qur'an in addressing them. This age is equivalent to middle age and the age of gray hair, and the complete age of theirs is 'the believers in truth.' Likewise, up to the age of 'the good-doers,' and to the unseen age of ﴿those who have certainty﴾ [al-An'ām: 75], and beyond that. For the ages of the body are fours (arābī'), and the ages of the heart are weeks (asābī'), known to whoever has developed in them, and unknown to whoever has had the seed of his heart sprout in ignorance while his bodily age has advanced to senility. 'The son of Adam grows old, and two things grow old in him: greed and hope.' Greed is his poverty even if he owns the world, and hope is his anxiety and fatigue. Whoever does not realize the ages of the heart and the variation of its address, the gate to understanding the Qur'an will not open to him. Whoever does not see clearly the descents of the address, the address of Allah will not become distinct to him from the address of the Most Merciful, from the address of the King, the Judge."
