End of quotation.

When He had explained the mercy that belongs to one who confirms him, inwardly or outwardly, He explained the vengeance upon one who denies him and harms him. So He said: ﴿And those who harm the Messenger of Allah﴾, i.e., from among these and from others, ﴿the Messenger of Allah﴾, i.e., the one whom He has manifested, and He is the Supreme King, in his honor and greatness by combining the two descriptions, and He exalted him by attributing him to Himself. He increased his elevation by using His greatest and all-encompassing name. He is an intermediary between the Truth and creation in the rectification of their conditions. So he deserves from them gratitude and honor, not harm and pain.

Since their harm is painful, He made their recompense of the same kind, so He said: ﴿For them is a painful punishment﴾.

Then he gave the reason for that: their contempt for Allah and His Messenger. He informed that they feared for their own lives, so they would correct their outward appearance to protect themselves with false oaths. Thus He said: ﴿They swear by Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses perfect greatness, ﴿to you﴾, that is, that they did not harm the Prophet ﷺ in particular, nor your children by opposing them in general. He stated the ultimate aim of their intention with His words: ﴿to please you﴾.

Since the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was not "an ear" in the sense they intended, he made clear that he was not pleased with their faith, because the truth of it had not settled in his heart; rather, he showed acceptance of their claims regarding the correction mentioned earlier. So He said: ﴿While Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom all command belongs and to whom no one has any share in command, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, that is, the one who is the highest of His creation, and he reached the utmost in exalting him by using the singular pronoun, which indicates the unity of the one being pleased, because whatever pleases either of them pleases the other. So He said: ﴿have more right﴾, that is, to ﴿be pleased﴾. Since the basis of being pleased is obedience, and the core of obedience is faith, He spoke with a descriptive term, because it is the decisive element, saying: ﴿if they are believers﴾, that is, they would know that he has more right to be pleased, and so they would strive for it. This indicates that if they renewed their pleasing of him at all times, it would be evidence of their faith, and if they opposed him, it would be a decisive proof of their disbelief.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 63:**

When he had made clear that their oath was only out of aversion to disgrace in the eyes of the believers, and had shown who is most deserving that they should seek to please him, he established the proof for this in an interrogative form of denunciation and rebuke, making clear that they had fled from a disgrace that would pass and so fell into a disgrace that is lasting. *Al-khizy* (disgrace) is *istihya'* (shame) in *hawan* (humiliation). So he said: ﴿Do they not know﴾, that is, by the indication they have of who is most deserving of being pleased. Since mentioning a thing in vague terms and then explaining it is more emphatic, he used the pronoun of the matter (*ḍamīr al-sha'n*), so he said: ﴿that﴾, that is, the great matter, ﴿whoever opposes Allah﴾, who is the Supreme King, and he makes the opposition manifest by what the *fakk* (the unassimilated spelling, writing the doubled letter separately as *yuhadiddu* rather than *yuhadds*) indicates, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, that is, the one whose greatness derives from His greatness, by acting toward both of them as one who disputes over the *ḥadd* (boundary) of a piece of land, who wants to prevail over his opponent's boundary and force him to be within a boundary other than his own. ﴿Then for him is the fire of Hell﴾, that is, its being his recompense for that is a truth beyond doubt. ﴿Abiding therein﴾, that is, forever without end, just as his intention of opposition was perpetual. Then he drew attention to the greatness of this recompense by saying: ﴿That﴾, that is, the matter far-reaching in description and great in import, ﴿is the great disgrace.﴾

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 64:

When he had given the reason for the act of those who mock, he followed it with the reason for the matter of another category, who were less hypocritical than them, owing to what they had that approximates to affirmation (taṣdīq), and so he said: ﴿The hypocrites are wary that there may be sent down against them a surah﴾. He expressed it with the descriptive form that indicates firm establishment (rusūkh), as a warning to them against even the least degree of hypocrisy, for it drags one on to its greatest degree. ﴿That there may be sent down﴾ — and since the surah that exposes them was a calamity and one of the misfortunes and hardships of time, he used the verb with ʿalā (against), saying: ﴿against them a surah﴾, i.e., a portion of the Qur'an of very strict arrangement (shadīdat al-intiẓām). ﴿Informing them﴾, i.e., telling them with a great and thorough information. ﴿Of what is in their hearts﴾, which they did not reveal to anyone else, or to anyone at all. Perhaps this category used to swear oaths in advance, so that they might cast doubt upon some people or lighten the matter for them if what would expose them descended. It is narrated that they used to say things that led to hypocrisy and indicated it, and they would say: "Perhaps God will not disclose our secret against us." And one of them said, after a statement they had made: "By God, I see us as the worst of God's creation, and I would wish that I were brought forward and flogged a hundred lashes, and that nothing would descend upon us that would disgrace us."

When their wariness together with the action, which is incompatible with it, of speech of hypocrisy, is that of one who mocks, He said, threatening: ﴿Say: Mock!﴾, i.e., act as a mocker with the utmost eagerness. ﴿Indeed God﴾, i.e., the One encompassing complete knowledge and perfect power, ﴿will bring out﴾, i.e., He has the attribute of bringing out, ﴿what you fear﴾, i.e., bringing out from you your ugly deeds. And on the authority of al-Ḥasan: The Muslims used to call this surah "al-Ḥaffāra" (the Excavator); it excavated what was in the hearts of the hypocrites and brought it forth.

When He described them with hypocrisy, He confirmed it by their failure to hasten to repentance, which is the act of the believers, and by their audacity in denial, even though the one questioning them was the one who had reached the utmost in majesty, dignity and perfection. So He said: ﴿And if you ask them﴾, meaning: while you are the one whose questioning must be believed, about what the surah revealed of the disbelief they displayed among themselves. That was when some of them said: "Look at this man, he thinks he will conquer the palaces and fortresses of Syria! Far-fetched, far-fetched!" So Allah informed him, and he said: "Hold the riders back for me." Then he questioned them, and they said: ﴿"We were only﴾, meaning: we said nothing of that, we were only ﴿conversing﴾, meaning: talking without order, ﴿and playing﴾, meaning: about things for which there is no blame upon us, and which lighten for us the burden of the road."

So it is as if it was said: What is said to them when they swear to that, as is their habit? He said: ﴿Say﴾, meaning: to them, as a reproof for their mockery, threatening them, turning away from what they offered as excuse, to inform them that he is not fit to be listened to. He made them as though they confessed to the mockery, since he placed the one mocked at right after the particle of interrogation حرف التقرير (ḥarf al-taqrīr, the interrogative particle used to affirm or confirm a matter). That is only correct after the mockery has occurred and been established, as a rebuke to them in their claim that he is أُذُنٌ (udhun, "all ears," one who believes everything), in the sense they intended, and as a clarification of what is in your showing them acceptance of their claim, from kindness toward them: ﴿Is it Allah﴾, meaning: He who encompasses the attributes of perfection, ﴿and His signs﴾, meaning: which cannot be altered and are not hidden from anyone with sight or insight, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, meaning: whose greatness derives from the greatness of Allah, and who strives for your reform, your honour and your elevation, ﴿you were﴾, meaning: constantly ﴿mocking﴾.

(p-517)

When he established their mockery, it produced His saying: ﴿Do not make excuses﴾, meaning do not exaggerate in establishing an excuse, which is what would clear you of blame, for that will not avail you however hard you strive, because it is certain that ﴿you have disbelieved﴾, meaning by this statement of yours. He indicated, by omitting the preposition (naz' al-khafid, dropping the governing preposition), that their disbelief nullified whatever deeds they had. This was an intensification against those among them who persisted, a warning to him, and a confirmation of the state of one who persists. Then He said: ﴿after your belief﴾, meaning the belief you claimed with your tongues, which was sincere from some of you and hypocritical from others.

Since the situation called for explaining what they came to after their disbelief, whether by repentance or persistence, He made clear that they are of two kinds. One kind has a seal upon its heart, and its repentance and love are not decreed. This is the more honourable kind, and it is what is meant by His saying, with the verb in the passive voice to indicate that the greater concern is the act itself and not a specific agent: ﴿If We pardon﴾, because the words of the King, although they take the form of a condition, point to its certain realisation, so that the difference between the speech of the Exalted and that of the lowly becomes evident. ﴿a group of you﴾, meaning because they are fit for repentance. ﴿We will punish a group﴾, meaning people who are numerous and capable of turning back. Asim read both verbs in the active voice, out of majesty. ﴿because they﴾, meaning because of the fact that ﴿they were criminals﴾, meaning that their earning of sins, which cut them off from good, is a fixed attribute of theirs that does not separate from them. Hence they are not fit for pardon.

The account of this story is that three hypocrites were walking ahead of the Prophet ﷺ during the expedition of Tabuk: two of them mocked the Qur'an and the Messenger, and the third was laughing. It is said they were saying: "Muhammad claims that he will overcome the Byzantines and conquer their cities. How far-fetched that is!" It is also said they were saying: "Muhammad claims that a Qur'an has been revealed concerning our companions who stayed behind in Medina, but it is only his own words and speech." God informed His Prophet ﷺ of this, so he said: "Hold the riders back for me." He summoned them and said to them: "Did you say such and such?" They said: ﴿We were only conversing and playing﴾ [al-Tawba: 65], meaning: "We were only chatting and engaging in talk, as travelling companies do to pass the road with conversation and play." Ibn Ishaq said: The one who was pardoned was a single man, Makhshi ibn Himyar al-Ashja'i. It is said that he was the one who was laughing and did not engage in the talk. He used to walk apart from them and disapproved of some of what he heard. When this verse was revealed, he repented.

He said: "O God, I will not cease to hear a verse recited which makes the skins shiver and the hearts marvel. O God, make my death a killing in Your way! Let no one say: 'I washed him, I shrouded him, I buried him.'" He was then struck down on the Day of Yamama, and no Muslim was there who did not recognise his place of death, apart from him, may God be pleased with him. Perhaps the application of the word "group" (ta'ifa) to him was to honour him and to conceal him, and to give good news of the repentance of others. Perhaps Makhshi was a believer, but his faith was unsteady, and for this reason the expression here is: ﴿Did you disbelieve after your belief?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 106]. This expression is more severe in reproach, especially among the Arabs, because they take pride in steadfastness in whatever matter they choose and disparage recklessness. Perhaps Jullas, the one referred to in the following story, alone or together with others, had not believed as others did among those referred to in it, and had not believed until he repented. For this reason the expression there is: ﴿and they disbelieved after their Islam﴾ [al-Tawba: 74].

Abu Hayyan said: "Ibn Umar said: 'I saw Wadi'a ibn Thabit clinging to the girth strap of the camel of the Messenger of God ﷺ, walking alongside it while the stones were pecking at him, and he was saying: ﴿We were only conversing and playing﴾ [al-Tawba: 65], while the Prophet ﷺ was saying: "Was it God and His signs that you were mocking?"'" The verse.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 67:

When Allah (glorified and exalted is He) had explained the deeds and statements of groups of the hypocrites, some of whom were with him (ﷺ) in the army, which are in the utmost degree of corruption, this may have prompted the question: As for those who stayed behind, had they gone out, what would their condition have been? So He answered that question, and as evidence that the criminality of those whom He did not pardon among them is an inherent trait, He said: ﴿The hypocrite men and the hypocrite women are [all] of one another.﴾ That is, those who displayed faith and concealed disbelief. ﴿Of one another﴾: since their return was to adherence to whim, nature, habit, and blind imitation of the follower among them to the one followed, He said: ﴿of one another﴾, meaning that in the attribute of hypocrisy they are like one body. Their affairs are alike in their statements, their actions, and all their conditions. The purpose is that their state is opposed to the state of the people of faith, and for this reason He explained it by His saying: ﴿They enjoin what is wrong﴾, that is, of what has preceded of corruption, sowing discord among the ranks, and other evil qualities. ﴿And forbid what is right﴾, that is, anything in which there is the exaltation of Islam and its people, desiring by that to cause strife. ﴿And they withhold their hands﴾, that is, they are stingy, so they spend only while being unwilling.

Since it was as if it were said: Did they not fear, by doing that, the swift punishment? He answered with His saying: ﴿They forgot Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, to whom all command belongs and to whom no one shares command. It is possible that this is the cause of what preceded it. Because they went forward in that, He made the following a consequence of it: ﴿So He forgot them﴾, that is, He dealt with them as one who forgets what he disdains, by leaving them out of His mercy. That abandonment was the cause of the descent of His vengeance. Because they were habituated to all these deficiencies, they were singled out for complete wickedness, and He explained that in the style of wonder at their condition, saying, placing the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun for generality and for attaching the judgment to the attribute: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites, they are﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿the defiantly disobedient﴾, that is, those who have gone outside the circle of what would benefit them of obedience, and who are firmly established in that. He knew that had they gone out to fight, they would have done the same as these, equally, because all are of one clay.

(p-521) When He had made clear much of their condition, and the longing to know their outcome grew intense, and since their aim in displaying faith and excusing themselves for their contradictions through emphatic oaths was in fact only to draw near to the believers and seek their affection, hoping to live under their protection and fearing immediate retribution for what they deserved from them through destruction, He made clear that for them, on account of this deception, there is the enduring punishment and the constant expulsion, and He joined with them those who openly disbelieved, to inform that if they were not greater in obstinacy than them, then they are equal. So He said: ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrites, men and women, and the disbelievers﴾, and He framed it in the form of good news, mockingly toward them and to intensify their distress. ﴿The hypocrites, men and women﴾ means: those who conceal their belief. ﴿And the disbelievers﴾ means: those who openly persist in their obstinacy.

Since they were naturally inclined to scowl at the believers and to recoil from them, even if they displayed the opposite, which is affectation, He said: ﴿the fire of Hell﴾, meaning: the fire whose nature is to make its people scowl and meet them with extreme sullenness. ﴿Abiding therein﴾, meaning: there is no escape for them from it. ﴿It is sufficient for them﴾, meaning: it is adequate for them as punishment. But since abiding (khulud) may be used figuratively for a long period, after which there might be relief, He said: ﴿And Allah has cursed them﴾, meaning: He has expelled them and distanced them from His mercy, and He is the King, the All-Knowing, the Wise, to whom no one has any command. Thus He made understood that there is no relief for them. Then He negated every possibility by His saying: ﴿And for them is a lasting punishment﴾, meaning: by both of these matters, a punishment whose only description is permanence, both in this world, through their subjugation by the might of Islam and its noble, distinguished armies, and in the Hereafter, through what none knows in its true measure except Allah, the King, the All-Knowing.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 69 (part 1 of 4):

Since their state was one of attachment to the fleeting world (al-'ajilah), because it is present and available, and of turning away from the outcome (al-'aqibah), because it is absent, resembling the state of those before them among the bygone nations and past generations, He made this clear to them and concluded by explaining the evil of their conditions and the ugliness of their final end, with the vanishing of their deeds. He said, turning to the mode of direct address (uslub al-khitab) because it is more effective in the domain of reproach and more fitting for attracting benefits for the one who repents: ﴿Like those﴾, meaning: the sum of what has passed of your affair, O hypocrites, is that you are like those who [came before]. Since the doer of what is mentioned is only some of those who passed, he affirmed the preposition, saying: ﴿before you﴾, meaning: from the bygone nations. Then he began to explain their condition and mention the aspect of resemblance, saying: ﴿They were stronger than you in power﴾, because the era at that time was closer to the age of youth, ﴿and more abundant in wealth and children﴾. This looks back to His saying: ﴿So do not let their wealth or their children impress you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 55]. ﴿So they enjoyed﴾, meaning: they sought enjoyment and benefit in this world with utmost desire, turning away from the hereafter, ﴿their share (bi-khalaqihim)﴾, meaning: their portion which Allah decreed and created for them. The most fitting course for them would have been to be sustained by it on the journey that is unavoidable toward the Hereafter. ﴿So you have enjoyed your share, as those before you enjoyed their share﴾, meaning: like those who follow their traces and aim for their fire. ﴿As those before you enjoyed﴾ and in the use of His saying ﴿those (alladhina)﴾: since they had not exhausted the past time, he affirmed the preposition, saying: ﴿before you, with their share﴾, explicitly and not in pronoun form, as a warning about their blame for the scant regard they had for themselves, which entails scant reason, since they were inferior to them in power of body, wealth and children, yet did not refrain from enjoyment (al-istimta') and immersion (al-khawd), out of fear of what destroyed those factions despite their strength, of punishment, without any means of benefit reaching them. ﴿And you immersed yourselves﴾, meaning: you went on in your words and deeds, floundering without a straight path (sanan qawim). ﴿As those who immersed﴾, meaning: like their immersion which ﴿they immersed in﴾. This looks back to their saying: ﴿We were only conversing and playing﴾ [al-Tawbah: 65]. Abu Hayyan said: It is borrowed from wading (al-khawd) in water, and it is used only for falsehood, because dealing with truth is in order and system, whereas the affairs of falsehood are only immersion (khawd). From this is his saying ﷺ: "Many a one who wades in the wealth of Allah will have the Fire on the Day of Resurrection."

When this arrangement signaled to them loss, there arose an eagerness to know the outcome of their affair, so he informed of that by His saying: ﴿Those﴾, meaning: the far from good, and the apparent meaning is that it refers to those he described with strength and abundance of wealth and children. ﴿Their deeds have become void﴾, meaning: they were corrupted and thus nullified, ﴿in this world﴾, meaning: by their departure from them and the forgetting of their pleasures, ﴿and the Hereafter﴾, meaning: and in the everlasting abode, because they did not strive for it as it should be striven for. He increased the warning about their distance from what they intended for themselves of benefit, saying: ﴿And those are the ones who are (hum)﴾, meaning: specifically, ﴿the losers﴾, meaning: there is no real loser other than them, because they lost their share in both abodes, and so they lost themselves; there is no greater loser than one who resembles them. Perhaps in the turn to the mode of address there is also an indication warning every hearer against the like of this state, since it is valid that it is intended by this speech, for among the secrets of the Qur'an in its inimitability is that its expression is directed at one thing while its indication encompasses others, by virtue of their sharing the cause of that state or other such traits. The Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Harrali said at the end of ʿUrwat al-Miftah, in explaining the comprehensiveness of the Qur'an for the comprehensiveness of the verse and for every reader who recites it from among the people of understanding and certainty: Know that Allah, glorified and exalted, sent down the Qur'an as a report about all existences, and that everything it reports from the affair of Adam until the time of Muhammad, peace be upon them both, concerning prophethoods, messages, successions, kinds of kings and pharaohs and tyrants, kinds of criminals, and all that befell them of rewards and punishments, from the day of Adam, peace be upon him, until the time of Muhammad ﷺ, which is about six thousand years or so, all of that recurs in its entirety in the day of Muhammad ﷺ, which is about a thousand years or so, in numbers corresponding to numbers and states corresponding to states, for good or evil; for each of the predecessors there is an example that recurs in this final community, as he ﷺ said: "For every prophet before me there is a counterpart (nazir) in my community." Then he ﷺ mentioned counterparts: "The likeness of Abraham is like Abu Bakr, the likeness of Moses is like Umar, the likeness of Aaron is like Uthman, the likeness of Noah is like Ali, the likeness of Jesus is like Abu Dharr." And he ﷺ said: "Indeed I know the counterparts of my community by their names, the names of their fathers and their tribes, the disbeliever and the believer among them, those who have passed, those who exist, and those who will come after, and had I wished to name them I would have done so."

What has turned most of this community away from understanding the Qur'an is their assumption that what it contains of the stories of the earlier ones and the reports of those rewarded and punished among all the people of religions is intended only as news and narrative. Not at all! Its intent is rather admonition and warning, for a repeated observation within this community of counterparts of all those numbers, states and traces. Thus the hearer hears the whole Qur'an from its beginning to its end applying to this community and its leaders, its guided and its misguided. Then the gate of understanding opens for him, the light of knowledge shines upon him, the state of fear (khashyah) takes hold of him, and he sees among the kinds of this community what he heard of the states of the past generations. It is as is said in the well-known proverb:
"It is you I mean, and listen, O neighbor."

[p. 526] Then, when one witnesses the Qur'an's application to the whole community (ummah), and thereby becomes a knower ('alim), a door of ascent (taraqqi) opens for him. His hearing ascends until he finds the whole of the Qur'an, as it applies to the whole community, applying to his own self: to the states of his soul, its changes, the workings of his actions, and the crowding of his thoughts. Thus he hears the Qur'an applying to himself, benefits by hearing all of it, and takes admonition from any verse he hears from it. He seeks its place in his soul and finds it, in some respect, as desire or as dread, as drawing near or as keeping away, toward the highest goals or toward the lowest depths. In this way he becomes a knower ('arif). This is the general purpose of the admonition in this section. Let us take an example that guides toward understanding this application, both in its general sense to the whole community and in its specific sense to the individual reader-listener's own self (in gnosis). Know that the foundations of the religions that are doubled, which have not ascended to the firm realities of the believers, and those above them among the virtuous (muhsinun) and the certain (muqinun), whose totality lies under the protection of the King, of recompense, and of debt, namely those whom the terror of death frightens first, then the terror of the Resurrection second, and then what the Day of Religion comprises of the horrors of its fifty standing-places, each standing-place of which is a thousand years, in a day whose measure is fifty thousand years. The number of these religions is seven. None of them exists except that it is found in one category of this community. You will find it considered in its own self at some time, in few or many instances, continuously or fleetingly, weakly or strongly, following a dominant religion or as a passing glance of the eye. These seven religions are: the religion of "those who believe" (alladhina amanu) from within this community, who have not realized the reality of faith so as to be among the believers for whom faith has become a firm attribute in their hearts, the monotheists who disavow power and strength, who realize its meaning, acknowledging that God empowers them with what He wills and not with what they will:

﴿Those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely﴾ [Al-Anfal: 2]

﴿Those are the believers in truth﴾ [Al-Anfal: 4]

As for "those who believe" (alladhina amanu), they are those who do not remain steady in the state of their faith, but are so at one time and otherwise at another. Therefore they are those addressed, commanded, and forbidden throughout the Qur'an, those to whom the call is repeated many times within a single surah, such as what His saying, exalted is He, makes clear:

﴿O you who believe, fear God and be with the truthful﴾ [At-Tawbah: 119]

up to His saying, exalted is He:

﴿O you who believe, whoever of you turns back from his religion﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 54]

[p. 527] and what lies between them, such as His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed﴾ [An-Nisa': 137]

These are the people of a firm religion, who are joined with those who have no firmness of the religions of the past. They are joined with those who have a basis of soundness among the three religions, as in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Christians, and the Sabians, whoever believes in God and the Last Day﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 62]

They are also joined with those who altered their religions and who invented a religion for which God sent down no authority, as in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associated [others with God]﴾ [Al-Hajj: 17]

This is the first religion. The second religion is the religion of those who were Jews, among whom are those who were entrusted with the Torah but did not carry it, and those who inherited the Book, who take the goods of this lower world and say, "We will be forgiven," and if the like of those goods comes to them, they take it; and those who write the Book with their own hands and then say, "This is from God"; and those who envy people for what God has given them of His bounty; and those who consume usury though they were forbidden from it; and those who took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God, and the Messiah, son of Mary. The third religion is the religion of those who say, "We are Christians," among whom are those who strayed from the right path, who exceeded the limits in their religion, who spoke against God other than the truth, and who took their monks as lords besides God, and the Messiah, son of Mary. The fourth religion is the religion of the Sabians, among whom are those who deify the stars, the worshippers of the sun, the moon, and the planets, and those who alter them. They are, in order, the first who worshipped a sensible celestial object. The fifth religion is the religion of the Magians, the dualists, who made two gods, light and darkness, and who worshipped a sensible celestial horizon. The sixth religion is the religion of those who associate partners, namely those who worshipped a sensible earthly thing not depicted in image, which is idolatry (wathaniyyah) [worship of unimaged objects], or depicted in image, which is the worship of statues (sanamiyyah). These are the six religions, completing the count of six for what has come concerning it. As for the seventh religion, know that God, glory be to Him, always made the seventh a comprehensive gathering of the six, whether good or evil. So the seventh religion is the religion of the hypocrites, whose outward is with those who believe and whose inward is with one of the remaining five religions mentioned, down to the lowest religion of its associators. They are those who, when they meet those who believe, say, "We believe," and when they go alone to their devils, they say, "We are with you."

These seven religions are repeated in their totality in this community, in a manner similar to what occurred before among the earlier nations. This is the content of the comprehensive hadith that mentions this, in his saying (ﷺ):

"You will surely follow the ways of those nations before you, span by span and cubit by cubit, so that even if one of them had entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it." They said, "O Messenger of God, like the Persians and the Romans?" He said, "And who are the people other than they?"

What the Prophet (ﷺ) explained in this hadith is part of the meaning of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Like those before you, they were stronger than you in power and greater in wealth and children, and they enjoyed their share, and you have enjoyed your share as those before you enjoyed their share, and you have plunged as they plunged﴾

Those of these seven religions, or some of them, are the ten ('amarah) [the seven] of the seven levels of Hell, in their order. The completely saved and the completely successful are the believers, those above them among the virtuous and the certain. [p. 529] Further elaboration on this, and a restatement of the matter, will be made clear, God willing, through aspects that follow the paths of groups within this community in the manner of those who preceded them in this.

As for the aspect of the repetition of the religion of the associators in this community: it is through their taking idols and deities that they worship besides God, sensible and inanimate, just as the polytheists took idols and images of stone and wood. This community has taken idols and images in a subtler and more hidden manner, for they have taken the dinar and the dirham as idols, and the ingots and the hacked silver as images, insofar as the idol (sanam) is that which has a form, and the image (wathan) is that which has no form. He (ﷺ) said: "The idol of my community is the dinar and the dirham." And he (ﷺ) said: "Every nation has a calf, and the calf of my community is the dinar and the dirham." So there is no difference between the polytheist's supposition that the idol he made with his own hand benefits him, and the supposition of the deluded among this community that what they have gained of dinars and dirhams benefits them, until their proverb indicates: "Nothing benefits you except your dirham."

﴿They swear by God that they did not say [it], but they did say the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their submission﴾ [At-Tawbah: 74]

There is no verse revealed concerning the polytheists, in mention of their states, the clarification of their misguidance, and the details of their secret and public conduct, except that it applies to every person deluded by his dinar and dirham. The position of the polytheists' saying about their idols, "We worship them only that they may bring us near to God in position" [Az-Zumar: 3], is similar to the position of the parallel saying of the deluded: "I love wealth only so that I may do good with it and spend it on the ways of righteousness." Yet had he intended righteousness, leaving off earning and accumulating wealth would have been more righteous for him. He (ﷺ) said: "What destroyed those before you was the dinar and the dirham, and they will destroy you." So whoever loves them and is impressed by gathering them is the associator of this community, and they are his al-Lat and al-'Uzza, which nullify for him the saying "There is no god but God," because he has made his wealth a god. He (ﷺ) said: "There is no god but God is salvation for the servants of God from the punishment of God, as long as they do not prefer the bargain of their worldly life over their religion." So whoever finds a touch of this in himself, let him listen to all that was sent down concerning the polytheists in the Qur'an, applying to him, descending upon him, and surrounding him, until God frees him from his shirk, just as He freed those brought out of darknesses into light among the earlier ones. This deluded polytheist is then freed, with his own darkness that veiled the weakness of his faith, into the clear light of faith, in the meaning of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿That He may bring out those who believe and do righteous deeds from darknesses into light﴾ [At-Talaq: 11]

This is an aspect of elaboration that clarifies something of the repetition of the religion of associationism in this community. As for the aspect of the occurrence of Magianism and its counterpart in this community, it is the people's consensus on seeing their actions as originating from themselves, whether good or evil, and their attributing God's actions to His creation, such that their beliefs are firmly fixed that so-and-so does good, so-and-so does evil, so-and-so gives, so-and-so withholds, so-and-so is better than me, so-and-so gave me. Until they have filled the registers with poems, sermons, and letters praising God's creatures for what they did not do, and blaming them for what they did not withhold. They thank the creation for the provision of God and blame them for what God did not give them, and they deviate in His names, until one writes to another: "My master, my support, and the best of my resources, your servant and your slave." By this they nullify the brotherhood of faith and deny the equality of the creatures of the Merciful, and they claim for themselves the actions of God, saying, "We did, we made, we did well, we punished." This is a Nimrodian word, which gave them what they did not perceive as God's particular prerogative in it, like the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord, when God gave him the kingdom, when he said, "I give life and cause death" [Al-Baqarah: 258]. This is pure Magianism and pure Qadarism, with which the religion of Islam cannot be sound, because the Muslim is one who submits all creation and command to his Lord.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 69 (part 3 of 4):

﴿I have submitted my face to God, and [so have] those who follow me﴾ [Al 'Imran: 20] ﴿Surely His is the creation and the command﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]. Anything other than this is Qadariyya (the Qadariyya, those who deny divine predestination), and they are the Magians (majusiyya) of this Umma, since they attributed to the servant a share in the act of the Lord and attributed to him, alongside Him (exalted is He), power, strength, will, choice and management. They did not know that predestination (taqdir) prevents management (tadbir), and that He (exalted is He) is the One who manages the affair from the heaven to the earth. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The Qadariyya are the Magians of this Umma." So everything that God (mighty and majestic is He) revealed in the Qur'an, the comprehensive book that mentions all the religions and creeds, of the words that He attributed to someone who divided the acts between the Truth and the creation, whether a speech of a tyrant (dhu far'ana), or of a Nimrodian, or of a man of authority, the one who believes in it has a share of that praise and blame according to the degree of his immersion and absorption in those whom they claimed had partners with Him, so they feared them and hoped in them. Thus every person who fears or hopes in the creation, from among those who believe and submit in this Umma, [p. 532] is one of the Magians of this Umma. Let the listener, then, take what he reads of this as a proof against himself, so that he may ask God (exalted is He) to free him from it, and that he may know that this has always been a proof against him, even if he was not aware of it before.

This is one aspect of the occurrence of Magianism in this Umma. As for the aspect of the occurrence of the Sabians (al-Sabi'a) and their like in this Umma, it is what has prevailed over most of them, and especially its kings, its sultans and those of its leadership: the study of the stars and acting according to what their configuration shows them of good fortune and misfortune, seeking rain through the stars, relying on the seasonal risings (anwa') of the stars, and the heart's devotion to celestial influences, judging and deciding by them, in accordance with what the worldly ones (al-khaliyyun) practise, who know only the outward appearance of the life of this world, and who are heedless of the Hereafter and of caring for it. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Four of my Umma are kufr among them, and they will not abandon them," and he mentioned among them seeking rain through the stars. Thus whoever's fear and hope are attached to the celestial influences, these are the Sabians of this Umma, just as whoever's fear and hope are attached to themselves and to other creatures, these are the Magians of this Umma. And just as whoever's aspiration and hope are attached to their dirham and their dinar, these are the polytheists (mushrikun) of this Umma. And whatever the secret of each group contains of that to which their fear and hope are attached, that is their lord and their object of worship, to which all their deeds are directed. The name of each person is written according to what his heart has come to rest in. So everything revealed in the Qur'an that refutes the opinions of the Sabians is a proof against whoever reads it or hears it without being aware of it, until a people read the Qur'an while it is a warning to them before a severe punishment, and they are unaware, thinking that they are shown mercy through it, and they are the greatest losers.

﴿And it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾ [al-Isra': 82]. From what is specific to this group of Sabian-imitators (al-mutasabbi'a) is what is like His saying (exalted is He): ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be of the certain﴾ [al-An'am: 75], [the verses] mentioning the star, the moon and the sun, down to the verses mentioning their subjection (taskhir), such as His saying (exalted is He): ﴿And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them in the darknesses of the land and the sea﴾ [al-An'am: 97]; ﴿and the sun and the moon and the stars, subjected by His command﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]; ﴿and He subjected for you the sun and the moon, both constant﴾ [Ibrahim: 33]; ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light and determined for it phases that you may know the number of years and the calculation. God did not create that except in truth﴾ [Yunus: 5]; ﴿and that He is the Lord of Sirius﴾ [al-Najm: 49]. All of this is so that God (exalted is He) may turn the fear and hope of the creation away from the spheres and the stars that are subjected, toward the Subjector, the Dominant over His servants, who is established over all of them. This is one aspect of the occurrence of the Sabian error among those who believe and submit in this Umma.

As for the aspect of the occurrence of what has prevailed over this Umma and become widespread in its deeds and conditions, from the excess of groups among them in the pattern of what the Jews and Christians were upon in their disagreement and in the dominance of their conditions, their kings and sultans, over the conditions of their prophets, their scholars and their saints, this is what this Umma has been warned against, and those of understanding have been made aware of its occurrence among them, through something like what is in the meaning of His saying (exalted is He): ﴿And do not be like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them﴾ [Al 'Imran: 105]. And [it is also in] what the Prophet (ﷺ) foretold: "You will certainly follow the ways of those before you, span by span and cubit by cubit, until even if they entered a lizard's hole, you would follow them." And in some of its chains: "Until if there were among them one who openly had intercourse with his mother, there would be such among you." We said: "O Messenger of God! The Jews and the Christians?" He said: "Who else?"

The condition of these two religions grew strong and multiplied in this Umma only because God gave them the Book, the knowledge and the wisdom, and they disagreed about them out of aims and desires and the preference of the goods of this world. They were lenient with the kings and rulers, made lawful for them what God had forbidden and forbade for them what God had made lawful, and used them to reach their aims in transgressing against those whom they envied from the people of truthfulness and uprightness. Oppression spread among them, and their condition became settled upon the likeness of their condition, and punishments like their punishments were imposed upon them. This continued among them from the time the caliphate turned into kingship until the war lays down its burdens and all religions become one religion, and separation returns to the unity of tawhid. Thus whoever selects and restricts himself from this Muhammadan law, which comprises the outward and the inward, to a particular portion of the outward or the inward, and does not combine the two in his knowledge, his state and his gnosis, then he is, by adhering to the outward legal aspect without the reality of its inward, one of the Jews of this Umma, like those who keep to the outward appearances of the conditions by which the world continues according to what pleases the kings and sultans of the age, who neglect the works of the inner secrets, who deny the states of the people of realities, and against whom the attachment of their fear and hope to the people of this world bears witness, those who prefer the goods of this lowly world. By this, the conditions of the Jews appeared in this Umma.

[p. 533] The Bedouins passed with the Prophet (ﷺ) by a green, luxuriant lote tree (sidra). The people of the pre-Islamic age had a lote tree that they venerated, gathered beside, and hung their weapons upon, and they called it Dhat Anwat (the one with hanging things). They said: "O Messenger of God! Make for us this lote tree a Dhat Anwat as they have a Dhat Anwat!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You have said it, by the Lord of the Ka'ba, just as the Children of Israel said: ﴿Make for us a god just as they have gods﴾ [al-A'raf: 138]. Indeed, these are the ways (sunan)!" Thus, wherever the events of the Jews appear, of transgression and envy, and the magnifying of what is magnified for its worldly aspect, and the belittling of the weak believers, there the signs of Judaism are manifest. Likewise, whoever restricts himself from this comprehensive Muhammadan law to an inward aspect, of reforming a state or a heart, while neglecting the outward matter and the totality of goodness and the mutual support of Islam, and is satisfied with what is hidden within and makes light of what is apparent, he is one of the Christians of this Umma, not possessing the criterion (furqan), so how could he be a possessor of the Qur'an? That is because this comprehensive religion stands only by the outward marks of Islam, the emblem of faith in the hearts, the inner states of the soul, and the realities of excellence (ihsan) witnessed, in which the one who does good does not witness anyone with God, and the believer does not believe in anything other than God with God, and the Muslim does not submit to anything beneath Him. By this it is completed. The groups who adhered to the marks of Islam are called the jurists (al-mutafaqqiha), and the groups who adhered to the emblems of faith are called the usulis and the theologians (al-mutakallimun), and the groups who aspired toward excellence are called the Sufis (al-mutasawwifa). So whenever the jurist denies the sincerity of the states of the Sufis, because of some flaw he sees in the conditions of the Sufis, he has adopted the ways of the Jews. And whenever the Sufi does not venerate the jurists, because of some flaw he sees in the condition of the jurist, he has adopted the ways of the Christians. The same applies to the theologian between the two groups, whichever of them he inclines toward. The imams of religion, those whom God has gathered to uphold the marks of Islam, the faith of the people of faith and the witnessing of the people of excellence, whose skins and hearts soften toward the remembrance of God, are followed by the Sufis; and the lights of their hearts appear over the darkness of the ambiguities, so the people of faith follow them; and the complete marks of Islam appear in their deeds, so the people of Islam follow them. ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace"﴾ [al-Furqan: 63]. "The best of people is a believer with good character, and the worst of people is a disbeliever with bad character."

The possessors of the criterion are comprehensive and perceptive. Whoever restricts himself to the outward and denies the inward, the blame of the Jews in what the Qur'an revealed about them befalls him in proportion to his excess and restriction. And whoever restricts himself to the inward without the outward, the blame of the Christians in what the Qur'an revealed about them befalls him.

It is related that a righteous Muslim man entered a church and said to a monk in it: "Direct me to a clean place where I may pray." The monk said: "Purify your heart of all else, and stand wherever you wish." That righteous Muslim said: "I was embarrassed by him." Know that each of these two states is not the state of a possessor of the criterion nor the state of a possessor of the Qur'an. For the possessor of the Qur'an does not feel embarrassed at this saying, because it is his state, and his heart is purified of all besides God. [p. 537] Yet he must still cleanse his outward appearance, because God (exalted is He), just as He is the Inward, loves the purity of inner states, so, since He is the Outward, He loves the righteousness of outward appearances. Thus the possessor of the Qur'an, when called to the purity of the inward, responds and does not hesitate, and when called to the righteousness of the outward, responds and does not delay, for his standing by the criterion and the right of the Qur'an.

It is related that a king, may God have mercy on him, entered the mosque after the 'asr prayer, and he was one who did not hold that prostration (ruku') is permitted after 'asr. He sat and did not bow. A boy said to him: "O shaykh! Stand and bow!" So he stood and bowed, and did not argue with him by what he considered his school of law. It was said to him about that, and he said: "I feared that I might be among those of whom [God says]: ﴿And when it is said to them, bow down, they do not bow﴾ [al-Mursalat: 48]."

«ووَقَفَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ عَلى سِقايَةِ زَمْزَمَ...» The Prophet (ﷺ) stood by the water-supply of Zamzam, where al-ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with him) had prepared basins of fadikh (a drink made from steeped dates). The Muslims were coming to drink from it, having dipped their hands into it. So the Prophet (ﷺ) leaned forward to drink from their drink. Al-ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said to him: "O Messenger of Allah! Shall we give you to drink from our drink in waterskins?" He (ﷺ) said: "I will drink from these, seeking the blessing of the hands of the Muslims," and so he (ﷺ) drank from it.

So the companion of the Qur'an worships Allah, blessed and exalted is He, with his heart and his body. He does not confine himself to the outward without the inward, nor to the inward without the outward, nor to the first without the last, nor to the last without the first. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "My community is like the rain; one does not know whether its first part is better or its last."

It is therefore the right of the reader to consider the Qur'an itself, to observe the places where it censures (the things that distinguish), and to weigh by it the states of his own soul against these six religions (al-adyan al-sittah) in this community. As for the manner in which hypocrisy arises and the states of the hypocrites, it is the great calamity of the reciters and the blight of the successor (al-khalifah). The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The majority of the hypocrites of my community are its reciters." One of the senior Successors (tabiʿun, the generation after the Companions) said: "I met seventy of those who had seen the Prophet (ﷺ), all of whom feared hypocrisy for themselves."

The root of its entry into people is preferring the sanctity of people over the sanctity of the Truth, out of ignorance of Allah, mighty and majestic, and deception by people. Therefore it is necessary to be courteous outwardly to those of righteousness and truthfulness, while hating them inwardly in the heart. Following from this is the wavering between the two states, with what Allah, exalted, described of their conditions and what the Prophet (ﷺ) explained of their signs, until he (ﷺ) said: "Between us and the hypocrites is the witnessing of the ʿAtamah (the night prayer of ʿIshaʾ) and Fajr; they cannot bear them." And as Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿They do not come to prayer except while they are lazy, and they do not spend except while they are unwilling﴾ [al-Tawbah: 54].

The hypocrite looks at whatever he can use to bring down the virtues of the people of virtue, and he feigns blindness to their good qualities. It has been related that Allah hates the one who abandons a good deed of the believer and takes hold of his bad deed. The sincere believer overlooks the faults of people of faults, so how much more the defects of people of good qualities! Among the most evident signs of the hypocrite is his resentment of the deeds of the sincere, as has been mentioned. There was never a believer in the past, nor a believer in what remains, except that beside him was a hypocrite who hates his deed. And that hypocrite is a backbiter, a slanderer, stingy, cowardly, startled, reluctant in gatherings of goodness, a stranger to them, quick to rush into places of evil and foremost in them, fluent of tongue in backbiting and slander, heavy of tongue regarding persistence in the remembrance of Allah, blessed and exalted, heedless of the remembrance of Allah, mighty and majestic, in every state, looking at people from every direction. Yet with all this he flatters them and does not befriend them. He takes from the religion what benefits him in this world, and does not take what benefits in the Hereafter; and he avoids in the religion what harms him in this world, and does not avoid what harms in the Hereafter, of what does not harm in this world. This is one aspect of the spread of hypocrisy in this community. Therefore it is the right of the reader to sense the positions of whichever part of the Qur'an falls upon his self: in the essence of his heart, in the states of his soul, in the deeds of his body, in his secret with his Lord and in his public dealings with His creation. For by this he finds the whole Qur'an applying to him and specific to him, until it is as if all of it was only sent down to him. When it urges him toward a matter, it urges him toward it from some aspect; when it warns him against a matter, he fears it from some aspect. When it speaks of the high, it is likewise; when it speaks of the low, it is likewise. He does not say: "This was only revealed concerning such-and-such," until he finds for every part of the Qur'an a point of contact in his deed, whatever deed it may be, and a place in his self, whatever state it may be, and an awareness in his heart of whatever observation it may be. Thus he hears the Qur'an as a message from Allah, glorified and exalted, to him, without any intermediary between Him and him. At that point he is close to being among those whose skin shivers at it at first, then whose skin and heart soften at its end. Perhaps he will find from Allah, glorified and exalted, a breath of mercy which opens for him a door to taking on the character of the Qur'an, following the example of the Prophet (ﷺ). "ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) was asked about the character of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and she said: His character was the Qur'an." And by this he is one of great character — and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing. End.

(p-540) When He, glory be to Him, established by this verse their resemblance to others in enjoying the fleeting worldly life, and concluded it with this ending that announces retribution, He followed it by warning them against resembling those among them who were overtaken by what befell them. He shifted to the third-person mode (*maqam al-ghayba*, the mode of absence), because it is more effective in inspiring awe. He said, establishing their loss: ﴿Has there not come to them﴾, i.e., these wicked ones of the people of hypocrisy (*nifaq*), ﴿the report of those before them﴾, i.e., their great account, which is worthy of investigation so that one may act in accordance with what it requires, when they disobeyed Our messengers. Then He substituted for that His words: ﴿the people of Noah﴾, i.e., in the length of their lives, the extent of their traces, and the pleasantness of their settlement through the good enjoyment of their land and their dwellings. He destroyed them by the flood, and none of their disobedient ones was left alive. And He joined to the people of Noah the tribe, saying: ﴿and ʿĀd﴾, i.e., in the strength of their bodies, their great station, their workshops and their buildings, and their tyranny in the greatness of their dominion. He destroyed them by a violent wind, and none of those among them who disbelieved was left as a human being. ﴿And Thamud﴾, i.e., in their establishment in the land of the rock (*al-Hijr*), its breadth and length, its mountains and its plains. They were destroyed by the earthquake, and none of the disbelievers among them was left as a dweller. ﴿And the people of Abraham﴾, i.e., in their possession of the whole earth in its length and breadth. God stripped them of dominion after a severe destruction. ﴿And the companions of Madyan﴾, i.e., in gathering wealth and extending their hopes to take it from both lawful and unlawful sources, and in diminishing the scale and the measure; so God overtook them with punishment. ﴿And the overturned cities (*al-Mu'tafikat*)﴾, i.e., in their turning away from guarding their honor in pursuit of the delights of their desires; so their deeds, after the sinking, bore as fruit their total extinction.

(p-541) When it was as if it had been said: "What was their report?", He said: ﴿Their messengers came to them﴾, i.e., to each nation among them came its messenger ﴿with the clear proofs﴾, i.e., with very clear miracles, because they had committed such abominations as necessitated their destruction. ﴿But﴾, i.e., as a consequence of that, ﴿it was not﴾, i.e., God, with all the attributes of perfection He possesses, was not ﴿intending to wrong them﴾, i.e., to act toward them in destruction before warning and before the manifesting of the clear proofs, in the manner of one whom you regard as a wrongdoer among yourselves. Rather, He sent to them the messengers, but they denied what they brought them of clear proofs; so whoever knows their condition, when he hears of their destruction and their annihilation, says: "God did not wrong them." ﴿But they were﴾, i.e., continually throughout the length of their lives, ﴿wronging themselves﴾, i.e., not others, ﴿by doing what causes their destruction.﴾ So if you do not return, then We warn you of a punishment like theirs. Perhaps He singled out these peoples for mention from among the rest of the nations because of what the Arabs know of their reports and the nearness of their dwellings to the Arabs' dwellings, although they were the most numerous of nations and their prophets were the greatest of prophets. Abu Hayyan drew attention to this. Perhaps He placed the companions of Madyan before the people of Lot, although they came after them in time, because this concerns those who were described as not finding anything to protect them from the punishment they were in, by witnessing the Prophet (ﷺ), whether a refuge, caves, or a shelter. Likewise, the overturned cities were grouped before them with this description. The people of Noah, peace be upon him, when the water came to them, had no impregnable stronghold, nor any lofty mountain to protect them, although it is said that they were the ones who built the pyramids, some of which are of stone to protect them from the calamity with which they were threatened if it was water, and some of which are of brick to protect them from it if it was fire. (p-542) ʿĀd, when the wind came to them, rushed into their houses, so it uprooted the doors and threw them down within the interiors of their houses. Neither the firmly built workshops, nor the lofty palaces, nor the strong fortresses that they had constructed availed them. As for the condition of Thamud, it is well known in their extensive use of houses hewn in mountains and plains, yet these did not protect them from the Cry that followed the earthquake. The people of Abraham, peace be upon him, built the tower (*al-Sarh*), whose height was five thousand cubits, or two farsakhs, so that Nimrod, as he claimed, could reach the heaven by it. God brought their structure down from its foundations; the wind cast its top into the sea, and the remainder fell upon them while they were beneath it, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive. As for the companions of Madyan, when the punishment came upon them and the earthquake seized them, their city did not avail them. If they are the companions of the Thicket (*al-Ayka*), then when the heat grew severe upon them on the day of the cloud, they headed for the caves and found them hotter than the surface of the earth, so they came out of them fleeing. Then the cloud gathered them with a cool breeze that it imagined to them and disguised for them; when they gathered beneath it, its fire burned them, and its shame remained upon them. As for the people of Lot, the command came upon them suddenly, and they did not perceive until their cities were overturned after being raised up to the heaven's firmament, and stones of brimstone blazing with fire were made to follow them. Perhaps He singled out the people of Lot for mention from among those who did not have this description, because the Arabs used to pass by the sites of their cities and witness them. He referred to them as the overturned cities because the stories concern the hypocrites, whose affair is founded on falsehood and on diverting matters from their outward meanings and turning them from their faces. (p-543) The meaning is that those [people of Lot], when they turned the act of intercourse away from its proper face, were punished by the overturning of their cities. These [hypocrites] therefore deserve a punishment like this one, for turning speech away from its proper face. The root *ifk* in all its forms revolves around turning and reversing; when you repay a man, it is as if you reversed his action, returned it to him and turned it away from yourself. The *ukāf* of a beast (the pad on its back) is likened to an upturned vessel. And falsehood is the diverting of speech from its face, so it is *ifk* for this reason. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 71:

When Allah, glorified is He, had made clear that the hypocrites are one another's kind, and what He had promised them, and what followed from it by way of threat to destroy those who resemble them, and concluded with what caused their destruction, namely their persistence and their failure to take heed, He turned to describe the condition of the believers, encouraging repentance and hoping for the likes of their state. So He said: ﴿And the believing men and the believing women﴾, meaning: by what came to them from their Lord, ﴿are allies of one another﴾. He did not say "min" (of) as He said of the hypocrites, "min baʿḍin" (of one another), indicating that none of them imitated another in the foundation of faith, nor agreed with him out of desire; rather, all of them are correct in essence and in primary intent, in following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by definitive evidence according to the understanding of each one of them. This is a proof of the soundness of their faith and its firmness in their submission and acceptance. Then he explained their alliance: that they are one hand against others, like one body, so that when one limb complains, the rest of the body responds to it with fever and sleeplessness. So He said: ﴿They enjoin what is right﴾, meaning: all of them, in a manner of mutual support and aid, ﴿what is right﴾, which is everything the Sharia recognized and permitted, ﴿and forbid what is wrong﴾ (p-544), meaning: likewise, ﴿what is wrong﴾, showing no favoritism toward anyone.

When He mentioned the definitive evidence for the soundness of faith, He followed it with the best of acts of worship, so He said: ﴿And they establish prayer﴾, meaning: they perform it in a manner that requires its standing with all its pillars, conditions and limits, watching over their Lord and seeking help through it in all that befalls them. ﴿And they give zakah﴾, meaning: by way of consolation from them to their poor, a connection to creatures after serving the Creator. This corresponds to His saying of the hypocrites, ﴿and they withhold their hands﴾ [al-Tawbah: 67]. Having singled out the foundations of the religion, He generalized, to make clear that they do not forget Allah for the blink of an eye, but mention Him in every state, by His saying: ﴿And they obey Allah﴾, meaning: the Greatest King, besides whom there is no king, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, indicating the goodness of their conduct and the beauty of their companionship.

When He mentioned the noble qualities of their deeds, He followed it with the goodness of their end, so He said: ﴿Those — Allah will have mercy on them﴾, meaning: those of great station, ﴿Allah will have mercy upon them﴾, meaning: the One who possesses all attributes of perfection, by a promise that admits no failure. This, together with the sentence before it, corresponds to His saying of the hypocrites, ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 67]. It indicates that the path is rugged and the matter is severe and difficult, so the traveler is in need of mercy, which is treatment after forgiveness with honor. He has no ability to cross the wastelands of the road except by it, and no arrival at all without its cause.

When He made clear that the condition of the believers is built upon mutual allegiance, and allegiance needs help, He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, meaning: the One to whom belongs complete encompassment (p-545), ﴿is Mighty﴾, meaning: Overpowering, not overpowered in any respect, so He is able to aid whoever allies with His party and to grant them of the fruits of mercy what He wills, without anyone being able to come between Him and any part of that. ﴿Wise﴾, meaning: none can annul what He has decreed or undo what He has firmly established. In this there is an indication that the believers will continue to be victorious over every corrupter so long as they remain upon these traits of alliance and what accompanies them of praiseworthy qualities.

After concluding the verse with the attributes of might and wisdom, which suit its opening with loyalty (al-muwalat) and its following verse on jihad, and after the promise of mercy in general terms, he followed it with what is more closely fitting to it, as an explanation of mercy and a detailing of it, encouraging the believers with the bounty upon them, in every respect that the hypocrites had sought by their hypocrisy in the life of this world. He added that this bounty is lasting, and he informed that this is the victory and nothing else. So He said: ﴿Allah has promised the believing men and the believing women﴾, that is, the One who is truest in His promise, to whom belongs all perfection, [promised] those who are firmly rooted in affirming everything that the Messenger (ﷺ) brought them. ﴿Gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, that is, they are ever green, possessing a radiant freshness. Since bliss is not complete except with permanence, He said: ﴿abiding therein﴾. The gardens are not pleasing except with dwellings, spacious abodes and retreats. He said: ﴿and pleasant dwellings﴾. Since some gardens are higher than others, and the highest of them is that which has been honoured with the attribute of being "with Him" (al-'indiyya), which indicates nearness to its Builder, a matter that confirms the meaning of permanence, He said: ﴿in gardens of Eden﴾, that is, a lasting abode, tranquillity, soundness of body, good dwelling, residence and origin. (p-546) This is like what He said concerning their opposites: ﴿a lasting punishment﴾ [al-Tawba: 68]. How fitting is the mention of this garden in the context of the expression by the attribute that indicates firm rootedness. It has been reported in a hadith that it is specifically for the prophets, the truthful (al-siddiqun) and the martyrs. Since that is not free from turbidity while permitting some kind of anger, he began, indicating the highest of glorification, saying: ﴿and the good pleasure﴾, that is, a pleasure that no describer can reach, by what the form of intensification points to, even if it were at the lowest degree, by what the indefinite nunation conveys. ﴿from Allah﴾, that is, the One above whom there is nothing greater in their estimation, ﴿is greater﴾, that is, absolutely. So He is greater than all of that, because His good pleasure is the cause of every success, and the joy which is the greatest of bliss does not occur except by the good pleasure of the Master. If the little of it is greater, then what do you think of the abundance of it?

When that was completed in the finest contrast with what He described their opposites by, He said, describing it further as encouragement toward it: ﴿That﴾, that is, this exalted matter, ﴿is﴾, that is, specifically, not anything else, ﴿the great triumph﴾, that is, that before which everything in the affairs of this world and the Hereafter is deemed insignificant. In the fact that this is a promise to those who are characterized by what they are characterized by, there is encouragement toward the jihad commanded after it, since it is one of the instances of enjoining good and forbidding evil, and the greatest summons to loyalty.

When the loyalty of the believers to one another and their separation from the hypocrites and the disbelievers were established, and what had preceded of encouragement and warning was sufficient for turning back to God, and whoever did not return by that, being greatly rebellious and drowned in disbelief, He followed that command with fighting them in a manner befitting their obstinacy. He said, addressing the greatest of those characterized by the aforementioned attributes and magnifying his rank by the most exalted instances of enjoining good and forbidding evil (al-amr bil-ma'ruf wal-nahy 'an al-munkar): ﴿O Prophet﴾, i.e., the one of lofty rank by what constantly renews for him from Us of tidings and what is within Us of knowledge. Since jihad (striving, here armed and verbal struggle) is most recognizable in regard to the openly hostile, and they were more deserving of it because of the severity of their stubbornness and the strength of their souls and resolves, He began with them, saying: ﴿Strive against the disbelievers﴾, i.e., the openly disbelieving, ﴿and the hypocrites﴾, i.e., the secretive ones, each with what befits them of sword and tongue.

Since he ﷺ was naturally disposed to gentleness and was commanded to it, God the Exalted said: ﴿and be harsh upon them﴾, i.e., in both kinds of striving, and do not treat them with the same leniency you showed them when they sought your leave in the matter of contracts. This is unlike what came earlier in the threat against the hypocrites, where He put them first, saying: ﴿the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women and the disbelievers﴾ [At-Tawbah: 68]. Thus in each context He put first what is most fitting to it. Since the meaning is: you will be dominant over them and victorious over them, and they are fodder for the sword and subject to the staff, He followed it with His saying: ﴿and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾, i.e., in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 74:

When he had presented the general proof of their criminality, he followed it with a specific proof of it, which is itself also a proof of a proof, and said: ﴿They swear by Allah﴾, that is, by the King Most High, than whom nothing is greater in rank, ﴿that they said not﴾, that is, that no statement had proceeded from them. Here he restricted the verb (by omitting its object) to generalize the object, informing us that, however much they are rebuked for any statement whatever, they hasten to swear to its denial, falsely, because they have become accustomed to hypocrisy, have acquired the habit of the worst lying (p-548) and have grown used to bad morals. The upshot of this is that they were made to hope for pardon, and were warned of the punishment of those who remain, because of their criminality, since they enjoin the reprehensible and what suits it, following in the footsteps of those before them in indulging in lusts, not refraining out of fear that Allah might strike them with the like of what struck them, and having no hope that He would grant them any of what He has prepared for the believers. They are bold in false oaths, swearing by the greatest name on whatever they are asked about, whether or not it deserves an oath, not fearing that Allah will expose them as He exposed others who did deeds like theirs. Then he indicated the magnitude of their criminality and what is contained in His saying: ﴿The hypocritical men and the hypocritical women are of one another﴾ [al-Tawbah: 67] – the verse – among the greatest of their sins. It is also possible that this verse stands in the position of a rationale for the verse before it: that they put forward, in order to avert what they deserve of jihad, harshness and Hell, the swearing of false oaths denying everything reported of them, showing contempt for Allah and His names, ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 16]. This then serves as an answer to one who seems to say: "As for jihad against the disbelievers, the matter regarding it is clear; but as for the hypocrites, how can they be fought when they rely on the mere word of faith and display the deeds of the people of Islam?" So he said: because they swear, ﴿and they certainly﴾, that is, while they are liars, ﴿said the word of disbelief﴾, that is, the word than which there is no greater disbelief, and it is the denial of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Since this context concerns a category of people who constantly renew their contempt for Allah the Exalted (p-549) through what the present tense indicates at every time, it indicates that their profession of faith is a lie and their deeds are forms without realities. So he expressed it in terms of Islam, saying: ﴿and they disbelieved﴾, that is, they manifested disbelief ﴿after their Islam﴾, that is, by what appeared of their deeds and statements, and that is the utmost wickedness. And since the highest attachment of a person to something is that his soul speaks to him about it with what does not reach it, and that is a kind of frenzy, he said: ﴿and they resolved upon what they could not attain﴾, that is, of killing the Messenger (ﷺ) or expelling him from Medina. Thus they combined all kinds of disbelief: speech, action and belief. It is also possible that it is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun in "their abode". The sense on this reading is: they will enter Hell, swearing by Allah that they did not say the word of disbelief, though they indeed said it. This is like His saying: ﴿Then their trial was only that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [al-An'am: 23].

When he had clarified among their conditions those which only a great matter would prompt them to do, he said: ﴿And they found fault﴾, that is, they said and did while the state of affairs was that they ﴿found no fault﴾, that is, they disliked none of the things that came to them from Allah ﴿except that Allah enriched them﴾, that is, He to whom belong all attributes of perfection and who is independent of the worlds, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, that is, the one who is most worthy of having the grandeur of being attributed to Him, may He be glorified. Their harm to this Prophet (ﷺ) and their resolve to kill him was despite his giving them what enriched them, unlike the preceding verse. So the more fitting way to censure them was to place His saying ﴿of His bounty﴾ later; thus it (p-550) falls under the category of: "and there is no fault in them" (a rhetorical form of praise by exclusion).

When he had alerted that these evils they returned for the good done to them, he encouraged them by saying that He accepts repentance from them, and frightened them by saying that there is no turning back from the punishment He wills, by His saying: ﴿So if they repent﴾. Since the situation was worthy that the listener's longing to know their state should intensify, he deleted the nūn of the verb "to be" (kāna) for brevity, as an alert to this, and said: ﴿it will be﴾, that is, that ﴿better for them﴾ than their persistence.

Since souls, from the original natural disposition, have a strong call toward repentance, and since the Qur'an in its admonition is a deterrent, of acceptable reproach, great in its grip on hearts and its inclination toward minds, he indicated this by the morphological form of the causative (tafʿīl) and said: ﴿And if they turn away﴾, that is, they impose upon themselves the turning away from repentance, ﴿Allah will punish them﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, by His might and strength, ﴿with a painful punishment﴾, that is, one for which they will have no patience, ﴿in this world﴾, that is, by what they are in of fear, disgrace, hardship and other things, ﴿and the Hereafter﴾, that is, with the greater punishment from which there will be no escape for them. ﴿And they have not in the earth﴾, that is, the earth they know nothing beyond, due to the lowness of their aspirations, ﴿any protector﴾, that is, one who manages their affairs, setting right what the punishment has corrupted in them, or who intercedes for them, ﴿or any helper﴾, that is, who rescues them. As for the heaven, they are too insignificant to hope for any helper or anything else from it, and too hard-hearted for their thought to ascend to its wonders and the hosts that are in it. The occasion of revelation of the verse, as Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) said, is that "the Prophet (ﷺ) was sitting in the shade of a tree and said: 'A man will come to you who looks at you with the eye of a devil; when he comes, do not speak to him.' Not long after, a man with blue eyes appeared, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called him and said: 'Why do you and your companions revile me?' The man went off and brought his companions, and they swore by Allah that they had not said it, so Allah revealed the verse." Al-Kalbī said: it was revealed concerning al-Julās ibn Suwayd, and that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) once delivered a sermon at Tabuk, mentioning the hypocrites and calling them filth and reviling them. Al-Julās said: 'If Muhammad is truthful, we are worse than donkeys.' ʿĀmir ibn Qays heard it and said: 'Indeed, Muhammad is truthful, and you are worse than donkeys.' When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to Medina, ʿĀmir ibn Qays came to him and informed him of what al-Julās had said. Al-Julās said: 'He lied about me, O Messenger of Allah!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the two of them to swear at the pulpit. After the afternoon prayer al-Julās stood at the pulpit and swore by Allah, besides whom there is no god, that he had not said it, and that ʿĀmir had lied about him. Then ʿĀmir stood and swore by Allah, besides whom there is no god, that he had indeed said it and had not lied about him. Then ʿĀmir (p-552) (may Allah be pleased with him) raised his hands to the sky and said: 'O Allah! Send down upon Your Prophet the confirmation of the truthful one among us.' The Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers said: 'Amen!' Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended, before the two had parted, with this verse, up to: ﴿So if they repent, it is better for them﴾, that is, the repentance. Al-Julās stood and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! I hear that Allah has presented me with repentance. ʿĀmir ibn Qays spoke the truth in what he said; I said it, and I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted that from him, and he repented and his repentance was good."
