There is no objection to all of that being a cause of it, as has been mentioned and will come. The reading most suited to the causal relation is the first report, because of the expression of disbelief with the definite article "al-" (kufr), which indicates completeness. Whoever reviles our Prophet (ﷺ) has committed every kind of disbelief. In the verse there is evidence for the acceptance of the repentance of the zindīq (one who conceals disbelief and displays faith), as Abū Ḥayyān said, and he said: this is the position of Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī. Mālik said: it is not accepted; but if he comes repentant of his own accord before he is discovered, his repentance is accepted.

When He, glory be to Him, had established the proof for what was mentioned in this verse, which He concluded by saying that He had enriched them from His bounty, He followed it with establishing the proof for that, for their withholding their hands, and for their audacity in the most abominable lying. So He said: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾, i.e., the One than whom there is nothing greater, ﴿If He gives us﴾, i.e., of His good that is with Him, and an acknowledgment, by His saying, that no one has any right over Him (p-553), ﴿from His bounty﴾, i.e., by whatever means, whether trade, spoils, agriculture, or otherwise. He emphasized it because he is a liar who thinks that people will call him a liar, and so is every liar. So He said: ﴿we will surely give charity﴾, i.e., from what He has given us, without showing off, as indicated by the *idgham* (assimilation of doubled consonants), ﴿and we will surely be among the righteous﴾, i.e., for every good to which we are urged.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 76:**

﴿So when He gave them of His bounty﴾ He repeated His saying ﴿of His bounty﴾ as an affirmation of what the covenanters had said, to emphasize the announcement that no one has any right over Him, that no one has any role in what He bestows, and that no one has any power over it in any way. ﴿They were stingy with it﴾, meaning: they lied concerning what they had covenanted and had confirmed it with the utmost emphasis. So they did not give charity; rather, they withheld the due right, the obligation of which was to make it manifest, let alone secret charity. ﴿And they turned away﴾, meaning: they imposed upon themselves turning away from obedience to the One who had bestowed favor upon them, while knowing the ugliness of breaking a covenant. Since turning away may be understood as referring only to what is in the body, He said: ﴿while they were withdrawing﴾, meaning: with their hearts. Withdrawal is a characteristic that is inherent in them and did not newly arise for them; rather, it was a natural disposition in them, and we know of it from the time they made the covenant. Abu Hayyan said: al-Dahhak said: "They are Tha'labah ibn Hatib, Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, Jadd ibn Qays, and Nabtal ibn al-Harith, and the verse was revealed concerning them." End of quotation.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 77:

Its being linked to what precedes it is also excellent in that the first (sin) was ingratitude for the blessing of wealth without a covenant, whereas in this one it is ingratitude for it together with a covenant. This is an ascent from the lower to the higher. The great status of the covenant is also indicated by the magnification of the recompense for breaking it, in His words: ﴿So He caused them to follow up* (their failure)﴾, i.e., God, or persistence in miserliness, as a recompense for that, ﴿with hypocrisy﴾ firmly rooted ﴿in their hearts﴾, meaning that they will not cease saying what they do not do ﴿until the day they meet Him﴾, i.e., with death, at the moment when there is no further opportunity ﴿because they failed God﴾, i.e., He who is the Supreme King, ﴿in what they promised Him﴾, because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Since breaking a promise is extremely ugly, and its perpetrator is not restrained from outright lying, He said: ﴿and because they used to lie﴾, i.e., they constantly renewed their lying in making promises and in what is separate from them. Thus they had completed hypocrisy: they covenanted and betrayed, they promised and broke their word, they spoke and lied.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 78:

When the covenant was a cause of material enrichment outwardly, and that could be a likely occasion for one who has no knowledge to suppose that this was because the inner matters were hidden from Him, glory be to Him, and since the ruling here was directed at the heart's hypocrisy, which is the most vile of morals, while its possessor is unable to rid himself of it, that was the strongest proof that He, exalted is He, knows what is in every heart concerning the owner of that heart. So He followed that with a rebuke against the one who does not know this, a reproach and a censure, and said: ﴿Do they not know that Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿knows their secret﴾, which is what their breasts conceal, ﴿and their private counsel﴾, i.e., what some of them confer about with others; nothing of it is hidden from Him. ﴿And that Allah﴾, i.e., the One who has complete encompassing knowledge, ﴿is the Knower of the unseen﴾ (p-555), i.e., all of it. That is: do they not know that He, exalted is He, is not deceived, due to His knowledge of the outcomes, so that they would fear His consequence and fulfill their covenant with Him? The benefit of giving [the covenant] despite His knowledge of the betrayal is the establishment of proof. Abu Hayyan said: ʿAli, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman and al-Hasan read ﴿Do you not know﴾ with the letter *ta'* (tā'), and it is an address to the believers in the manner of affirmation. End.

The benefit of the shift (*iltifāt*) is an indication that this knowledge benefits only the one who is prepared for faith.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 79:

When God, exalted is He, informed that the ingratitude for the blessing of wealth had not sufficed for them without a covenant, until they committed ingratitude by withholding what was obligatory despite the covenant, He informed that this likewise had not sufficed for them, until they overstepped it to the defamation of the generous who spend, by way of their love for their Lord, what He had not made obligatory upon them. So He, exalted is He, said, expressing it in a form that applies to all of their categories of the past, for the sake of conveying that they were all characterized by this, even if only some of them said it: ﴿Those who find fault﴾, i.e., who defame in secret, ﴿with the volunteers﴾, i.e., those upon whom there is no obligation regarding their wealth, so they give charity and love to conceal their charities, which is what the idghām (assimilation of the doubled letter) indicates, ﴿among the believers﴾, i.e., the firmly established in faith, ﴿concerning the charities﴾. And since what has passed included both the wealthy and the poor, He specified the poor for the sake of increasing their merit, and as an indication that urging toward a little good is like urging toward much of it. So He said, joining by conjunction to ﴿the volunteers﴾: ﴿and those who find nothing﴾, i.e., of wealth, ﴿except their effort﴾, i.e., their capacity, in which they strained themselves until they reached it.

Since al-lamz (fault-finding) is defamation, and it looks to concealment like al-ghamz, and its root in every arrangement revolves around necessity, the meaning is: they impose a defect upon the volunteers and do not make this apparent to everyone, but rather whisper about it among themselves. It returns to mockery and derision, so He made the following a consequence of it: ﴿so they ridicule them﴾. And since there is nothing greater for a person than that the Mighty One take up vengeance for him against his oppressor, He said: ﴿God ridicules them﴾, i.e., He is the One to whom all command belongs and there is no command for other than Him, ﴿them﴾, i.e., He requited them for their deed with people of His party. And He added to it His saying: ﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾, i.e., because of what they used to hurt hearts with that. And when they are confronted about it, they ward off from themselves what would deter them from it with false oaths. Al-Bukhari related in the Tafsir, "From Abu Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When we were commanded to give charity, we used to carry loads (to earn money for it). Abu 'Aqil came with half a sa', and someone else came with more than that. The hypocrites said: Indeed Allah is not in need of the charity of this one, and this other one did not do it except for show. So there was revealed: ﴿Those who find fault...﴾ the verse."

When the Prophet (ﷺ) was known for his great forbearance and gentleness, which is what is indicated by ﴿May Allah pardon you. Why did you give them leave?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 43], this was out of his earnest striving to win them over and his eagerness for the salvation of all creation. He was therefore known for seeking forgiveness for them, at times specifically, by asking forgiveness for them when they offered excuses and swore oaths, and at times generally, when he sought forgiveness for all the Muslims. Allah, exalted is He, informed him of the outcome of the matter in a way that would make him averse to them (p-557), so that he would turn away from them entirely and completely. This was because they had transgressed the right of Allah by abandoning jihad and withholding charity, and the right of the Prophet (ﷺ) by finding fault with him concerning the charities and describing him with what is far beneath him, and they had transgressed the rights of the mujahidin, over whom He, glorified is He, is the Successor in their persons, their families, and their wealth. Moreover, it had already been decreed in His knowledge concerning the hypocrites that He would not forgive them. So He said: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾, meaning: seek forgiveness for them. ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or not﴾, meaning: your asking forgiveness for them and your not asking are equal in their case. ﴿If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times﴾, meaning: if you ask for forgiveness for them, ﴿Allah will not forgive them﴾. This is either literal or hyperbolic. Since the statement that the two matters are equal, namely seeking forgiveness and abandoning it, could be a consequence of forgiveness and could also be a consequence of perdition, He specified the second possibility when He said: ﴿Allah will never forgive them﴾, meaning: the One who has decreed their wretchedness, whose command cannot be averted, ﴿for them﴾. This may be a response to the imperative, and the response to the conditional is omitted because it is indicated by it. The intended meaning of "seventy", according to what became apparent in the outcome, is hyperbole regarding the fact that He will not forgive them for anything at all. Had He forgiven them for anything, it would have been in acceptance of the intercession of His Prophet (ﷺ). The Arabs use hyperbole with anything that contains the word "seven", because it is an ultimate, exhaustive limit that encompasses most of the divisions of number, and it completes the number of created things, such as the heavens, the earth, the seas, the climes, and the limbs.

Since the Prophet (ﷺ) was extremely eager for their guidance and benefit (p-558), and since the real structure of the verse was an option concerning seeking forgiveness and abandoning it, and the negation of forgiveness through seeking it, restricted to the number seventy, he (ﷺ) made the verse a qualification of what is in Surat al-Munafiqun. So he sought forgiveness for Ibn Ubayy, prayed over him, stood at his grave, and declared that if he knew that by exceeding the seventy it would be accepted, he would increase. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, considered this grave from him (ﷺ) and began to hold him by his garment, saying: "Will you pray over him when Allah has forbidden you from doing so?" This was because he did not understand from the verse anything other than the figurative sense, due to his hatred of the hypocrites. As for the Prophet (ﷺ), he saw that holding to the literal sense, out of gentleness toward the successor, is a beautiful course, bringing about harmony after discord and other benefits and noble customs. For this reason, when the explicit prohibition was revealed, ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: "I was astonished afterward at my boldness toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." That is, I realized after this explicit statement that the first was open to interpretation, for otherwise Allah would have forbidden the prayer over him. In Allah's agreement with ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, there is a noble virtue for him, and Allah agreed with him in many matters despite this. Al-Bukhari in the Tafsir (the commentary on the Qur'an section of his Sahih) and others narrated: "From Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: When ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy died, his son ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him to give him his shirt to shroud his father in, and he gave it to him. Then he asked him to pray over him. In another narration, in the book of clothing: he gave him his shirt and said, 'When you have finished, inform us.' When he finished, he informed him, and he came. In another narration: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (p-559) stood to pray over him, and ʿUmar stood up, took hold of the garment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Will you pray over him when Allah has forbidden you to pray over him?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Allah only gave me a choice when He said: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them. If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times﴾, and I will increase it beyond the seventy.' In another narration: 'If I knew that if I increased beyond seventy he would be forgiven, I would increase upon it.' He said: 'He is a hypocrite.' Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed over him. He said: Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And do not pray over any of them who has died, ever, nor stand at his grave﴾ [al-Tawbah: 84], up to: ﴿and they are defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Tawbah: 84]. So he abandoned praying over them. He said: I was astonished afterward at my boldness toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." And Allah and His Messenger know best.

In the last part of the chapter on jihad, [al-Bukhari] also narrated from Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "When the Day of Badr came, the captives were brought, and al-ʿAbbas was brought without a garment. The Prophet (ﷺ) looked for a shirt, and they found the shirt of ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy, which fitted him, so the Prophet (ﷺ) gave it to him to wear. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) removed his own shirt which he had put on him." Ibn ʿUyaynah said: "He had a favour from the Prophet (ﷺ), so he wished to repay him." In another narration from him, in the book of clothing, he said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) came to Ibn Ubayy after he had been placed in his grave, so he ordered that he be brought out, and he was placed upon his knees, and he breathed upon him from his saliva and clothed him in his shirt." End of quotation.

So it seems that his son, may Allah be pleased with him, was too shy to inform the Prophet (ﷺ) of him, because he knew of his hypocrisy; or he informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of him, but found him occupied, so he buried him. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came (p-560) after he had been placed in the grave and before the burial was completed, so he had him brought out, to console his righteous son and to remove any resentment that might be suspected of him, and to win over others. It is reported that he (ﷺ) said: "I hope from Allah that many will enter Islam because of this cause." Then a thousand of the Khazraj embraced Islam, because they saw that he sought healing through the garment of the Prophet (ﷺ). In some reports it is he who asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to shroud him in his shirt. His kindness toward him is more conducive to the mercy of the Muslims and the compassion of some of them toward others. His statement "and clothed him in his shirt" with the conjunction "waw" does not contradict the first narration. The first narration is understood to mean that he promised him the giving of the shirt, but there was an obstacle that prevented its immediate fulfilment at the time of the request. So the affirmative statement about the giving is understood as a truthful promise, which he then fulfilled after bringing him out of the grave. And Allah knows best.

This verse came as a reply to one who might have said: the previous conduct of the hypocrites was a violation of the sanctity of Allah or of the right of the Messenger (ﷺ), but it did not state that He would humiliate them by causing them to die in hypocrisy; so it would have sufficed for the Prophet (ﷺ) to seek forgiveness for them. As for these two categories, one of them informed that He would cause them to die as hypocrites, and the second violated the sanctity of the sincere Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all. So is seeking forgiveness for them beneficial? It was said: seeking forgiveness and not seeking it are equal in that it will not benefit them. He concluded it with the reason for the absence of forgiveness in His saying: (p-561) ﴿That﴾, meaning: the matter whose doing is far removed from the Wise, the Generous, ﴿is because they disbelieved in Allah﴾, meaning: He is the Supreme King, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, meaning: they do not deserve forgiveness, because they were not guided, due to their persistence in defiance, which is a meaning established within them in the case of exceeding seventy just as it is established within them in the case of limiting it to seventy. ﴿And Allah﴾, meaning: the One who encompasses all in knowledge and power, ﴿does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾, meaning: He does not guide them, because He created them disposed to defiance, and whoever He does not guide because He has drawn him to defiance, He does not forgive. So He does not forgive them, because of what He knows about them that no one else knows. Thus this is a preparation for the excuse of the Prophet (ﷺ) in seeking forgiveness for them before knowing, by the nature which makes return impossible.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 81:

When Allah, glorified is He, gave as the reason for the non-forgiveness of them their defiant disobedience (fisq), and used the explicit noun in place of the pronoun, as an indication of their being characterised by it and to make the ruling depend on the attribute, He then gave as the reason for their being firmly rooted in defiance, after having previously stated that the hypocrites are some of them from others, so that they are like one body, His saying: ﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced﴾, meaning: those whose staying behind occurred by your permission to them and the displeasure of Allah at their setting out, ﴿in their sitting﴾, meaning: their sitting back from the expedition of Tabuk. Perhaps He expressed it with this verbal noun (masdar) because it is suitable for the place of sitting, so that by its indication of joy it would be a greater indication of joy at the matter. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father. He placed the description of staying behind in place of the pronoun, to add to the reprehensibility of what they were content with for themselves, and He increased its reprehensibility further with His saying: ﴿against the Messenger of Allah﴾, meaning: after and behind, or for the sake of opposing ﴿the Messenger of Allah﴾, meaning: the Supreme King, whoever stays behind from his party is destroyed. ﴿And they disliked to strive﴾

Since this was in the context of wealth, sometimes through contentment with gaining it and displeasure at being deprived of it, and sometimes through withholding the hand from spending it, and sometimes through enjoying the staying behind, which is a share (nasib) more general than whether it is with wealth or with the self, and sometimes through disparaging those who spend, and other matters of this kind, He placed His saying: ﴿with their wealth and their selves﴾ before His saying: ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, meaning: the path of the King who possesses the attributes of perfection, because there was not in them the motive of faith and the call of certainty that moved the believers. This indicates their deep rootedness in defiance: a person may commit a sin and grieve over having committed it, whereas these rejoiced in it despite its baseness; a person may be pleased with a sin without disliking that an act of obedience take its place or accompany it, whereas these combined their joy in it with aversion to obedience; a person may dislike something without forbidding others from it, whereas these combined all of that with forbidding others. So they did all of that, ﴿and they said﴾, meaning: to others, ﴿Do not go forth in the heat﴾, out of distance from Islam and blindness regarding the chief of rulings, because the expedition of Tabuk took place in the intensity of the heat.

Since this was the saying of one whose mind had not conceived of the Hereafter, Allah, the Exalted, commanded him to warn against whoever listens to them or turns towards them, by His saying: ﴿Say﴾, meaning: O most knowing of His creation, mocking them, ﴿the Fire of Hell is more intense in heat﴾, meaning: which Allah prepared for whoever opposes His command. The turn of speech to the third person indicates that (p-563) the greatest intended purpose of this admonition is the weak among the believers, lest they imitate them out of desire for ease. Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿If only they were understanding﴾, meaning: if the hypocrites had understanding by which they would know the truthfulness of the Messenger and the power of the One who sent him over what he threatened, they would have known that, and they would not have fled from the heat to a heat far more intense; for whoever flees from the heat of an hour to the heat of eternity is the most ignorant of the ignorant. Abu Hayyan said: When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned what appeared of hypocrisy and mockery from those who went out with Him to the expedition of Tabuk from among the hypocrites, He mentioned the condition of the hypocrites who did not go out with Him, meaning in His saying: ﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced﴾. End of quote.

So the verse then serves as an answer to one who as it were said: these are the states of those who went out, so what is the state of those who stayed behind? Ka'b ibn Malik and his two companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and others like them went out, possessing none of the attributes mentioned in this verse, nor characterised by what was mentioned along with them of their attributes, having not rejoiced in staying behind.

Since the ultimate expression of joy is laughter, and what befits them in the Hereafter is weeping in the abode of misery, which is the ultimate of grief for them, wherein there is "groaning and wailing, and they will cry out therein," Allah, Exalted is He, said, threatening them, giving the reason for the ugly deed mentioned, and informing in the form of a command to signify that it is a matter that must come to pass: ﴿So let them laugh a little﴾, that is: let them enjoy in this abode, with their rejoicing at their seat, the enjoyment whose ultimate joy is laughter—a little, for it is an abode of uprooting, cessation, upheaval, and departure. ﴿And let them weep much﴾, that is: in the fire of Hell, whose scorching they neglected to remember and whose intense blaze they failed to guard against (p-564), in exchange for that little laughter, just as they exchanged its great heat for the base heat of the sun. ﴿As a recompense for what they used to earn﴾, that is: from rejoicing in sins, delighting in desires, and immersing themselves in pleasures.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 83:

When the one who is pleased with something, who dislikes its opposite, and who forbids it, does not do the opposite except by forcing himself, and his heart is not inclined to it, and since this religion is built upon might (ʿizza) and self-sufficiency (ghina), He followed that with His saying, explaining the cause of their rejoicing at staying behind: ﴿So if Allah returns you﴾, that is, the King to whom all greatness belongs, and so to Him belongs absolute self-sufficiency, from this journey of yours, ﴿to a group of them﴾, that is, those whom Allah extends their lifespans until you return to them, and this indicates that He, glorified is He, had destroyed some of them during your absence, so you wished to go out on another journey, ﴿and they ask your permission﴾, that is, they request that you permit them ﴿to go out﴾, that is, with you on that journey of yours. ﴿Then say﴾ as a punishment for them, and as self-sufficiency from them, and as might over them, forbidding them through the form of a statement of fact, so that your truthfulness in it would be a sign of the signs of prophethood and a proof among the proofs of the message: ﴿You will never go out with me ever﴾, that is, on any of the journeys, because Allah has made me independent of you and has made you in need of me. ﴿And you will never fight with me against an enemy﴾, because you have placed yourselves among the ranks of women who sit in their chambers, and you are not fit for fighting. The restriction by "with me" indicates their being burdensome to him, and it excludes what came after him ﷺ with his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, of their journeys and their fighting.

When Allah humiliated them with what they had humiliated themselves with, He explained it by His saying: ﴿Indeed, you were pleased with sitting [at home]﴾, that is, from the honour of accompanying me. And since the first instances are more indicative of the firm establishment of innate dispositions in faith and disbelief and other things, He said: ﴿the first time﴾, that is, at the Battle of Tabuk, and whoever misses us, it suffices him that we miss him. Abu Hayyan said: He gave the cause in terms of the effect, which is the pleasure arising from the cause, which is hypocrisy. End.

When He had concluded the judgment and the reason, He made His saying a consequence of it: ﴿So sit [back] with those who remain behind﴾, that is, those who were pleased for themselves with this description, of whose meanings the corrupt is one; so they are not fit for jihad, and they will never be found in the places of glory. Some said: what is meant by them are those who stayed behind without an excuse at the Battle of Tabuk, or the women and children, or the lowly among the people, or the dissenters, or the sick and the disabled, or the people of corruption. The better view is to take it as applying to all of them, that is, because the purpose is their rebuke and reproach,

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 84:

When He, glorified be He, had completed His discourse on seeking forgiveness for them and its rationale, concluding with the humiliation of those who stayed behind, and since killing in jihad was a cause for not performing the funeral prayer over the martyr, honoring him, so death occurring while sitting behind, which was approved, was made a cause for not performing the prayer as a humiliation to that one who stayed behind, He said, linking it to what the sentence "﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾" [al-Tawbah: 80] implied, "the verse" – along the lines of: "So do not ask forgiveness for them at all": ﴿and do not pray﴾, i.e., the prayer which was prescribed to honor the one prayed over and to intercede for him, ﴿over any of them﴾. Then He described (p-566) the "any" by His saying: ﴿who has died﴾, and His saying: ﴿ever﴾ is connected to the prohibition, not to the death, ﴿and do not stand at his grave﴾, i.e., because your standing is a mercy and they are not worthy of it. Then He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿Indeed they disbelieved in Allah﴾, i.e., the One to whom belongs all greatness. And since dying in disbelief prevents the prayer over the deceased in all its meanings, the repetition of the preposition was not needed for emphasis, so it was said: ﴿and His Messenger﴾, i.e., the one who is the greatest of people in blessing upon them through his counsel with the message. The meaning is that, because of the magnitude of what they committed of that, Allah did not guide them, so they persisted in misguidance until they died in a state resulting from the prohibition against seeking forgiveness for them, indicated by His saying: ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾ [al-Tawbah: 80]. That is what is meant by His saying, expressing it in the past tense while the meaning is in the present, to affirm the report and that it is certain to occur: ﴿and they died while they﴾, i.e., while their inner selves and outward conduct were, ﴿defiant﴾, i.e., drowned in defiance.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 85:

When Ibn Ubayy was the cause of the prohibition against asking forgiveness for them, and his son, ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbdullah, was among the best of the believers and the sincere among the good-doers, and some of the hypocrites had sons like him, and it is in the nature of human beings that in much of their speech they mention a mistake for which they later feel regret, and [Ibn Ubayy] was strongly inclined to be held back by the bodily ties that surrounded him and the obstacles of the carnal illusions that covered him, along with his illusions and obstacles, being confined to his fetters and ties, then repeating the speech, restating it, reiterating it, and further affirming it had an effect of confirmation and consolation and firmness in hearts, [Allah] repeated the verse of admiration (p-567) for these reasons, so that its ruling would remain in the mind of the addressee, who would not forget it, because of the belief that acting upon it is very important and requires special care, and that this resembles what has misled its owner: he speaks about it, then moves on to something else for a valid purpose, then returns to it in the course of his discourse because of his intense concern with it, as an alert to that. He does not return to it except with the utmost excellence of connection and skill of coherence. It is joined with the conjunction waw rather than fa', because this is not a consequence of what precedes it, as was mentioned in the first verse. That is: do not ask forgiveness for them, do not pray over them, and let not their words impress you, as they seek your favour in asking for your love, even if they embellish them and emphasize them with the oaths which they have taken as a shield. ﴿And let not their wealth impress you﴾, and the prohibition is attributed to it for the sake of emphasis.

Since there was nothing here that required emphasis of the negation as in the first verse, he did not repeat the negative particle, nor did he affirm the lam, nor the word "life", so he said: ﴿and their children﴾. That is: even if they show that they strive with them alongside you and draw near to Allah through them; for Allah does not intend that for them, so He does not facilitate it for them, because of what He knows of their remoteness from good and their lack of readiness for it. So let admiration for any of that not lead you to do any of what the prohibition has previously forbidden, in order to win the hearts of their like, for their assistance with their children and their wealth (p-568), and to console the hearts of the believers regarding their children; for if they are believers, leaving that will not harm them, and otherwise, far away with them and destruction. ﴿Indeed, Allah intends﴾, that is, by His might, majesty, knowledge and comprehensiveness, ﴿to punish them﴾, that is, to make them suffer, ﴿through them﴾. So the verb here is used in contrast to the preceding verse. ﴿In this world﴾, that is, through their gathering [of wealth] and the love of inclining toward it and toward the children, if they are like them in belief; otherwise they will be an increase of punishment for them in both abodes. ﴿And [that] their souls depart﴾, that is, come out with extreme difficulty, ﴿while they are disbelievers﴾ because of their being deceived by them. There is no doubt that addressing the head [of a group] with something has a greater effect on the hearts of his followers; therefore the address was directed to the Prophet ﷺ while the intended meaning is others among his followers, his community and his partisans, of those who may incline toward the means and stop at them, as is the nature of souls in contemplating what is witnessed and forgetting what is absent and past, as training for them in loving for the sake of Allah and hating for His sake, because this is among the most subtle doors of religion in understanding and the most exalted in rank. Most of its chapters are built upon it, and most of its fruits and courtesies are gathered from it. That is because the observer may, regarding one upon whom the world has been expanded, think that he is among the saved, and so befriend him because of his fine speech, heedless of his bad conduct; or he may think that the people of religion are in need of his assistance for them in jihad or otherwise with his wealth and kin, out of deliberation, and so he courts him. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, informed them that what is of this kind is cut off from blessing, as a prohibition against looking at appearances and an alert to confining one's gaze to meanings. ﴿Say: not equal are the evil and the good, even if the abundance of the evil impresses you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 100], the verse.

﴿And when you see them, their bodies impress you; and if they speak, you listen to their speech﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 4]

(p. 569) When their account was opened by stating that the God-fearing do not hesitate to set out for *jihad* (striving in the way of God, including fighting) upon a new command or seek permission, but are content with the general exhortation to it and the encouragement toward it that came before, so they hasten to it with a glance and do not fear death. And that among the hypocrites are those who seek permission for *jihad* while making their request for it a door to seeking permission to stay behind from it. And among them are those who openly seek permission to be excused from the obligations from the outset, without concealment. He followed this with a prohibition against being impressed by their wealth and their children. Then he went on to mention their categories and the disgraceful and sinful acts that were attached to them, until he concluded the account by stating that their wealth is only a trial for them and not a mercy to them, and a affliction for them and not a gift to them. He followed this with its proof, that they cannot use it to reach *jihad* and cannot use it to reach the abode of the Hereafter. So he said, conjoining it to what the context implies, such as saying: because they do not do good with it and do not earn reward; or as a clause in a state (*hal*) following the *kaf* in "tu'jibuka" (it impresses you): ﴿And when a surah is sent down﴾, meaning: a portion of the Qur'an was sent down.

Since sending down necessarily indicates the One who sends down, he explained it with His words: ﴿that believe in God﴾, meaning: the One to whom perfection belongs entirely, ﴿and strive﴾, meaning: carry out *jihad*, ﴿along with His Messenger﴾. ﴿They ask your permission﴾, meaning: to stay behind, those who have no excuse, and they are ﴿those of wealth among them﴾, meaning: those possessing bounty of wealth, abundance and affluence in most circumstances. ﴿Among them﴾: He singled them out for mention because blame is more binding upon them, especially after hearing the Qur'an. It may also be conjoined to the predicate of "inna" in His words: ﴿That is because they disbelieved in God and His Messenger﴾ [al-Tawbah: 80]. This, together with what their seeking permission included of base characteristics and lowly aspirations, is expressed by His words: ﴿And they said, "Leave us﴾, meaning: let us be, even if in a bad state, ﴿that we may be﴾, meaning: by what agrees with our natures, ﴿with those who remain behind﴾, meaning: with the excuse that is implied. Especially with the expression "dharna" (leave us), whose root revolves around what is disliked, rather than "da'na" (leave us), for the sake of what he began with, or what was made clear, from His words:

They were content to be with those who stay behind (al-khawālif), that is, with the women, as a state that had become their very nature (ka-annahu jibilla lahum). And a seal was set (wa-ṭubi'a), that is, the sealing that prevents (al-ṭab' al-māni') fell upon their hearts, to the point that they accepted for themselves staying behind from the cause of happiness, while being counted among those kept in seclusion, with what is shame in this world and fire in the next.

Since he left the agent of the sealing unspecified, he then negated fine understanding, saying: ﴿So they do not understand﴾, that is, because of this sealing they have no understanding by which they would recognize what there is in jihad of honour and happiness in both abodes, and what there is in staying behind of misery and shame. For this reason they do not strive. There is nothing more harmful than these wealths and children, which removed them far from praise and brought upon them blame and disgrace. Thus the verse about wealth and children is framed at the beginning and the end of the story by what indicates its meaning.

Then he explained the greatest success by His saying: ﴿Allah has prepared﴾, i.e., the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿for them﴾, i.e., now, so that He may give them delight therein after their death and their transfer from this abode, which is the source of troubles, ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, i.e., constantly, ﴿beneath them﴾, i.e., while they are close to them, ﴿the rivers﴾. Then he alluded, through this swiftly passing worldly life, by saying: ﴿abiding therein﴾. Then he encouraged them toward it by His saying: ﴿That is﴾, i.e., the matter of lofty rank, ﴿the great achievement﴾, i.e., nothing else.

(p-572) When He had concluded the accounts of the people of the settlements (ahl al-madar) by censuring those among them of means (ulu al-tawl) who stayed behind, and their censure was only because they were able to go out in that direction, and He placed them first because of their frequent hearing of wisdom, and the people of the desert (ahl al-wabar) were the most able of people to travel, because the basis of their affairs rests on freedom of movement and migration, they were the most deserving of censure, since they were in the utmost readiness for that. He followed them with them, saying: ﴿And there came those who make excuses﴾, that is: those who exaggerate in establishing hidden excuses that prevent them from jihad, with what the idgham (assimilation of the letters) points to. The real meaning of al-mu'adhdhir is one who imagines that he has an excuse when he has no excuse. And al-udhr (excuse) is the exhausting of stratagem in a way that repels what has appeared of shortcoming. ﴿From among the Bedouin (al-a'rab)﴾. It was said: they were the band of 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl from the Banu 'Amir; and it was said: Asad and Ghatafan; it was said: a band from Ghifar. ﴿That permission be granted﴾, that is: that permission be given by whatever granter it was regarding their staying behind from the expedition. ﴿To them﴾, that is: so they gave excuses by which they lied and sat back from the expedition with you. This was the original wording, but it was replaced by: ﴿And those who lied to Allah sat back﴾, that is: and He is the one who encompasses knowledge and power, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, as an alert to their description, and so that it would be more evident in including the Bedouin and others.

And since among them were those whose disbelief was decreed, and others, He said: ﴿There will afflict﴾, that is: by a promise that admits no failure, ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, that is: those whose disbelief was decreed, ﴿among them a painful punishment﴾, that is: in both abodes.

(p-٥٧٣) Since among those who stayed behind from the people of the settlements and the nomads there were some who had a valid excuse, He (glory be to Him) made an exception for them, presenting this in the manner of a conclusion drawn from evident premises, and said: ﴿There is no blame on the weak﴾, i.e., by reason of such things as old age, ﴿nor on the sick﴾, i.e., by reason of such things as fever and ophthalmia, ﴿nor on those who find nothing to spend﴾, even if it is by borrowing that they would repay in the future, ﴿[there is] no fault﴾, i.e., no sin, that would turn them away from the straight path and cause hardship to their religion.

Since it might be that one of the hypocrites possessed this description, He guarded against that by saying: ﴿when they are sincere﴾, i.e., in their staying behind and in all their circumstances, ﴿toward Allah﴾, i.e., the One to whom belong majesty and honor, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, i.e., privately and publicly. For in that case they are doers of good (muhsinun) in their sincere advice, which includes their regret at sitting out in this manner and their resolve to go forth whenever they are able. His saying ﴿there is no way against the doers of good﴾ stands in the place of "there is no way against them," to clarify the goodness of their sincere advice together with their excuse, ﴿[no] way﴾, i.e., no path, to blaming or reproaching them. The whole sentence is an explanation of ﴿they are sincere toward Allah and His Messenger﴾. And His saying ﴿And Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿is Forgiving﴾, i.e., the eraser of sins, ﴿Merciful﴾, i.e., the Bountiful, the Gracious, indicating that man is a place of shortcoming and incapacity however hard he strives, and nothing can encompass him except pardon;

Then he linked to that His saying: ﴿Nor [is there blame] upon those who, when﴾, and he emphasized the meaning with His saying: ﴿they came to you﴾, meaning: and they did not come without your intention, eager to join you in jihad. ﴿That you might carry them﴾, while they could not find a mount. ﴿You said﴾, meaning: they came to you saying, or at the time of your saying, "and qad" is implied, as they said in ﴿their breasts constrained﴾ [al-Nisa': 90]. ﴿"I cannot find anything﴾, meaning: anything ﴿to carry you on."﴾ (p-574) And he answered the ﴿when﴾ with His saying. It is permissible that it be a resumption (isti'naf), and "you said" is the answer (jawab). ﴿They turned away﴾, meaning: from hearing this statement from you. ﴿While their eyes overflowed﴾, meaning: they were filled so that they flowed over. Attributing the overflowing to the eyes is more eloquent, insofar as they were made entirely into tears. Then he specified what overflowed with His saying: ﴿with tears﴾, meaning: tears. The original would be: "its tears overflowed." Then he gave the reason for their overflowing with His saying: ﴿out of grief﴾. Then he gave the reason for their grief with His saying: ﴿that they could not find﴾, meaning: because they did not find ﴿what they could spend.﴾ So their grief, in reality, was over missing your companionship and being in your party. This is the story of the weepers, which he stated explicitly, even though they were included in ﴿those who find nothing﴾ [al-Tawbah: 91], to show their nobility and to affirm that the sincere advisor—however much he strives—has no independence from pardon, since He made clear that they, despite their striving to obtain the means and their distress at their failure, which made their eyes overflow, are among those against whom there is no way, or those upon whom there is no blame, the forgiven.

When he negated blame for those who were weak, he turned back to censure those who lacked this attribute, and said, exalted is He: ﴿Surely the blame is upon those who ask your permission﴾, that is, with reproach and otherwise, ﴿those who ask your permission﴾, that is, who seek your leave to stay behind from you, desiring it, ﴿while they are rich﴾, that is, they have no excuse for staying behind from you and for not helping you. His words, exalted is He, in the form of a new sentence, include: ﴿They are content to be with the women who stay behind (al-khawalif)﴾, that is, a state as though it were their natural disposition, ﴿with the women who stay behind﴾, the absence of weakness and sickness from them. Inasmuch as He gave as the cause of their action their contentment with staying behind, this conveys that there is no cause for them other than that. It also conveys that anyone who is like this is like them, even if he is weak or sick. He repeated the mention of al-khawalif (those who stay behind) to censure them for their contentment with being counted among the women, since that is among the greatest of disgraces in the eyes of the Arabs. He omitted the agent of the sealing in the first instance, and when he mentioned it the matter became grave, and this required the greatness of the sealing. So he negated knowledge in absolute terms, saying, conjoining it to ﴿they are content﴾: ﴿And Allah has sealed their hearts﴾, that is, He who has complete power and all-encompassing knowledge, ﴿upon their hearts﴾. Then he attributed as a consequence of that contentment and sealing His words: ﴿so they do not know﴾, that is, they have no knowledge, and therefore they were ignorant of the benefits of the two abodes that lie in jihad for them, and so they were content with what no sensible person would be content with. This is more eloquent than negating understanding (fiqh) in the first instance. The coupling of the Bedouins (al-a'rab) with the people of the settled towns in these verses added further beauty to the connection, for they are far from understanding and deserving of lacking knowledge.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verses 94–96:

(p-١) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Then he began to inform about things that will happen from them upon their return, as evidence that this is His speech, and that He is All-Knowing of the unseen, both in its totality and in its details. He knows what has been, what will be, and what would not have been, had it been, how it would have been. So he said, clarifying their lack of knowledge: ﴿They will make excuses﴾, that is, they will establish excuses for themselves. And he indicated their distance from the heart by his saying: ﴿to you﴾, that is, concerning their staying behind, ﴿when you return to them﴾, that is, from this expedition. It is as if it were said: what will be said in answer to them? So he said to the head who does not fear the blame of any blamer in the cause of Allah: ﴿Say, "Do not make excuses"﴾, that is, for your excuses are false. And for this reason he gave the reason for the prohibition with his saying: ﴿We will never believe you﴾, that is, we will not accept as true anything of them. Then he gave the reason for their not being believed by what made it certain for them to be so, and said: ﴿Allah has informed us﴾, that is, the King, to whom belongs complete encompassment of everything, has informed us with a majestic information.

﴿of your news﴾, that is, which you thought in your ignorance of Allah would remain hidden, but We have known it. Then he threatened them with his saying: ﴿And Allah will see﴾, that is, because He is All-Knowing of everything however subtle, All-Powerful over everything, ﴿your deed﴾, that is, after that: will you repent or will you persist in your present wicked state, \ as He saw the one before (p-٢) ﴿and His Messenger﴾, that is, by what He, glory be to Him, causes him to know, either by revelation or by insight. Since the discussion concerned the hypocrites, and the seeing was of their hypocrisy which they strive to conceal, and the believers did not have knowledge of all of them, He did not mention them, in contrast to those who come after, for they are believers.

Since this might have led them to think that He knows only what they have actually done, He negated that by making the attribute apparent in the place of the pronoun, threatening with his saying, indicating by the particle of delay their distance from standing before their Return: ﴿Then you will be returned﴾, that is, by a overpowering return which you cannot repel after the completion of your terms by death, however long they may be, then resurrection, ﴿to the Knower of the unseen﴾, which is what is hidden from creation, ﴿and the witnessed﴾, which is what any of them has perceived. So it becomes such that they perceive it. This is an expression for the One who knows a thing before it exists, and knows it after it exists. ﴿Then He will inform you﴾, that is, He will inform you with a great, majestic, comprehensive information ﴿of what you used to﴾, that is, of your natures, ﴿do﴾, that is, of what you brought out into the external world and of what was in your natures; had you delayed, it would have emerged. This is a great threat. Their arrangement of excuses was in order from easiest to most difficult, in three stages: The first: mere excuse-making, whose matter has already passed. The second: confirming that by swearing oaths, to turn away from them. So He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿They will swear by Allah﴾, that is, the One above whom there is nothing greater, ﴿to you when you return to them﴾, that is, striving in their oaths that they were excused in staying behind (p-٣), falsely on their part, desiring to turn your hearts away from what you believed about them, ﴿so that you may disregard them﴾, that is, disregarding them by overlooking their rebuke, ﴿so disregard them﴾, that is, disregarding them with disdain. It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not sit with them, and do not speak to them." Then he gave the reason for the obligation of disregarding them with his saying: ﴿Indeed, they are filth﴾, that is, reproach will not purify them, so it is futile.

Since it is established that they must have a recompense, and the soul yearns to know it, He said: ﴿And their refuge is Hell﴾, that is, in the Hereafter, ﴿as recompense﴾, that is, for their recompense, ﴿for what they used to earn﴾. So do not burden yourselves with seeking for them any recompense other than that, whether by rebuke or otherwise. The third stage: swearing for approval of them. So He said: ﴿They will swear to you﴾, that is, striving in swearing by the One previously mentioned by whom they swear, namely Allah, ﴿that you may be pleased with them﴾, out of fear of the peril of your anger. ﴿But if you are pleased with them﴾, that is, merely because of their oaths, which are based on their lack of faith, ﴿indeed, Allah﴾, [that is] the One who possesses absolute self-sufficiency, ﴿is not pleased﴾ with them. This was the original wording, but He said: ﴿with the defiantly disobedient people﴾, indicating that the ruling is tied to the attribute, and generalizing to everyone who is characterized by it. The meaning is that your approval will not benefit them, and by it you would be opposing Allah. Thus it is in reality a prohibition to the believers from being pleased with them, presented in this wondrous, startling style. In this is a refutation of one who imagines that if the believers were pleased with them, that would entail the pleasure of Allah. That is a refutation of the tendency of what the rabbis and monks do in their approval and anger, and in their declaring things lawful and unlawful, which their followers believe comes from Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 97:

When He, glorified be He, arranged the seeking of permission in matters of contracts and the acceptance of what it contains of baseness upon lack of understanding (fiqh) at one time and lack of knowledge ('ilm) at another, and concluded with the category of the Bedouins (a'rab), He clarified that the Bedouins are more deserving of that, because they are more deeply rooted in this quality and more bold in transgression (fisq), due to their distance from the source of knowledge (ma'din al-'ilm) and their turning their thoughts to other kinds of shameful acts in pursuit of wealth, which, whenever they circle around it, flies away from them and recedes. So they are always preoccupied with its concern, which has occupied them from every other concern, and they think they are doing well in their work. Thus the Exalted said: ﴿The Bedouins﴾, i.e., the people of the desert, ﴿are more intense﴾, i.e., than the people of the settled towns (madar), ﴿in disbelief and hypocrisy﴾, because of their distance from the abode of emigration (dar al-hijrah) and the source of knowledge, and their harshness, in that the mirrors of their hearts have not been polished by the lights of the Book and the Sunnah. ﴿And more likely﴾, i.e., and more worthy, ﴿that they not know﴾. And since withdrawal is harder than advancing, and the edges of mixed things are in the utmost confusion, He said: ﴿the limits of what Allah has sent down﴾, i.e., the One encompassing all things in knowledge and wisdom, ﴿upon His Messenger﴾, i.e., the one who made the creation aware of the Qur'an, the laws and the rulings, because of their not turning to it, being occupied with other things; for Allah knows that about them. ﴿And Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses all attributes of perfection, ﴿is Knowing﴾, i.e., of perfect knowledge of everything, ﴿Wise﴾, i.e., of perfect wisdom, so He places things in their most fitting places.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 98:

When He had established this description for this category, He explained that its individuals are divided into those who remained (ثَبَتَ) upon what is most fitting for their condition, and a group who inclined toward what is most fitting for the people of the settled life (أهْلُ المَدَرِ), just as the people of the settled life were divided in the same way. He began with the wicked, because it is the root (الأصْلُ) among them, so He said: ﴿And among the Bedouins﴾, i.e., those mentioned, ﴿are those who take﴾, i.e., who burden themselves with (يَتَكَلَّفُ) other than what the first natural disposition (الفِطْرَةُ الأُولى) calls for of generosity (الأرْيَحِيَّةِ) and lofty aspirations (الهِمَمِ العَلِيَّةِ), by regarding ﴿what they spend as a loss﴾, i.e., they give it only grudgingly and see no benefit in it for the Hereafter, but rather regard it like the plunder of raiding and the like, ﴿and they wait﴾, i.e., they burden themselves with waiting (الرَّبْصَ), which is to remain still, be patient, and watch, ﴿for misfortunes to befall you﴾, i.e., the calamities (الدَّواهِيَ) that revolve around their possessor so that he cannot escape them; and this is so that he may be relieved of spending and other things the religion has obligated him to.

When they waited in this manner, He invoked upon them the same as what they had awaited, so He said: ﴿Upon them is a misfortune of evil﴾, i.e., perpetually, never ceasing, either by the humiliation of Islam or by the punishment of annihilation (الِاصْطِلامِ). So they are, in what they intended against you, constantly (عَلَى الدَّوامِ) so. The reading of Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr with a dhamma on the sin (بِضَمِّ السِّينِ) is on the basis that its meaning is harm and injury (الشَّرُّ والضُّرُّ), while the reading of the rest with a fatha is on the basis that it is a verbal noun (مَصْدَرٌ), so it is a censure of the misfortune.

When the taking of vengeance upon enemies and the inflicting of might upon them depends, for the Capable One, generally, only upon hearing their news and knowing it, His established practice (سُنَّتُهُ) in concluding such matters was to say: ﴿And Allah﴾, i.e., the Supreme King who has complete encompassing, ﴿is All-Hearing﴾ [who hears what they say], ﴿All-Knowing﴾, i.e., He knows what they conceal, in conjunction with a phrasing such as: "So Allah is over all things Competent," and similar to it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾ [Ta-Ha: 46].

(p-6) When he began the second verse with His words, ﴿And among the Bedouins is he who believes﴾, meaning: he continually renews his faith, the traces of religion, ﴿in God and the Last Day﴾, he knew that the first category are not believers in that, and that only the acknowledgment by the tongue, without submission, came from them. Faith (al-iman) is the foundation upon which spending is built, [spending wholeheartedly, hoping for its reward on the Last Day, without which wisdom in this creation in this order would be absent]. Then He conjoined to it what faith yields, saying: ﴿and takes﴾, meaning: he urges his soul and struggles against it if satanic whisperings beset him, so that he counts ﴿what he spends﴾, meaning: in what God has commanded, ﴿as acts of nearness﴾, plural of qurbah (nearness), because they bring him near to Him, glorified is He, ﴿with God﴾ [i.e.,] the One from whom there is no nobler nearness, because He is the Supreme King; ﴿and the prayers﴾, meaning the supplications, ﴿of the Messenger﴾, i.e., the one whose function is conveying the message; so he says nothing to them except from God. He used "nearness" and "prayers" to refer to their cause.

When He reported their actions, He reported their outcome and their end. He said, resuming, confirming their hope, encouraging charity, with the most emphatic affirmation against their enemies' denial: ﴿Unquestionably, it﴾, meaning their expenditures, ﴿is an act of nearness for them﴾, meaning: just as they intended. Then He explained the fruit of its being an act of nearness by His words: ﴿God will admit them﴾, meaning the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, by a promise that admits no failure, ﴿into His mercy﴾, meaning His honor, so that it encompasses them. Then He gave the reason for that by His words (p-7), expressing it with the greatest Name to indicate that nothing suffices a person except pardon, even if he exerts the utmost effort: ﴿Indeed God﴾, meaning the One whom no one can truly estimate as He deserves, ﴿is All-Forgiving﴾, meaning abundant in concealing the offenses of those who repent, ﴿All-Merciful﴾, meaning abundant in honor. That is an attribute of His that is established, which covers every one who deserves it.

When he had mentioned the righteous part of them, and they were of differing ranks, with the foremost (al-sabiq) among them and most of them following later (al-lahiq), he followed it with "the foremost" (al-sabiqayn) in a comprehensive manner that encompasses and restricts both categories, the nomadic and the settled. This indicates that although He placed it later, its root (asl) precedes it, and its attribute has advanced it, to the point that it equals the people of perfection in the general sense of joining their kingdom and attaining their rank, because of its excellence in following them. This is to encourage those capable of [following] the people of good pleasure and blessing to follow the people of approval and favor. So He said: ﴿And the foremost﴾. When He indicated their precedence through their elevated rank in its levels, He indicated their ancient entry into it, so He said: ﴿the first﴾, that is, to this upright religion, ﴿of the Emigrants﴾, that is, those who left the abode of disbelief, not merely its people, ﴿and the Helpers﴾, that is, those who gave shelter and gave support, ﴿and those who followed them﴾, that is, the two groups, ﴿in excellence﴾, that is, in their following, so that they did not deviate from any part of their path. ﴿Allah is pleased﴾, that is, He to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿with them﴾, that is, because of these deeds of theirs which are in accordance with what He commanded [it], ﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾, that is, with what came to them from Him of glad tidings, and what He cast into their hearts of light through gentle admonition and remembrance. ﴿And He has prepared for them﴾, that is, as recompense for their deeds, ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. He drew attention to the generality of their irrigation and the abundance of their water by omitting the preposition, according to the (p-8) recitation (qira'ah) of the majority (al-Jama'ah), so He said: ﴿beneath which the rivers [flow]﴾, that is, they are abundant in water. So every place you desire, water springs forth from it and a river flows from it. Since the purpose of water is ease in its extraction through its nearness, and the ease of its flow and spreading out, Ibn Kathir (Ibn Kathir) affirmed this as an indication of that, as in other passages. Perhaps the specification of this passage by the difference [in wording] is because it concerns this community, so perhaps it is specified with a garden that is greater than the gardens in irrigation, beauty, and adornment.

Since the greatest of defects is interruption, He negated it by His saying: ﴿abiding therein﴾, and He emphasized the intended meaning of eternity by His saying: ﴿forever﴾. Then He resumed praising this which He has prepared for them by His saying: ﴿That﴾, that is, the matter of lofty station specifically, ﴿is the great triumph﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 101:

When he had completed the four divisions, the two divisions of the settled folk and the two divisions of the Bedouins, he then mixed two of the divisions among them as an honour to the foremost and an encouragement to those who follow. He mixed all of them together in another manner, then mentioned among them groups: some of whom had their judgment executed by their punishment, either through persistence or through repentance. And among them are those whose affair is deferred until the Day of Reckoning. He began the divisions with the one concealed from knowledge other than His own, so that the people of that division would know that He, glorified is He, is Knower of hidden things, and so they would not cease to be abased out of fear of what He threatened them with. He said, stating plainly what had not previously been stated plainly, concerning their hypocrisy: ﴿And among those around you﴾, that is, around your city, Madinah, ﴿of the Bedouins﴾, that is, those whom we have mentioned as being more intense in disbelief because of their harshness, ﴿are hypocrites﴾, that is, firmly rooted in hypocrisy. It seems that he put them first because of their coarseness and obstinacy. He followed them with those who are more skilled than them (p-9) in hypocrisy, and said: ﴿And among the people of Madinah﴾, that is, hypocrites also. Then he made clear that they do not repent by describing them in his saying: ﴿They have become accustomed﴾, that is, they became hardened, persisted, were stubborn, transgressed and disobeyed, and had [in it] a great practice and eagerness, until all their outward and inward limbs became subservient to it, and it became a disposition for them. ﴿To hypocrisy﴾, that is, they gained the upper hand in this quality, to the extent that they reached the utmost capacity in it. Then he showed their skill in it by his saying: ﴿You do not know them﴾, that is, by their persons, despite your great discernment and true insight, because of their extreme caution and their avoidance of whatever would make their affair doubtful. Then he threatened them and showed their loss by his saying: ﴿We know them﴾, that is, exclusively. [Then] he resumed their punishment by his saying: ﴿We shall punish them﴾, that is, by a promise without any breach, ﴿twice﴾, that is: the first by your return safe, the eminence of your affair, the elevation of its status, the magnitude of its pillars, the might of its authority, and the manifestation of its proof. For they cut themselves off, through their stupidity, coarseness and hardness, as I indicated by my saying: ﴿And they await misfortunes to befall you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 98], that you will not return this time from this journey, because of what they know of your steadfastness against equals, your advancing against brave lions, your plunging into terrors when the arena is narrow, and the lions of the champions shrink back; and because of the greatness, power, establishment and numbers of the Romans. And it escaped the foolish and was hidden from the wretched rich that God, who created them, is greater than them and mightier, and His armies are stronger and more numerous than their armies. The second is after your death, by the subjugation and destruction of the people of apostasy and the return of what you established under your successor, al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him (p-10), to what it was in your days of manifestation, the spread of light and radiance, and the judgment against whoever opposes it with perdition and ruin. And it will come that it is possible for the second time to be the ruin of the Mosque of Harm and the reporting of what they concealed concerning it of hidden secrets. ﴿Then they will be returned﴾, that is, after death, ﴿to a great punishment﴾, that is, whose greatness none knows in its true knowledge except God, Exalted is He, and it is the greatest, everlasting punishment that never ceases at all.

The Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 9, Verse 102:

When he (Allah) mentioned this category, the stubborn and rough ones, He followed it with the counterpart of the pure and gentle, namely the group upon whom forgiveness was bestowed and whom He regarded with the eye of mercy. So He said: ﴿And others﴾, meaning: among those around you of the Bedouins and among the people of Madinah, there are others ﴿who have acknowledged their sins﴾, meaning: they burdened themselves with mentioning them as repentance, out of regret, giving them up, and resolve, and they did not resort to false excuses [and they are the moderate ones (al-muqtasidun)].

Since mixing (al-khalt) is gathering in blending, the mere mention of it implies that what is mixed has been blended with something else. So the use of "wa" (and) in "ākhar" (others) conveys the meaning: ﴿they mixed a righteous deed﴾ with an evil one, ﴿and another evil deed﴾ with a righteous one. Thus this is among the most subtle evidences for the type of rhetorical device called al-ihtibak (a figure in which each of two parts omits what the other expresses). Perhaps the expression that conveys this meaning is an indication of the equality of the two deeds, and that neither of them is more deserving than the other to be the basis. [The Prophet ﷺ explained it in this way regarding people he saw in a dream, half of whom were good and half of whom were ugly, as narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir from Samurah, may Allah be pleased with him.] Then He made the realization of their repentance obligatory, which entails acceptance of it, by His saying: ﴿Perhaps Allah﴾, meaning: by what He possesses of encompassing all attributes of perfection (p-11) ﴿will accept their repentance﴾. For "perhaps" (ʿasā) from Him, glorified and exalted is He, is binding, because this is the practice of kings. Perhaps the use of it conveys, along with the notification that nothing is incumbent upon Him toward anyone, and that every kindness He does is by way of grace, an indication that they became like others among the sincere believers who are not infallible, in falling into shortcoming and hoping for mercy from Allah by returning them to vigilance. Just as those (others) are counted among the party of Allah despite this shortcoming, for which forgiveness is hoped, so likewise are these. Then He gave the reason for His action toward them, encouraging more, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, meaning: the Possessor of Majesty and Honour, ﴿is Forgiving, Merciful﴾, meaning: He has never ceased to be described as accepting the one who turns back when he turns to Him, and as replacing his evil with good, out of His grace and generosity. Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih, in the Tafsir, from Samurah ibn Jundub, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: "Two came to me last night, woke me, and we set off until we reached a city built of gold bricks and silver bricks. Men met us, half of their creation like the most beautiful thing you have seen, and half like the most ugly thing you have seen. The two said to them: 'Go and plunge into that river.' They plunged into it, then returned to us, the evil having left them, and they became in the most beautiful form. The two said to me: 'This is the Garden of Eden, and that is your dwelling.' The two said: 'As for the people who were half good and half ugly, they mixed a righteous deed and another evil deed; Allah has pardoned them.'"

(p-12) Since it is part of the nature of good pleasure (ridwan) that offerings are accepted, he ﷺ was commanded, for their purification and for the comforting of their hearts, with His saying: "﴿Take﴾" and He showed them mercy by making it partial, so He said: ﴿from their wealth a charity﴾, meaning that they should be content in their souls when bringing it out. ﴿You purify them﴾, meaning it is from their sins and takes the place of an expiation for them. ﴿And You cleanse them﴾, meaning you increase them and make them grow ﴿thereby﴾, by multiplying their good deeds. ﴿And pray for them﴾, meaning incline toward them and show their nobility by your supplication for them. Then he gave the reason for that with His saying: ﴿Indeed, your prayer﴾, meaning your supplications by which you connect them, so that it becomes a means of their connection to Allah, ﴿is a comfort for them﴾, meaning their hearts become tranquil through them after the anxiety of fear of the consequence of sin, because they know that acceptance is only for one toward whom good pleasure has been attained, and [because] Allah heard your word in response to you and knows your sincerity in their righteousness. ﴿And Allah﴾, meaning the One encompassing everything, ﴿is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾, meaning of everything that can be heard and everything that can be known, from you, from them, and from others. So He is worthy of answering and rewarding. The reason for this was that this group, "when their regret over staying behind intensified, they tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked about them when he arrived, and it was said: 'They regret having stayed behind you, and they swore: None shall release them except you.' He said: 'And I will not release them until I am commanded to do so.' So Allah, glorified and exalted, sent down these verses. They said: 'O Messenger of Allah! These are our wealth that kept us behind you, so give charity from it!' He said: 'I have not been commanded to do that.' When Allah sent down this verse, he took a third and gave it in charity."

[p. 13] When He (glorified is He) had brought their repentance within the scope of ﴿Perhaps﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:102], and the original sense of "perhaps" is expectation regarding what is loved and apprehension regarding what is disliked, [and] He (glorified is He) commanded that money be taken from their wealth for this purpose, and since parting with wealth is burdensome to the souls, especially in that time, Satan might have deterred whoever's foot was not firmly planted in faith from repentance and what follows from it of almsgiving, because he lacked certainty that it would be accepted. Therefore He (glorified is He) followed this with His saying: ﴿Do they not know﴾, i.e., those who acknowledge their sins, so that their souls may be willing to give charity, or others, so that they may desire repentance and charity, ﴿that Allah﴾, i.e., the One to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿He is﴾, i.e., alone, ﴿the One who accepts﴾, i.e., it is part of His nature to accept, ﴿repentance﴾ by overlooking [faults], ﴿from His servants﴾, i.e., the sincere penitents, ﴿and takes﴾, i.e., accepts as one who takes for himself, ﴿the charities﴾, i.e., from those who draw near to Him through them with sincere intention. ﴿And that Allah﴾, i.e., the One encompassing the attributes of majesty and generosity, ﴿He is﴾, i.e., alone, ﴿the Ever-Relenting, the Most Merciful﴾, i.e., overlooking and bestowing honor have never ceased to be part of His nature and attributes. In this there is a rebuke to others among those who differed concerning whether they had not done the like of their deed, [namely] the remorse that drives them to punish themselves by binding themselves to pillars and to bring near some of their wealth as these did, or something similar to that which indicates acknowledgment and remorse.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 105:

When He commanded him to purify them with that which returns them to the state they were in before the sin, He followed His saying ﴿Take﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103] with His saying, as a warning to them against the like of what they had fallen into: ﴿And say, "Work"﴾, i.e., after your purification, ﴿and Allah will see your work﴾, i.e., He to whom belongs complete encompassment, ﴿your work﴾, i.e., with the encompassment of knowledge and power that He possesses. So work as one who knows that he is under the eye of Allah ﴿and His Messenger﴾, i.e., through Allah's informing him. And since this category of believers had works in which there was concealment, He said: ﴿and the believers﴾. So perfect your works with your utmost effort and sincerity. And in the hadiths: "If a man were to work within a rock that has no door, Allah would make his work manifest to the people, whatever it might be."

Since this context is addressed to the believers, the word "then" (thumma) was omitted from it. However, since it concerns the sinners, it was emphasized with the particle "sa" (sawfa) and He said: ﴿And you will be returned﴾, i.e., by a promise that admits no failure, ﴿to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, i.e., after death and resurrection, ﴿and He will inform you﴾, i.e., through His knowledge of everything, ﴿of what you used to do﴾, i.e., what you displayed of your work and what was in your dispositions. So if you had delayed, you would have purified yourselves; He will repay you for a good deed and increase it from His bounty, and for an evil deed with justice if He wills, and He does not wrong [anyone] an atom's weight.

When he mentioned the two groups whose punishment and reward were immediate, he mentioned the group whose affair was deferred [and it is the group that wronged itself, in what he began with in Surat Fatir, the other Surat al-Hashr (surah (chapter) of the Gathering). It is not far-fetched that this is the first Surat al-Hashr, because he ﷺ (ﷺ) drove the people to the land of the gathering]. So he said: ﴿And others﴾, meaning: and among them are others ﴿deferred﴾, meaning: postponed, between hope and fear, ﴿awaiting the command of God﴾, meaning: awaiting what the Greatest King, to whom all command belongs, will ordain concerning them. They do not know whether they will be punished or shown mercy. He placed first His saying ﴿either He will punish them﴾, if they persist, as a warning, to urge them to hasten to repentance, to purify it and sincerely devote themselves to it, and to encourage fear to remain dominant as long as a person is healthy (p-15). He followed it with His saying ﴿or He will turn to them in forgiveness﴾, meaning: if they repent, as a promise of hope for them and a softening of their hearts by reminding them of the abode of intimacy from which they expelled themselves and prevented their souls from dwelling in it, and of its pleasant resting place and its repose, the beauty of its times, the loftiness of its stations, and the delight of its provisions.

Since perhaps someone would say: What is the benefit of the delay, and what prevents immediacy? He said: ﴿And God﴾, meaning the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, ﴿is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾, as a means of instilling both fear and hope, of drawing near and keeping at a distance, and as a safeguard against what the alternation might suggest of doubt, and as a training. The reading ﴿Forgiving, Merciful﴾ is for added emphasis on hope.

When he had mentioned those whom he placed in a station of peril, he followed it with specifying a group from the first, hidden category, described as being insolent (al-marudun). So he attached the harm to them and said: ﴿And those who﴾. This is coordinated (ma'tuf) with his saying ﴿and others﴾ [al-Tawbah: 106] according to the reading of whoever includes the conjunctive waw. Its predicate, in a way that suits the narrative, is: hypocrites, insolent ones (munafiqun, maridun). As for the reading of the people of Medina and Ibn 'Amir, which omits it (the waw), it is taken as answering an imagined questioner. That is because when God, exalted is He, said ﴿You do not know them; We know them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 101], the soul longed to be informed about them. Then when He said ﴿and others have acknowledged their sins﴾ [al-Tawbah: 102], the listener was occupied with understanding it, and perhaps he thought that at the end of the speech there would come a naming of them that would suffice him without asking. Then when He moved on, with His saying ﴿and others are deferred﴾ [al-Tawbah: 106], to another category, and concluded the verse with the two attributes of knowledge and wisdom, so that it would be known that the dividing is for classification, and that if there is doubt, it is with respect to the servants, while God, exalted is He, is exempt from it. So He reminded the listener, by the two attributes, of what had been turning in his mind and what his heart had inclined toward, namely the information about the insolent ones in hypocrisy. His longing for it intensified, so it was as if He had said: Who among the insolent ones is among them? Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who took a mosque﴾ [meaning] from among the insolent ones, and they are among the greatest of them in skill at hypocrisy and concealing deceit and dissension. For they reached that by obliging themselves to take hold of the greatest handholds of the religion while contending against the original nature (fitrah) and fearing lest they be exposed. So the conclusion of this verse is one of the marvelous conclusions, for it is a safeguard against what might be suspected regarding what is in their hearts, and an indication of what follows. For this reason He also concluded their story with the two attributes of knowledge and wisdom. It becomes clear from this that His saying ﴿We will punish them twice﴾ [al-Tawbah: 101] may mean: once by your return, and once by your demolishing their mosque and dispersing their gathering after the exposure of their secrets by unveiling their inner intentions.
