Then He, glorified is He, explained the cause of their taking it by His saying ﴿out of harm﴾, that is, against the people of the Mosque of Quba' or against the party of God [in general]; ﴿and disbelief﴾, that is, in God, by making His religion a mockery; ﴿and division﴾, that is, [by means of] what they plot of schemes, by enticing some of the believers whom they deceive and in whom they hope, so that he (the Prophet) would come to their mosque and leave the mosque founded upon piety ﴿between the believers﴾, that is, those firmly rooted in faith in what came from God, because they used to gather in the Mosque of Quba', so it would be exclusive to them; ﴿and in preparation﴾, that is, readiness and waiting ﴿for one who has warred against God﴾, that is, the greatest King ﴿and His Messenger﴾. And since their warring was not confined to the past time, he introduced the preposition, so He said: ﴿from before﴾ (p-17) that is: before their taking this mosque by a near time, and he was Abu 'Amir the Corrupt, so that he would come to them and increase them in strength in their hypocrisy by becoming a refuge they take shelter in and a head around which they gather. That was because he was from the Banu Ghanm ibn 'Awf, and he was the father of Hanzalah al-Ghasil, who was among the best of the Companions. Abu 'Amir had been a monk in the pre-Islamic period and had worn woolen garments. When the Prophet (ﷺ) arrived in Medina, he said to him: "What is this religion that you have brought?" He said: "The hanifiyyah, the religion of Ibrahim." Abu 'Amir said: "I am upon it." He (ﷺ) said: "You are not upon it." He said: "Yes, but you have introduced into it what is not of it." He said: "I did not do that, but I brought it white and pure." Abu 'Amir said: "May God cause the liar among us to die, a wanderer, solitary, lonely, a stranger!" So the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Amin!" and he named him the Corrupt. Then he sided with the Quraysh and fought alongside them against the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud, and said: "I do not find a people who fight you except that I fight you alongside them." When he fought on the day of Hunayn with Hawazin and they were routed, he despaired and fled to Syria, and he sent to the hypocrites: "Prepare yourselves, for I am going to Caesar, and I will come back with troops and expel Muhammad!" They had envied their brothers, the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, over the Mosque of Quba' when they built it, and the Prophet (ﷺ) used to come to it and pray in it. So they built the Mosque of Harm (p-18) and sent to him (ﷺ) to come to them so he would pray in it. He was preparing for Tabuk, so he said: "I am on the verge of a journey and a state of occupation, and when we arrive we will pray in it, God willing!" When he arrived and was near Medina, the verse was revealed. He summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum and a group and said to them: "Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, demolish it and burn it." They did so, and he (ﷺ) ordered that its site be made a dunghill where carcasses and refuse would be thrown. Abu 'Amir died in Syria [solitary, a stranger, a wanderer]." It is also said: every mosque built for boasting or for a purpose in which there is no sincerity, or with tainted wealth, is linked to the Mosque of Harm.

When He informed about their inner secrets, He informed about their hypocrisy in their outward displays by His saying: ﴿And they will surely swear﴾, that is, with the utmost of their oaths, ﴿that we intended only﴾, that is, by our taking it, ﴿the good﴾, that is, of the qualities. Then He denied them by His saying: ﴿And God﴾, that is, He to whom belongs complete encompassment, ﴿testifies﴾, that is, informs with the information of a witness, ﴿that they are indeed liars﴾. It has become clear through all of this that the cause of their disgrace is what their action contained of great harm to Islam and its people.

Then He said, forbidding them from complying with what they desired of deception, as a consequence of this statement which is more piercing than arrows: ﴿Do not stand in it﴾, i.e., in the Masjid of Harm, ﴿ever﴾, i.e., whether they repent or not. And some of the sincere believers wished to take it [as a place of prayer] first, i.e., it is necessary to ruin it and erase its trace from the face of the earth.

When He had censured it and censured its people, He praised the Masjid of the Prophet ﷺ, either the one in the noble city of Madinah or the one at Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf in Quba', according to the difference of opinion on that. It is the one that was taken as a mosque at the beginning of Islam, [built] in goodness, faith, gathering the believers together and preparing for whoever is truthful to Allah and His Messenger. He praised its people as guidance for every believer who was inclined toward it, due to proximity or otherwise, to a substitute for it. Perhaps He left its specification vague and mentioned its attribute so that it would be suitable for either of the two mosques.

Because of the characteristic of this description, [distinguishing it] from other than these two, He said, emphasizing, informing of its rightful status and of the hypocrites' denial: ﴿Surely a mosque founded﴾, i.e., its foundation was laid, ﴿upon piety﴾, i.e., piety encompassed it, for when piety encompasses its beginning it encompasses its end. And since the foundation may last for a long period of days so that its beginning would differ from its end, He said: ﴿from the first day﴾, i.e., from the days of its founding. In this there is an indication of what preceded regarding the possibility that one of the sincere people might wish to take it as a place of prayer. So He clarified that it is suitable for that, because its foundation was for something that is the opposite of it. ﴿More worthy that you stand in it﴾, i.e., for prayer, preaching and other things, rather than a mosque not intended for piety, on the assumption of an impossible supposition, except in the second state [of affairs].

When He praised it, He praised its people, saying: ﴿In it are men﴾, i.e., they possess the perfection of manhood, ﴿who love to purify themselves﴾, i.e., in their bodies and hearts, the perfection of purity, as indicated by the explicit mention; so they are constantly in the struggle against their souls in this matter. Therefore Allah loved them. ﴿And Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿loves﴾, i.e., does what a lover does of honoring with grace and kindness. And to affirm what the effort implied, the reflexive prefix of the tafa''ul form was dispensed with, or [it is] to encourage purity even to its least degrees of partial fulfillment, so He said: ﴿those who purify themselves﴾, i.e., all of them among them and among others.

Since this was indicated by allusion and hint, that founding (ta'sis) is like the beginning of the creation of living beings: whoever is formed from the very first with a nature of evil will never become fit for good and will not accept it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were refusing﴾ [al-Anfal: 23]. He mentioned it by way of explicit statement, and so, after what preceded, He made His saying, depicting falsehood as a building founded on the edge of a very unstable valley overlooking the brink of Hell, a consequence: ﴿Is one who founded his building﴾, that is, as I indicated concerning the mosque toward which people are urged to turn with devotion, ﴿upon piety from Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, ﴿and approval﴾. So he was like one who built his building upon a mountain that the rains cannot demolish and the torrents do not affect; ﴿is better, or one who founded his building﴾ upon wickedness, depravity, and indifference to matters, so he was like one who built his building ﴿on the brink﴾, that is, the edge (shafa, from which comes the word shafah, "lip"), ﴿of a crumbling bank﴾, that is, a place where the torrent has eroded and undermined it, so that it became overhanging and about to fall. For this reason He said: ﴿collapsing﴾, that is, crumbling; from "hara al-jurf", meaning the bank overhung to fall because of the torrents' erosion. ﴿So it collapsed﴾, that is, his building was for this reason a cause, for it fell in a collapse with no holding together, ﴿with him﴾, that is, while he was in it, secure from its falling because of the feebleness of his mind and the foolishness of his opinion, ﴿into the Fire of Hell﴾.

(p-21) So the answer: there is no doubt that the first is better; rather, there is no good in the second at all. The utmost wonder is that he built this building in this manner. He is answered that there is no wonder, because the matter is in the hand of Allah; there is no escape from His decree. He has guided the first to what is good for him, and did not guide the second, since He knew in him the lack of readiness for good. ﴿And Allah﴾, who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿does not guide the people﴾, that is, those who have the power to strive toward what they want, ﴿the wrongdoers﴾, that is, those stamped with blindness of insight. So they do not succeed in anything except that it comes out in a place other than its place and without order, like the steps of one walking in darkness. It is known that the verse is of the type of ihtibak (elliptical balancing): it first affirmed piety, because the people of Islam are more deserving of it, so it indicated the omission of its opposite second; and it affirmed second the weakness of the building in sensation, because the mosque of harm is more fitting for it, so it indicated the omission of its opposite first. Thus He mentioned the rational end for its people and the sensed beginning for those who look upon it. It is related from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I saw smoke from the mosque of harm." And it is reported from Khalaf ibn Yasar that he saw in it a stone from which smoke came out at the beginning of the Abbasid dynasty.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 110:

Since what preceded does not definitively establish the destruction of the mosque, given the sanctity that the mosques possess, he (Allah) resumed with the information that it (the building) is not counted among the mosques in any respect. Rather, it is counted among the houses of idols, and so it must be destroyed. He said: ﴿Their building which they built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts﴾ (p-22), meaning the very structure itself, which is the mosque. ﴿A source of doubt﴾ means skepticism and hypocrisy. Just as the houses of idols are likewise for their people, this constituted an exhortation to its demolition, its erasure, and the severing of its trace. The meaning is that it gathers them upon doubt at every time that is possible. ﴿Unless﴾ and since severing achieves the purpose without regard to a specific severing agent, he said, using the passive form: ﴿their hearts be cut to pieces﴾. That is, except for a time in which there occurs a thorough and abundant severing of their hearts and resolves, and it separates them and disperses their unity through its removal. The reading of Ya'qub with the preposition ﻿"ilā" (until) is clear in meaning. Or the intended meaning is that it continues to drive them to resolve upon hypocrisy until they die, so it is a metonymy (kinaya) for their not repenting.

Since the implied sense is: "Allah is All-Knowing of what He has informed you of, so do not doubt it," it is followed by a conjunction to generalize the ruling and to magnify the matter.

His statement: ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom belongs all-encompassing knowledge, ﴿is All-Knowing﴾, that is, of perfect knowledge of every known thing, ﴿All-Wise﴾, so He perfects whatever He commands.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 111:

When the rebuke against those who were sluggish about going forth in the way of Allah had already preceded, in His saying, ﴿What is the matter with you that, when it is said to you, "Go forth," you grow heavy to the earth?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 38] and so on, and then the command to strive with one's self and one's wealth was affirmed, in His saying, ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ [al-Tawbah: 41], and the command of Allah sufficed for the believer whose faith was sincere in Islam, in complying with it in his ease and in his hardship, and since many of them had, by their sluggishness, done what harms their faith, out of greed to cover it with their excuses and their claimed faith, the context required the rebuke of the sluggish and the reproof of the hypocrites in a manner that tears away their veils and uncovers their secrets. When He, exalted is He, had fully enumerated their categories, overturned their banners and standards, and concluded them with this group in which the Prophet's (ﷺ) compliance with His saying, ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 73] became manifest, by demolishing their mosque, burning it with fire, removing its structure, scattering it, and tearing up its foundation from the new land and rending it, He, glorified is He, followed that by reminding the believers of what He had commanded them in His saying, ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day﴾ [al-Tawbah: 29] and His saying, ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ [al-Tawbah: 41], so that they might do in it what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did in what he was commanded. He thus proceeded in the manner of an answer to a question, as if one who asked had said: The distance has grown long and the matter has become great in this surah, in exposing disgraces, tearing away secrets, and revealing ugly deeds. Why did He do that, when His custom has been to command concealment and the acceptance of pardon?

His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, i.e., the King, besides whom there is no true king, whose punishment alone is feared, and whose goodness alone is hoped for,

﴿has purchased﴾ [i.e.] with firm covenants and strong, binding pledges; and for this reason He expressed it with what indicates persistence in them, saying, ﴿from the believers﴾, i.e., in Allah and in what came from Him. He placed the selves first, indicating that the pledge preceded the acquisition of wealth, so He said, placing the dearer first: ﴿their selves﴾, i.e., which He alone created, ﴿and their wealth﴾, i.e., which He alone provides for, and He owns it to the exclusion of them.

When He mentioned the thing sold, He followed it with the price, saying: ﴿that for them is the Garden﴾, i.e., specifically for them, restricted to them, not belonging to any non-believer. He distinguished them so that each would be repaid with what he deserves. It is as if it were said: With what did He purchase that from them? So it was said: ﴿They fight in the way of Allah﴾, i.e., [the Supreme King], for the sake of His religion, which He does not accept other than, a fighting in which the religion encompasses them and is their vessel, so that nothing foreign to it mixes in. Then He made the consequence that befits it the cause of that, saying: ﴿so they kill and are killed﴾, more general as to whether that occurs potentially or actually, so He singles them out with the Garden as He promised them. The reading of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i with the passive form "qutilu" placed first is more eulogistic, because one who seeks death is not stood against by his opponent, so the meaning is: they sought to be killed, so they killed their equals. It is also possible to consider the whole, so the meaning is that they fight after seeing the fallen of their companions, without that weakening them. It is related of one of the Bedouin Arabs that when he heard this verse he said: "A sale by Allah that is profitable! We will neither cancel it nor seek cancellation," so he went out to the raid and was martyred.

Since killing, being a cause for the Garden, is good tidings and a promise, He emphasized that with His saying, ﴿a promise﴾, and added to it the particle of obligation, saying: ﴿upon Him﴾, and completed the emphasis with His saying: ﴿truly﴾. When He confirmed this noble pledge with these great emphases, He increased that by mentioning it in all the earlier scriptures, saying: ﴿in the Torah﴾ (the Book of Moses, peace be upon him), ﴿and the Gospel﴾ (the Book of Jesus, peace be upon him), ﴿and the Qur'an﴾, i.e., the Book comprehensive of all that preceded it and of every good. Those mentioned in this surah all claimed faith and clothed themselves in its garments of security; then they did, by their holding back from paying out and their hesitation in hastening and rushing, and other of their sayings and the evils of their deeds, the deed of one who lies in his claim, or of one who doubts, more general as to whether it is a lie concerning the Hereafter that includes the Garden, or a doubt about Allah's promise to make them inherit it or to single them out for it. It was permitted that others might enter it, and he hoped that he himself would be among those who enter it despite denial. Allah, exalted is He, is far above all that, and He is faithful to His covenant. ﴿And who﴾, i.e., who promised this while He is the most faithful of those who make covenants, is spoken of in the form of a rhetorical question of denial: who ﴿is more faithful to his covenant than Allah﴾, i.e., He who has all the attributes of perfection; for breaking a promise is not undertaken by the noble among people, so how about their Creator, who has absolute independence?

Since that was a cause of good tidings, because there is no better encouragement to jihad than it, He said, congratulating them: ﴿So rejoice﴾, i.e., produce in your souls the utmost joy, O assembly of the fighters. Since He mentioned it at the beginning of the contract as an indication of emphasis, He mentioned it at its end with a word indicating expansiveness, as an indication of the vastness of the reward, saying: ﴿in your sale which you have concluded﴾ (i.e., you have concluded the pledge to Allah ﴿with it﴾), for He will certainly fulfill it for you; ﴿that is﴾, i.e., your inheritance of the Garden and your being singled out for it, ﴿the great triumph﴾, i.e., exclusively, not other than it. The summary is that this verse stands in the position of giving the reason for the command to go forth with one's self and one's wealth.

[p. 27] When the covenant and its rulings were established, he described those who make the covenant in the manner of praise, to encourage people to adopt their attributes, and said: ﴿The repentant﴾, beginning their attributes with repentance, which is the foundation of righteous deed. Then the Founder (al-mu'assis) began with absolute worship ('ibadah), which encompasses all kinds of religion, including knowledge and other things, and said: ﴿the worshippers﴾, meaning those who devoted themselves to worship and made it sincerely for God. Since the commitment to religion is not recognized except through affirmation by the tongue, he followed this with praise (hamd), whose root meaning revolves around reaching the goal, and of which verbal commendation of the beautiful, comprehensive of tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) and other things, is a part. So he said: ﴿the praisers﴾, meaning those who extol Him, may He be glorified, with a great praise, whose tongues and hearts agree upon it, so that its effects follow. Since the affirmation by the tongue is not accepted except when the heart corresponds to it, he followed this with wandering (siyahah), which revolves around every order in expansion, of which is the rectification of the heart so that it may be broadened to be stripped of the narrowness of familiar things, reaching the expanse of the divine presences. So he said: ﴿the wanderers﴾. Since prayer (salah) is the result of this, as it comprises the work of the heart, the tongue, and the other limbs, and it is the greatest means of reaching the carpet of intimacy in the presences of holiness, and the highest stripping away from dwelling with the familiar, and since the first degree of humility is standing, its middle is bowing, and its ultimate is prostration, and since all forms of prayer conform to custom except bowing and prostration, he indicated them by his saying, singling them out for mention to alert that what is meant by prayer is the utmost in submission: ﴿the bowers﴾. Thus he made clear that the completion of this glad tiding for this community is that the prayer of others has no bowing in it. And he completed it with his saying: ﴿the prostrators﴾. Since one who advises himself by refining his tongue, his heart, and all his limbs is not accepted unless he exerts effort in advising others, as the example of travelling in the ship clearly states, so that the intended aim of religion may be achieved, which is the gathering of all upon God, requiring mutual support and aid, which necessitates the continuance of worship and victory, and through this the stripping away of every familiar thing, whether akin or not akin, is realized, he followed that with His saying: ﴿those who enjoin right (al-ma'ruf)﴾, meaning the Sunnah.

Since religion is firm, no one will oppose it without being overcome by it, the intended meaning of the commanded matters is their essence rather than their completion and utmost extent: "If I command you with something, then do of it what you are able" (ﷺ). And the intended meaning of the prohibited matters is to abandon them entirely, and of the limits is to stop at them without transgressing. "And if I forbid you from something, then avoid it." Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of I'tisam of his Sahih, and Muslim also, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. The Arabs, as was previously mentioned in al-Baqarah at His saying: ﴿and the middle prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:238], and in Al 'Imran at His saying: ﴿the patient and the truthful﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:17], from al-Ustadh Abu al-Hasan al-Harrali, when you follow some attributes with others without conjunction, it is known that they are not complete; but when you join them with a conjunction, you intend firmness in them, establishment and completeness. So God, may He be glorified, made known that what is intended in the preceding attributes [p. 28] is the bringing of what is possible of them, so He brought them in succession without conjunction for this. And He indicated that enjoining right, forbidding wrong, and standing at the limits is not accepted from one except in completeness, because whoever falls short in any of that is either content with the demolition of religion or is himself a demolisher. Therefore complete stripping away is required in it. For forbidding is the most difficult kind of worship, since it relates to others, provokes anger, requires zeal, and manifests enmity, and often leads to striking and killing. Therefore He joined it with conjunction and did not follow it without one, so He said: ﴿and those who forbid﴾, meaning with utmost earnestness ﴿from the wrong (al-munkar)﴾, meaning innovation (bid'ah). And since the doer of good does not benefit from his deed except by continuing in it until death, He followed it with His saying: ﴿and those who guard﴾, meaning with utmost resolve and strength ﴿the limits of God﴾, meaning the Supreme King, which He set in this upright Law, so they did not transgress any of them. He concluded with what He began with, along with the condition of continuance in observance and strength. The sum is that the first attribute is for stripping away from the bond of a particular familiar thing, which is the shirk of disobedience, by its shirk or otherwise; the second is for stripping away from the constraints of customs toward the fulfilment of acts of worship; the third is for reaching the utmost in refining the outward; the fourth is for expansion toward stripping away from the constraints of the inward; the fifth and sixth are for combining perfection of the inward and the outward; the seventh is for travelling toward bestowing that upon others; and the eighth is for continuance upon those limits by abandoning all constraints.

Thus the purpose of the verse is ascent from the bodily lowland to the spiritual nobility. Then His command to the Prophet (ﷺ) to give glad tidings to whoever has adopted these attributes, linking His command to him with the conjunction [fa] to an omitted supposition whose estimate, and God knows best, is: "So warn whoever abstains from them with everything that will harm him after his imprisonment in the abode of wretchedness, for he is an unbeliever. And give glad tidings to them," i.e., these described people. This was originally to be expressed by pronoun, but it was made apparent to conclude with what He began with, and to attach it to the description, and to generalize: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, meaning those who have adopted these attributes, with everything that will gladden them after their being assigned to the abode of happiness. And in concluding the two verses with glad tidings, once from the Creator and once from the most perfect of creation, is a greater distinction for the believers. In making the first from God is the greatest encouragement toward jihad and the highest urging to plunge into the torrents of battle. And in beginning the two verses with the attribute that indicates firm rootedness in faith, which is the attribute completing the ten, and concluding them with its like, is an indication that this is a table upon which no parasite may steal, and that whoever other than the firmly rooted is in the rank of neglect, there is no speech with them and no regard for them in any way.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 113:

When the commands to disassociate from the living polytheists (al-mushrikin) became frequent in this surah, and the command to disassociate from the dead hypocrites also came, by the prohibition against praying for them, this verse came pointing to disassociation from every polytheist, so that after it the matter it pointed to was stated explicitly. This is because, by this verse's placing of the prepositional phrase first (taqdim al-jarr), it was established that the pledge (al-mubayaʻah) was made on the basis of restricting Paradise to the believers, and that He, exalted is He, is the most faithful of those who make covenant. Thus it was established that no one other than them may enter Paradise, and that others are the companions of the Fire, because it is known that the Hereafter has two abodes: Paradise and Fire. When all of this was established, the conclusion (ʻilm al-natijah) from the sound premises was known with certainty, that it is not (ma kana) — that is, in reality (fi nafs al-amr) (p-30) — for the Prophet (lil-nabiyy), that is, the one who speaks only by what has from God a clarification concerning it, and for those who believed (wa-alladhina amanu), that is, who affirmed that they had accepted his call, so they do nothing except what they have knowledge of from it, that they should ask forgiveness (an yastaghfiru) for the polytheists (lil-mushrikin), that is, those firmly established in associating others with their Lord in worship, even if they were (wa-law kanu) — that is, the polytheists — near kin (ulي qurba) to those who believed (lilladhina amanu), after it has become clear to them (min baʻdi ma tabayyana lahum), that is, by their dying in polytheism and by the sending down of this verse to conclude with the restriction to Paradise, that they (annahum) are the companions of the Blazing Fire (ashab al-jahim), that is, they have no fitness for Paradise. For seeking forgiveness (al-istighfar) means the erasure of sins so that their possessor is saved from the Fire and enters Paradise, and it is not fitting for them to have any inclination toward them, for that may lead to softness that slackens the fighting upon which the pledge was made. So nothing is appropriate except pure separation, harshness, and opposition. The restriction of the prohibition by the word "clarified" (al-tabyin) indicates the permissibility of praying for the living, for the aim of seeking forgiveness is to turn the person toward faith, which necessitates forgiveness.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 114:

When He denied that they could have this, and Abraham, peace be upon him, was the one commanded to be followed and to adhere to his creed, having asked forgiveness for his father, He made clear that he had also done so before knowing what was actually the case regarding his father's deserving eternal abiding in the Fire. So He said, indicating by the conjunction waw that the implied meaning is: no one among the believers asked forgiveness for them after knowing: ﴿And the asking of forgiveness by Abraham﴾, that is, the Friend of Allah, ﴿for his father﴾, that is, after he had opposed him in religion, ﴿was only because of a promise﴾ [ʿan mawʿidah], that is, the saying: ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you, though I have no power for you against Allah in anything﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4]. He emphasized the issuance of (p-31) the promise by His saying: ﴿which he had made to him﴾, that is, Abraham to his father, before he knew that he had shown wickedness. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the father, who had promised him that he would become Muslim, so he asked forgiveness for him, supposing that he had been truthful in his promise and would become Muslim. [And what shows that this was before his knowledge of that is His saying]: ﴿When it became clear to him﴾ [that is, with clear and decisive clarity] ﴿that he was an enemy of Allah﴾, that is, of the Supreme King, with enmity that is everlasting toward Him by his dying upon disbelief, or by revelation that he would die upon it.

﴿He disassociated himself﴾, that is, he compelled himself to disavowal ﴿from him﴾. Then he gave the reason for what the form of the verb (tafaʿʿul), with its sense of effort, implies, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was ʾawwah﴾, that is, intensely tender-hearted, which necessitates sighing (taʾawwuh) out of fear of Allah and out of compassion for the servants. Al-Zajjaj said: taʾawwuh is that a sound is heard from the chest from the breath of exhaustion. ﴿Forbearing﴾, that is, intensely patient and overlooking of one who harms him. Thus He created him in his very essence, so how much more concerning his father, even if he had said to him: ﴿I will stone you, so leave me﴾ [Maryam: 46], and many times that.

The Imam Abu Muhammad Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Isma'il al-Bustiyy, the judge, said in his tafsir: Harmalah narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed me, from Ayyub ibn Hani', from Masruq ibn al-Ajda', from ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day, and we went out with him, until he reached the graves. He commanded us and we sat down, then he stepped over the graves until he reached one of them, and sat beside it and conversed with it at length. Then the weeping of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose, and he was weeping, so we wept at the weeping of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then (p-32) the Prophet ﷺ came toward us, and ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, met him and said: 'What made you weep, O Prophet of Allah? For it has made us weep and frightened us.' He took ʿUmar's hand, may Allah be pleased with him, then came toward us, and we came to him. He said: 'Did my weeping frighten you?' We said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah!' He said: 'The grave which you saw me conversing with is the grave of Aminah bint Wahb, and I sought my Lord's permission to ask forgiveness for her, but He did not permit me, and this was revealed to me: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives﴾ [al-Tawbah: 113], until he finished the verse.'

﴿And the asking of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise which he had made to him﴾, so what a son undergoes of tenderness seized me; that is what made me weep." And this is a good chain (sanad hasan). In Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, in the Book of Funerals, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ visited the grave of his mother, and wept and made those around him weep, and said: 'I sought my Lord's permission to ask forgiveness for her, but He did not permit me; and I sought His permission to visit her grave, and He permitted me. So visit the graves, for they remind of death.'"

In al-Bukhari's Tafsir and elsewhere, from Ibn al-Musayyib, from his father, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "When death approached Abu Talib, the Prophet ﷺ entered, and with him were Abu Jahl and ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Umayyah. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'O uncle! Say: There is no god but Allah, so that I may plead for you with it before Allah.' Abu Jahl and ʿAbdullah ibn [Abi] Umayyah said: 'O Abu Talib! Will you turn away from the creed of ʿAbd al-Muttalib?' — and in another narration: the last thing he said to them was that he was upon the creed of ʿAbd al-Muttalib — so the Prophet ﷺ said: 'I will surely ask forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from you.' Then it was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists﴾ [al-Tawbah: 113], the verse. [And Allah revealed concerning Abu Talib: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Qasas: 56], the verse.]"

Perhaps he continued to ask forgiveness for him between his death and the battle of Tabuk, until it was revealed. Other causes of revelation have also been related for it, and it has already been mentioned that it is permissible for the causes to be multiple.

This is the commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 115:

When seeking forgiveness for the polytheists was a grave matter, and it carried a kind of alliance with them, Allah, glorified is He, showed the believers the favor He bestowed upon them by not holding them to account for undertaking it. This was to magnify the matter and to sever whatever lies between the peak of faith and the depths of disbelief in every respect. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah would not﴾, that is, the One who possesses the attributes of perfection. Since misguidance is the cause of destruction, and whoever lays down a law and then punishes one who abides by it without making it clear is like one who points out a path that does not lead to its destination, so that its traveler perishes, the one who points it out is thereby a misleader, He said: ﴿to lead astray a people﴾, that is, He does to them what He does to the misguided by way of punishment, because of their committing what He forbids, by means of an abrogating ruling that abrogated it, ﴿after He had guided them﴾, that is, by a law He established for them, ﴿until He makes clear to them﴾, that is, a clarification sufficient to cure the ailment of ignorance, ﴿what they should fear﴾, that is, what is worthy of their being wary of and avoiding out of fear of its harm, [by an abrogating ruling that abrogates the state of permissibility in which they were].

(p-34) Since one who commands a path to be followed and then leaves in it what needs explanation is only open to attack for ignorance or forgetfulness, He, glory be to Him, negated that of Himself, saying, giving the reason for the absence of misguidance: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing the attributes of perfection, ﴿is Knowing of all things﴾ [At-Tawbah: 115], that is, His knowledge is complete, so no obscurity reaches it in any respect or at any time. Thus He makes clear to you everything you do and refrain from, and whatever guidance depends upon. What He has left unmentioned, He leaves out only out of mercy toward you. ﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Taha: 52], so do not search for what He has left out.

Then he gave the reason for His knowledge of all things: His power is comprehensive, so He is able to grant victory to whom He wills and to take vengeance on whom He wills. Therefore no one should love except for His sake, hate except for His sake, or concern himself with the enmity of anyone who opposes Him. So He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the Greatest King, ﴿to Him﴾, that is, in every respect you count among the aspects of perfection, ﴿belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾. Nothing is hidden from Him, so He is Aware of everything that benefits or harms you, and He is your Protector, making things clear to you. Whoever possesses the entire dominion is in a position where nothing resists his command, neither knowledge nor anything else, because knowledge is among the greatest of powers and capacities, and a king is only a king if he is knowing and capable. Then he gave the reason for His power and knowledge by what is repeatedly observed of His action in animals, plants, and other things, saying: ﴿He gives life and causes death﴾, that is, in every sense. He is the One who gave you and others bodily life, and He specifically granted you the life of faith. Just as He made others allies of one another and gathered them all under the guardianship of their enemy, Satan, He made you (p-35) allies of your Lord, the Most Merciful. So He is your Protector and your Helper. ﴿And you have not﴾, the state being that ﴿you have not﴾, since it is not permissible for anyone to take as a protector anything below His rank, glory be to Him, He affirmed the preposition, saying: ﴿besides Allah﴾, that is, the King to whom all command belongs, and He went to the extreme in negation with His saying: ﴿any protector﴾, that is, any close relative who would show you the care and sincere counsel that a close relative shows in support, or other than that.

Since a person may be helped by someone other than his relative, He said:

﴿nor any helper﴾, that is, do not take as allies except those who are of His party and the people of His love and nearness. In this there is a warning to anyone who proceeds to do what he should guard against, especially flattery toward the enemies of Allah, whether those who conceal their enmity or those who openly declare it, for the ultimate result of that is making them allies, and that does not avail anything against Allah.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 117:

When he indicated that He is their Walī (Protector/Ally), who gives them life with a Spirit from Him, clarifying for them what sets them right and that there is no Walī for them other than Him, he established the proof for that with His saying: ﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet﴾, that is, He to whom belongs majesty and honor, ﴿to the Prophet﴾, that is, the one who continually has from Allah a great news that guides him to what indicates the strengthening of his life by raising his ranks. Thus there is no station to which He elevates him except that he sees that, because of the increase of his exaltedness and nearness, it is for the station that was below him. So he is, in every glance, in ascent from perfect to more perfect, toward that which has no end.

When Allah, exalted is He, informed of the high rank of the Prophet ﷺ by raising him in the ranks of perfections and greater perfections, toward that which has no end, in a manner that is in the utmost stirring of every (p-36) believer to hasten to repentance, He affirmed that with His saying: ﴿and the Muhājirūn (Emigrants) and the Anṣār (Helpers)﴾, by erasing their lapses and raising their ranks, ﴿who followed him﴾, that is, the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿in the hour of hardship﴾, that is, the times of the expedition of Tabūk. They were in hardship from time: by barrenness, narrow straits, and severe heat; and in hardship of mounts, [so that] ten shared one camel in turns; and in hardship of provisions, "they took dates [wormy], barley [weevily], and rancid fat"; the distress reached such a point that two persons would divide a single date, and sometimes a group would suck on it so as to drink water after it; and in hardship of water, to the extent that they slaughtered the camels and squeezed their dung. He called it an "hour" to lighten the times of distress and to encourage enduring hardships, for its duration is brief and its reward is great and momentous. Thus their state in following him in this expedition was more perfect than their state before it. (Allah, exalted is He, indicated the variation among them in steadfastness upon high stations, in that they ascended by repentance to what is higher than them, and in accepting whisperings that repentance had kept far from their acceptance) with His saying: ﴿after the hearts of a group of them had nearly swerved﴾, that is, came very close ﴿to swerve﴾, that is, to depart from their places which necessitate their soundness. By "min" (after) he indicated the closeness between the beginning of the swerving and the remedy through repentance. And since the situation called for upheavals, (p-37) it was fitting to express with what involves turning and division, so He said: ﴿the hearts of a group﴾, that is, they were such that division would occur among them because of the disturbing upheavals there, ﴿of them﴾, that is, because of the great hardships that befell them, so they would incline away from the truth, like Abū Khaythamah, and whoever loved ease and dreaded the journey in that severe heat, toward the Banū al-Aṣfar, the kings, the hunters, the heroes, the champions, who fill the earth in multitude, equal the pebbles in number, and are like the mountains in strength. Then Allah resolved for him, and he joined the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Thus He, exalted is He, returned all of them to what they had been upon, just before the approach of swerving, from his distancing. When they became like one who had not come close to swerving, He elevated the highest of them to another station, and expressed His greatness with the particle of delay, saying: ﴿Then He turned in forgiveness to them﴾, that is, [all of them, as a repetition of the elevation, or to those who had nearly swerved], by steadfastness in keeping far from lapses and by ascending to the high ranks until death. Abū Ḥayyān transmitted from al-Ḥasan that their swerving was their intention to depart because of the hardship they met with. He said: It was also said: their bad opinion of what they saw of the severity of the hardship, the scarcity of provisions, the distance of the journey, and the strength of the enemy targeted. End.

It is permissible that He expressed with "thumma" (then) because they reached a state in which steadfastness was remote, let alone keeping far from the places of lapses, so He made them firm until they became like iron, without an apparent cause from "an army or otherwise." Thereby it is established that He is the Possessor of dominion, able to do whatever He wills, and that there is no Walī for them besides Him. (p-38) Then He gave the reason for His kindness toward them with His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful﴾. Ra'fah is intense mercy, so He put forward the more emphatic; what was said about "al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm" applies to it. The meaning: He has mercy on them with the highest mercy by bestowing great blessings and repelling great calamities, and He has mercy on them also by bestowing subtle blessings and repelling subtle calamities. It was also said: ra'fah is the removal of harm, and raḥmah is the conveyance of benefit; the root r-'-f revolves around breadth together with intense connection, as was pointed out in Surah Subḥān. So ra'fah, as al-Ḥarrālī said regarding al-Baqarah, is the inclination of one who inclines toward someone in whom he finds a favor and a connection; it is the mercy of one with a relation toward the one who shows mercy, whereas raḥmah encompasses one who has no relation to the one who shows mercy. End. Thus ra'fah is then for the steadfast and raḥmah for those who came close to swerving. So the steadfast one becomes shown mercy twice, since he is regarded with both attributes. What benefits here was already mentioned among the Ḥizbayn in al-Baqarah.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 118:

When He had explicitly mentioned repentance for those who came close to deviation and mixed with them the people of steadfastness, as an indication that every person is in need of the Self-Sufficient, the Great, [and so that their association with the people of lofty standing, and His placing them within their sphere, would be an honour for them and a comfort, lest their denunciation become too severe], He followed it with repentance for those who had actually fallen into deviation. He said, without explicitly mentioning deviation, as a teaching [in good manners and as a consolation to broken hearts]: ﴿And to﴾, meaning: and indeed (p-39) Allah relented toward ﴿the three who were left behind﴾.

Since the One who removes hearts from their places is absolute in causing to be left behind, the verb ﴿were left behind﴾ is put in the passive. Its meaning is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left them behind by boycotting them and forbade the people from speaking to them, and he deferred the ruling concerning them so that the command of Allah might come regarding their matter. Their being left behind continued. ﴿Until, when the earth became constricted for them﴾: he indicated the magnitude of the matter by the particle of elevation, saying ﴿upon them﴾, meaning the earth entirely, ﴿despite its vastness﴾, meaning despite its great breadth; that is, its open expanse and its extent became constricted for them.

Since this might be taken literally, and since constriction of the place does not necessarily entail constriction of the breast, he followed it with an indication that the intended meaning is figurative, saying: ﴿and their souls became constricted for them﴾, by distress that unsettles and anxiety that disturbs, ﴿their souls﴾, meaning because of the severity of what they encountered of the boycott, even to the point of not being spoken to, even to the point of not returning a greeting. Since this would not call for repentance except through constant self-reckoning, he followed it, for the sake of being left behind in that state, with His saying: ﴿and they became certain﴾, meaning: they were certain. Perhaps He expressed it with ﴿zann﴾ (supposition, opinion) rather than ʿilm (knowledge) to signal that, because of the intensity of their bewilderment, their hearts were not settled in one state, so their certainty, because of the agitation of their thoughts, was like a supposition. [Or it may be said, and this is good: the use of this term for the certainty of the sincere ones is an indication that the highest certainty in tawhid does not reach the reality as it is, in that no one can estimate God with His due estimation, as the most truthful of creation ﷺ said: "I cannot enumerate praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself." This is one of the precious points, so employ it in similar cases.] ﴿that there is no refuge﴾, meaning no escape or recourse ﴿from Allah﴾ (p-40), that is, the One who has complete encompassment, ﴿except in Him﴾, meaning by that which pleases Him. This is an image of their bewilderment regarding their situation. The answer to ﴿when﴾ is omitted, and the opening of the speech indicates it; its estimated meaning is: He overtook them with repentance and returned them to what they were upon before they had committed the sin.

Since what they had done of holding back from the command of the Messenger ﷺ was grave by mere opposition, then they abandoned consolation, then they turned away from him ﷺ, then by grave matters of extreme ugliness and evil consequence, it would be far-fetched that there could be an increase beyond the rank of repentance. He, glorified is He, made known that He had elevated them in ranks of perfection, by making that a cause of purifying them from all impurities and cleansing them from all remaining defilements, which requires greater nearness through ascent in the stations of knowledge, as is indicated by the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him: "Rejoice in the best day that has passed over you since your mother bore you." Then He, glorified is He, followed this announcement with His saying, indicating what comes after it, "Had it not been for the grace of Allah," with the particle of remoteness: ﴿Then He relented toward them﴾, meaning He returned them, after repentance, to a station of the stations of soundness of nature, which is the best of forms, rising by its loftiness in relation to what is below it, a repentance ﴿that they might repent﴾, meaning: that they might return to what the original nature requires, namely steadfastness in what they were upon of excellence in religion and adornment with the character of the foremost. Perhaps He expressed it with ﴿zann﴾ in place of ʿilm to indicate that, in fear of His majesty, for the sake of turning wholly to Him, mere supposition suffices that there is no cause except from Him, because He encompasses everything and nothing can overpower Him. It is also possible that the expression ﴿then﴾ is an indication of the magnitude of the terrors they endured and the degrees of fear they ascended to, and a bestowal of favour upon them with repentance (p-41) from the magnitude of what they had committed. They were singled out from their companions in being deferred to the command of Allah because of the height of their rank through their precedence and their firm footing in Islam; thus a slight opposition from them is greater than much from others, because they are imams of guidance and lamps in darkness. From this flash comes: "The good deeds of the righteous are the sins of the near ones." Then He explained the repentance by a matter that encompasses others, as encouragement, saying, expressing with what indicates, along with their high rank, his descent from the rank of those before them: ﴿Indeed Allah﴾, that is, He to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿He is﴾, that is, alone, ﴿the Accepter of repentance﴾, that is, the one who is abundant in relenting toward whoever repents, however great his sin and however often he repents because of the repetition of his sins, ﴿the Merciful﴾, that is, the Bestower of honour upon whomever He wills of His servants by keeping him upon what He is pleased with, so that he does not deviate, and who magnifies His favour upon him.

al-Biqa'i, *Nazm al-Durar*, on Surah 9, verse 119:

Since what they attained through their Lord's favour toward them, after what He had described them as suffering (from hardship and what came with it), was piety and sincerity in faith, just as a person finds in himself that death or being thrown into the Fire is dearer to him than uttering the clear declaration of faith with the testimony of the Chosen One (ﷺ), He, glory be to Him, encouraged sincerity, saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning, those who claim that, ﴿fear God﴾, meaning, be wary of the might of the One who possesses perfect greatness, so that your claim is confirmed, and do only what pleases Him. ﴿And be﴾, meaning, be in a sincere state with your whole nature and disposition, ﴿with the truthful﴾, meaning, in every matter that is required of them. Perhaps He phrased the command in a general form so that it includes every believer: whoever falls short is commanded to catch up, and whoever is ahead is urged to maintain his station of being foremost. Perhaps He expressed it with "*ma'a*" (with) so that it includes the lowest degree, which is being present physically (*bi-l-jatth*). Al-Bukhari narrated the repentance of Ka'b, one of these three, may God be pleased with them, in several places of his *Sahih*, including the chapter on *tafsir* (exegesis). Others also narrated it from Ka'b himself, may God be pleased with him, who said: "He had not stayed behind from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in any expedition he undertook, except two: the expedition of al-'Usrah, meaning this one, and the battle of Badr. As for his staying behind at Badr, it was only because the Prophet (ﷺ) had not called the people to it or urged them to it, for he had only set out at first for the caravan." He said: "I resolved to be truthful to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He rarely returned from a journey he had undertaken except in the forenoon, and he would begin with the mosque and pray two rak'ahs. The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade people from speaking to me and to my two companions, meaning Murarah ibn al-Rabi' al-'Amri and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi, and he did not forbid speaking to anyone among the others who had stayed behind apart from us. So the people avoided speaking to us, and we remained in this state until the matter grew long for me. Nothing weighed on me more than dying without the Prophet (ﷺ) praying over me, or the Prophet (ﷺ) dying while I remained among the people in that position, with none of them speaking to me or praying over me. Then God, mighty and majestic, revealed our repentance to His Prophet (ﷺ) when the last third of the night remained, while the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was with Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her. Umm Salamah was kind to me and concerned for my affair. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'O Umm Salamah! Ka'b has been forgiven.' She said: 'Shall I not send to him to give him the good news?' He said: 'If you do, the people will crowd upon you and keep you from sleep for the rest of the night.' When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) prayed the dawn prayer, he announced God's forgiveness of us. When he was pleased, his face would light up until it was like a piece of the moon. We, the three who had been left behind, had been set aside from the matter that was accepted from those who gave excuses when God revealed the repentance for us. When those who lied to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) among those who stayed behind and gave excuses falsely were mentioned, they were mentioned with the worst that anyone has been described with." God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿They will make excuses to you when you return to them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 94], the verse.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 120:

Since what befell them of terrors was only because they stayed behind from the Best of Creation, and what turned them toward the pastures of advancement is truthfulness, God the Exalted said, forbidding in the form of a statement so that it would be more eloquent, and including with them whoever was in the same condition as them in general staying behind: ﴿It was not [fitting] for the people of Madinah﴾, i.e., it was not right or proper in any respect, ﴿nor for those of the Bedouins around them﴾, i.e., in all the regions of the noble city, ﴿from the Bedouin Arabs﴾, i.e., from the inhabitants of the deserts who had sworn by Islam, ﴿to stay behind﴾, i.e., in any matter of affairs, ﴿from the Messenger of God﴾ (p-44), i.e., the Supreme King, and it is incumbent upon the one sent that he not depart from the side of the Messenger, especially since he is the leader of the truthful ones with whom the command to be with them has come, ﴿nor to prefer [themselves]﴾, i.e., and it was not for them to prefer, and perhaps He reduced them by the form of paucity in relation to those whom He strengthened him with of his soldiers, ﴿over his own self﴾, i.e., which is the most noble of souls absolutely, by protecting their souls from what he (ﷺ) experienced, rather by casting them into destruction in his stead and in order to safeguard his noble self from the lowest harm. So this is like a reason for the command to piety; i.e., fear God and be truthful to Him as these have been truthful, ﴿so that He may relent toward you as He relented toward them﴾, for it was not for you to stay behind. This is an eloquent prohibition together with reproach, rebuke, incitement and stirring.

Since He gave the reason for the command to piety, He gave the reason for the prohibition of staying behind by what indicates the truthfulness of faith, so that its opposite becomes indicative of its opposite. So He said: ﴿That﴾, i.e., this great prohibition of staying behind in this style of negation of being, ﴿is because they are not afflicted by thirst﴾, i.e., severe thirst, ﴿nor fatigue﴾, i.e., extreme exhaustion, ﴿nor hunger﴾, i.e., severe famine, ﴿in the way of God﴾, i.e., the paths of the religion of the Greatest King leading thereby to fighting His enemies. These things are arranged in the order of their occurrence in existence, for absolute movement stirs up heat, so thirst arises, and its continuation produces exhaustion, and most often it comes before hunger (p-45).

Since the purpose of exerting oneself with what has been mentioned is to humiliate the disbelievers by entering their land, which leads to their faith through gaining from them, He followed that with His saying: ﴿nor do they tread a path﴾, i.e., a treading or a place whose treading ﴿enrages the disbelievers﴾, i.e., their treading of it with their feet or their animals, ﴿nor do they gain any gain from an enemy﴾, i.e., whatever it may be, small or great, ﴿except that a righteous deed is written for them thereby﴾, i.e., in the books of deeds. It is stated in the passive because the intention is to affirm it without reference to a specific agent, ﴿a righteous deed﴾, i.e., a great reward is established for them because of it.

Since the doer of these things has advanced toward perils in himself and has attained the display of jihad, it was indicated, in an emphatic nominal sentence, that he is a doer of good: in regard to his own self, by establishing evidence through obedience of the truthfulness of his faith; in regard to others among the believers, by protecting them from the greed of the disbelievers; and in regard to the disbelievers, by urging them toward faith to the utmost possible extent. So God the Exalted said, giving the reason for the recompense: ﴿Indeed, God﴾, i.e., He who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿does not waste﴾, i.e., does not leave unrewarded that which is by its nature liable to be neglected, ﴿the reward of the good-doers﴾. The place of the pronoun was made explicit to generalize and to attach the judgment to the description.

When the hardship of spending, whose harm returns to one's wealth, and of treading on any land, which does not necessarily lead to reaching what enrages the enemy, is considered apart from the hardship that arises in the self from thirst and what accompanies it, and from doing what enrages the enemy and diminishes him, He placed that before His saying: ﴿and they do not spend﴾. And since a little may be looked down upon, He began with it, encouraging it, in His saying: ﴿a small expenditure﴾. And since a captious person may perhaps be pedantic and make its mention a condition, He said: ﴿nor a large one﴾, informing that it is considered significant, lest it be abandoned. In this there is an allusion to the verse of censure (ayat al-lamz) directed at those who volunteer in charity. ﴿Nor do they cross a valley﴾, meaning, of the valleys, by marching in jihad. The wadi (valley) is every open space between mountains and hillocks through which the torrent flows; it is originally a form (fa'il) from "wadā", meaning it flowed. ﴿except that it is recorded for them﴾, meaning that expenditure and crossing, He built the verb in the passive because the aim is preservation by recording in general. ﴿that Allah may reward them﴾, meaning the Possessor of Majesty and Honour, meaning by that, of His bounty, ﴿the best of what they used to do﴾, meaning by disposition and nature, ﴿they were doing﴾, multiplied according to the measure of steadfastness. The closing phrase of the first (verse) was emphasised but not this one, because that one carries an increase in hardship and benefit, and for this reason it explicitly mentioned the reward and the righteous deed. Imam Abu Hayyan drew attention to this. From here, rather, from His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah has purchased﴾ [at-Tawbah: 111], he began to connect the other (passage) to the first, whose content is the disavowal of the polytheists and striving in fighting them after their term has expired, wherever they are found, up to His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden﴾ [at-Tawbah: 29], up to His saying: ﴿What is [the matter] with you that when you are told, "March forth in the way of Allah," you cling heavily to the earth?﴾ [at-Tawbah: 38], then He said (p. 47) ﴿March forth, light and heavy﴾ [at-Tawbah: 41]. Then He followed that with the stories of the hypocrites, just as He did here, by concluding with His saying: ﴿Fight those of the disbelievers who are near to you﴾ [at-Tawbah: 123], the verse, and then followed it with the mention of the hypocrites.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 122:

When the prohibitions against those who stayed behind became frequent, the rebukes followed one upon another, and the reproach and threat grew severe, hearts took flight and souls became fearful. This was likely to mean that after this, no one would stay behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) or from the one who would take his place, and then the enemies would be able to gain control over the wealth, the offspring and the dependents. Therefore, Allah the Exalted followed this with His saying: ﴿It was not for the believers﴾, that is, those whom firmness in faith had prompted to go forth, ﴿to go forth all together﴾, that is, all of them; for that would harm many of the good objectives. This is an instruction in what is most suitable for both religion and worldly life, namely that people be divided into two groups: one group for jihad, and another for providing sustenance and guarding wealth and children. All of this is by his command (peace and blessings be upon him) and by acting in what pleases him, and this is not hidden from the sincere person. Perhaps the use of the past tense verb in His saying, as a consequence of what came before it, ﴿So why did not there go forth﴾, is so that the rebuke of those being rebuked among the ones who stayed behind throughout this surah may be understood, namely that it was incumbent upon them to go forth with the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿from every division﴾, that is, from a large number of people whose separation is easy. They said: it is a term that applies to three. ﴿From among them a group﴾, that is, people who never leave, surrounding the Prophet (ﷺ) and staying with him. It was said: a ṭāʾifah is one or two, so the verse is evidence for accepting the report of a single narrator and the obligation to act upon it. [And perhaps He expressed it with this word to indicate encouragement toward a large number of those who go forth, as is its most common basic meaning in this usage.] ﴿that they may gain understanding﴾, that is, that those who go forth may exert themselves to comprehend from him (ﷺ) little by little ﴿in the religion﴾, that is: by what they hear of his sayings, what they see of his good deeds, and what reaches their hearts from the illuminating circumstances of his life. This is the highest honor for knowledge, since it is made the ultimate purpose of remaining with him (ﷺ) in jihad. This applies if he (ﷺ) himself was the one who went forth in that expedition; if it was someone else, then the pronoun in "yatafaqqahū" refers to those remaining with him (ﷺ).

Since knowledge includes both glad tidings and warning, and since a human being, because of his deficiency, is in greatest need of warning, He singled it out for mention, saying, coordinating with what came before (that they should fear for themselves so that they act to save themselves): ﴿and that they may warn their people﴾, that is, that they may caution them about the dangers before them if they neglect the side of piety, ﴿when they return to them﴾, that is, of what the Messenger (ﷺ) warned them of, and give them good news [of what he gave them good news of]. Then He explained the ultimate purpose of knowledge, indicating that whoever makes for himself any other ultimate purpose, such as arrogance or boasting, has indeed gone greatly astray. So He said, making it obligatory to accept the report of the one who conveys to them: ﴿so that they may beware﴾, that is, all of them, so that their state may be the state of those who fear Allah, through what they have acquired of understanding, for it is the foundation of every good; by it hearts are illuminated, so they turn toward goodness and turn away from evil. Caution is avoiding a thing because of the harm in it. The intended meaning of fiqh here is preserving the Book and the Sunnah and understanding their meanings, from the fundamentals and the branches, the etiquette and the virtues. Al-Rummani said: fiqh is understanding the implications of the meanings contained in them without an explicit indication of what they point to.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verse 123:

When the purposes became known and the hearts were prepared [to accept] the benefits, and he was commanded to warn with *fiqh* (deep understanding of the religion), and among the people there were those who would not turn back except through severe force, he addressed everyone, speaking to them through the lowest teeth of the hearts, so that he would direct himself to the lowest and take the highest from it by way of the greater. He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, that is, who claimed with their tongues to have faith. ﴿Fight﴾, that is, as confirmation of your claim, ﴿those adjacent to you﴾, that is, those close to you, ﴿of the disbelievers﴾. So those who are adjacent to you, if you see no other course more appropriate for a meaning that presents itself, then there is in that good arrangement and what wisdom (*hikmah*) requires. Also, because *jihad* (struggle) is a known good and a benefit, and those nearest have more right to what is known as good. And [it is] so that you may push the enemy away from your lands, so that their well-being increases and your corruption decreases, and you will have combined, through understanding and fighting, the two struggles: the struggle of argument and the struggle of the sword, while guarding through this order against what you fear of their scheming if you fight, lest there remain behind you those whose plotting you fear.

Since gentleness is more fitting for peace-making, and harshness is more fitting for breaking off relations, he said: ﴿and let them find in you harshness﴾, from *wijdan* (finding), ﴿harshness﴾, that is, severity and zeal, because that is more awe-inspiring in their breasts and restrains them from their wickedness. The literal meaning of *ghilzah* (harshness) is in bodies; it is borrowed here for severity in war, and it comprises boldness, patience in fighting, and intensity of enmity. When they do that, they will be combining the struggle of argument and of the sword, as it has been said:

Whoever the Qur'an does not straighten, for him there is straightening through humiliation and Indian swords.

Abu Hayyan drew attention to this.

Since the implied meaning is: let all of that be together with taqwa (God-consciousness), not on account of wealth or status, for it is the foundation of the whole matter, he said, alerting to this by his saying: ﴿And know that Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿is with the righteous﴾. So do not fear that anything of accompanying them will lead to weakness, for what matters is the one with whom Allah is.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 9, verses 124–125:

When He mentioned this surah, namely the group that urges (the others) with the particle "lawla" (why not) to hold back alongside the Messenger of God (ﷺ), the surah that commands fighting the disbelievers and being harsh toward them, and since nothing prompts such a response except what He indicated, He concluded the preceding verse about taqwa (God-consciousness) with the renewal of faith whenever any part of the Qur'an is revealed. He, glorified is He, had mentioned those who opposed the command to fight by staying behind, without mentioning the command of faith, when He said: ﴿When a surah is revealed, saying, "Believe in God and strive alongside His Messenger," the people of wealth among them ask your leave and say, "Leave us to be with those who sit back."﴾ [al-Tawba: 86]. He turned to that matter in order to mention the other category, the one who sits back from faith, and so He said: ﴿And when﴾, and it was emphasised by adding the negating particle, as an alert to the excellence of faith (p-51), so He said: "mā" (whenever).

Since what is attributed to them is the mere act of revelation, the verb ﴿was revealed﴾ is in the passive form. The phrase ﴿a surah﴾ means a portion of the Qur'an, that is, in some sense of its meanings. ﴿Among them﴾ means among those to whom it was sent down. ﴿There are those who say﴾ [meaning], in denial and mockery, and they are the hypocrites. ﴿Which of you﴾ means: which of you, O hypocritical group, ﴿has this increased in faith?﴾ This is said as a deception, because they are characterised by the basic faith, since increase means adding something to another thing that shares its attribute. This is what they display, concealing themselves. As for the reality of their state among their like, it is mockery, considering it unlikely that it could increase anyone's state at all. The reason for their doubt and questioning is that those who heard it divided into two groups, believers and hypocrites. For this reason God, exalted is He, answered by saying, linking it to its revelation: ﴿As for those who believed﴾, meaning, they truly established faith, because the temperaments of their hearts were sound, ﴿it has increased them﴾, meaning that surah has increased them, ﴿in faith﴾, meaning by their belief in it, added to what they already had of faith in other things, and by reflecting upon it, the softening of hearts through it, and the understanding of the knowledge it contains which brings tranquillity to hearts and soothing to breasts.

Since the intended meaning of faith is its reality, and since increase implies something added to a prior state, it was unnecessary to say "to their faith," both because of this and because "those who believed" indicates it.

﴿And they rejoice﴾, meaning good comes to them through what it has increased in them of lasting good, which nothing can equal. ﴿As for those﴾ [in whose hearts is a disease], and He clarified that the most noble thing in them is a dwelling place for affliction, so He said: ﴿in their hearts is a disease﴾. So faith was denied to them and disbelief was affirmed for them, and so they did not believe.

(p-52) Since the intended meaning of disease is moral corruption which leads to corruption of belief, He expressed it by the word "rijs" (filth), saying: ﴿it has increased them in filth﴾, meaning in disturbance that necessitates doubt. He further clarified the matter by saying, to show that the meaning is metaphorical: ﴿to their filth﴾, meaning their doubt, which was in other things. ﴿And they died﴾, meaning that this continued with them, since it had taken firm root in them, until they died. ﴿While they were disbelievers﴾, meaning they were deeply immersed in disbelief. Doubt in religion was called a disease because it is a corruption of the spirit that requires treatment, just as the corruption of the body requires it, and heart disease is more grave; its cure is more difficult and more obscure, its remedy is rarer, and its physicians are fewer. Since the surah increased the disbelievers in filth because of their disbelief in it, it is as if it were what increased them, and its description with that was apt, just as one says: "Safety is a disease enough," and as the poet said:

"My sight has doubted me after its advice, and it is enough of a disease for you that you be sound and safe."

This was said by al-Rummani. So the believers report an increase in their faith, while these report its absence in their inner feeling. This is what necessitates their doubt and their persistence in their error and falsehood. Had they returned to the judgment of reason, it would have removed their doubt and made them aware of the truthfulness of the believers, by the difference between their two states, for the appearance of fruits removes doubts. The verse is an instance of al-iḥtibāk (a device in which two complementary elements are mentioned while each omits the counterpart of the other): the mention of faith first indicates the omission of its opposite second, and the mention of disease second indicates the omission of health first.
